expanded_source_wording_tex:
Equally important are the non-claims.
We do not claim that closure ladders arise automatically in arbitrary dynamics, nor that any particular choice of lens $f$ or timescale $\tau$ is preferred.
We also do not claim that protocol holonomy by itself yields sustained directionality under autonomy; on the contrary, the lifted-model statements formalize that sustained asymmetry requires a genuine affinity (a non-exact 1-form component) or an externally imposed schedule (which lies outside \textbf{A\_AUT}).
Finally, the finite forcing lemma is used only as a \emph{finite proxy} for generic extension: it justifies that strict theory extension is cheap and typical when there is hidden volume, not that all forms of novelty reduce to random predicates.

\noindent
Six Birds Foundations I~\citep{Tsiokos2026SixBirdsFoundations}
introduced a stratified closure calculus with six primitive closure
roles. The present paper extends that calculus
into a theorem-level framework in three parts: a primitive role
architecture fixing the meanings, levels, local boundaries, and
selected lifts of the six typed closure roles \(P_1,\ldots,P_6\); an
admissibility and meta-theory regime in which honest bookkeeping,
typed non-collapse, level profiles, forgetting with selected lifts,
activation thresholds, instrument-relative visibility, and
empirical-bridge admissibility are stated as theorem schemas; and a
scoped exact-six theorem chain over the domain \(\ensuremath{\mathsf{FATCD}}\) of finite
audited typed closure descriptions. Within this domain we prove six
role-lower-bound witnesses, an upper-bound classification with
corrected role-projection alignments (closing the probability,
causality, and agency threats in the covered scope), a
decomposition/exhaustion theorem, and an integrated stress
certification. The terminal theorem asserts that every
\(D \in \ensuremath{\mathsf{FATCD}}\) admits a well-formed decomposition/exhaustion
record with exactly six role channels, each in one of five recorded
statuses, with residual features classified under an explicit scheme
and, under an explicit recognition hypothesis (the three principal threat
classes --- probability, causality, and agency --- closed unconditionally), no
seventh irreducible role required in the covered scope. The
claim concerns role channels rather than active projections, and the
decomposition is existential, not unique. We do not claim unrestricted
exact-six, all-emergence coverage, a full six-primitives algebra,
global primitive independence, empirical realization, internal
instrument-family completeness, or recognition-completeness of the six roles.

\begin{definition}[Selected-lift atlas]\label{def:selected-lift-atlas}
The \emph{selected-lift atlas} for the six roles records, for each
\ensuremath{\mathrm{P1}}, \ldots, \ensuremath{\mathrm{P6}}:
\begin{itemize}[topsep=2pt,itemsep=1pt]
  \item \ensuremath{\mathrm{P1}}: proof or witness together with quotient structure, carrying
    either a descended map or an explicit no-map obstruction;
  \item \ensuremath{\mathrm{P2}}: representability or non-representability certificates
    together with the macro-specification layer and realization relation;
  \item \ensuremath{\mathrm{P3}}: the selected lift data recorded in the promoted atlas,
    carrying generated route terms, non-reducibility certificates, and
    categorical route grammar or a reduced categorical universe;
  \item \ensuremath{\mathrm{P4}}: validity certificates together with structural
    stage/refinement architecture;
  \item \ensuremath{\mathrm{P5}}: quotient-validity certificates together with the
    structural quotient data, a packaging map, and universal-property or
    tower/coarsening data;
  \item \ensuremath{\mathrm{P6}}: record-event or check evidence together with the audit
    schema and its provenance and replay/check relations.
\end{itemize}
Each lift is selected and not unique, and forgetting from a higher level
loses structural content that is not recoverable without re-adding data.
\end{definition}

    (Definitions~\ref{def:raw-record} and~\ref{def:annotations}) are

    the residual classification scheme rather than barred at the door.

    categories (x) and (xi)---an unresolved candidate seventh-role threat,

    options. At the domain-definition level the scheme records the available
    labels but does not assert that those two categories are empty, so it
    cannot smuggle the exact-six answer into the definition of the domain.

projection or a six-channel record, membership in \ensuremath{\mathsf{FATCD}} is independent of

\end{proof}

conclusion: Each family is a guardrail that restates a nonclaim already secured by an earlier result, so each is recorded as a remark.
expanded_source_wording_tex:
With the theorem chain of Sections~\ref{sec:lower-bounds},
\ref{sec:upper-bound-classification}, and
\ref{sec:decomposition-exhaustion} in place, we record six stress
families that act as consistency checks against overclaims. These are
not proofs of the scoped exact-six target; they verify that the
theorem chain does not silently admit overclaims. Each family is a
guardrail that restates a nonclaim already secured by an earlier
result, so each is recorded as a remark. Their joint satisfaction is

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\begin{itemize}[topsep=2pt,itemsep=1pt]
  \item \emph{Six channels, not six active witnesses.} The theorem
    asserts six role channels in \(\Dec{D}\) for every
    \(D \in \ensuremath{\mathsf{FATCD}}\). It does not assert that every \(D\) activates
    all six roles, that every \(D\) carries six active projections
    \(\pi_1(D), \ldots, \pi_6(D)\), or that a single \(D\) realizes
    all six witness schemas of Section~\ref{sec:lower-bounds}.
  \item \emph{Existential, not unique, decomposition.} The theorem
    asserts existence of \(\Dec{D}\); it does not assert uniqueness or
    canonicity. Distinct well-formed records of the same \(D\) may
    exist (Proposition~\ref{prop:non-uniqueness}).
  \item \emph{Conditional residual exhaustion.} The residual
    exhaustion clause is conditional on the recognition hypothesis
    (Definition~\ref{def:recognition-hypothesis}) and restricted to the
    covered scope: the three principal threat classes are closed
    unconditionally, while whether every finite audited feature is recognized
    is the open recognition-completeness question
    (Remark~\ref{rem:recognition-open}). Features requiring non-finite or
    unbookkept semantics are classified as outside-domain structures under
    category~(viii) of Definition~\ref{def:residual-scheme}, not absorbed into
    primitive roles.
  \item \emph{No broader claim.} Theorem~\ref{thm:scoped-exact-six}
    is a statement about \ensuremath{\mathsf{FATCD}}. It does not assert a full
    six-primitives algebra, global primitive independence, empirical
    realization, instrument-family completeness, or coverage of all
    emergence phenomena. See Section~\ref{sec:limitations-nonclaims}.
\end{itemize}

expanded_source_wording_tex:
Each of the three scope features --- domain restriction, existence
rather than uniqueness, residual exhaustion within a covered scope
--- is structural rather than cosmetic. An unrestricted exact-six
theorem would require a domain-free argument for which the present
paper does not claim to have the instruments. A uniqueness or
canonicity claim would require a theory of translation records
identifying distinct well-formed decompositions, which lies outside
the present admissibility regime. Scope-free residual exhaustion
would require scope-free closure of the three high-priority threats
addressed in Section~\ref{sec:upper-bound-classification}. Stating
the theorem at the scope the proof supports keeps the
endogenous-instrument meta-limit (Section~\ref{subsec:meta-limit})
separate from the current claim instead of folded into it. The posture
aligns with the broader view that scientific laws form a patchwork of
domain-local regularities rather than a single global
theory~\citep{Cartwright1999}.

conclusion: The discipline is one of epistemic hygiene, in the spirit of Bohr's complementarity doctrine : we do not claim that instruments are incompatible in principle, only that they are not interchangeable without explicit visibility bookkeeping and, where contexts shift, explicit translation records (Definitions and ).
expanded_source_wording_tex:
The consequence is epistemic. Every admissible claim carries an
explicit visibility record: its visible content, its suppressed
content, the instruments under which visibility and suppression are
asserted, and the resulting instrument-relative claim strength
(Definition~\ref{prop:visibility}). Triangulating a role projection
across several instruments is a disciplined way to strengthen an
assertion; reading a projection off a single instrument and declaring
its content canonical is not admissible. The discipline is one of
epistemic hygiene, in the spirit of Bohr's complementarity
doctrine~\citep{Bohr1958}: we do not claim that instruments are
incompatible in principle, only that they are not interchangeable
without explicit visibility bookkeeping and, where contexts shift,
explicit translation records
(Definitions~\ref{prop:visibility} and~\ref{prop:level-profile}).

expanded_source_wording_tex:
Each nonclaim below is preserved throughout the paper and is enforced
locally by the theorem-chain result that would otherwise overread it.

\begin{itemize}[topsep=2pt,itemsep=1pt]
  \item \emph{No full six-primitives algebra.} Scoped exact-six is
    proved over \ensuremath{\mathsf{FATCD}}; it is not claimed that \ensuremath{\mathrm{P1}}--\ensuremath{\mathrm{P6}}
    generate a global algebra of closure operations
    (Remark~\ref{rem:atlas-global-nonclaims},
    Remark~\ref{prop:overclaim-stress}).
  \item \emph{No global primitive-independence theorem.} Typed
    non-collapse (Proposition~\ref{prop:typed-non-collapse}) is
    strictly weaker than global independence and is the sole claim at
    that level.
  \item \emph{No empirical realization.} Empirical-bridge admissibility
    (Definition~\ref{prop:empirical-bridge}) admits
    threshold-dependent, level-indexed, instrument-visible substrate
    evidence; it does not assert that any \(D \in \ensuremath{\mathsf{FATCD}}\) is itself
    a substrate observation.
  \item \emph{No unique selected lift.} Every lift is recorded as
    selected and non-unique
    (Definition~\ref{prop:forgetting-lifts}).
  \item \emph{No lower-to-higher determinacy.} Behavioral or
    verification content does not determine structural-categorical
    content.
  \item \emph{No instrument-free formulation.} Admissible claims carry
    an instrument-relative visibility record
    (Definition~\ref{prop:visibility}).
  \item \emph{No internal instrument-family completeness.} The
    accepted instrument family is not asserted to be sufficient for
    every exact-six judgment formulable in the same regime.
  \item \emph{No unrestricted all-emergence coverage.}
    Theorem~\ref{thm:scoped-exact-six} is scoped to \ensuremath{\mathsf{FATCD}}.
  \item \emph{No surrogate terminal evidence.} The proof chain does
    not invoke any surrogate for the terminal scoped exact-six
    theorem.
  \item \emph{No uniqueness of primitive presentations.} Distinct
    admissible presentations of the same role may coexist.
  \item \emph{Cross-level comparison requires translation.} Direct
    comparison of claims at different levels is inadmissible without a
    translation record (Definition~\ref{prop:level-profile}).
\end{itemize}

expanded_source_wording_tex: Earlier work in the Six-Bird program supplies six primitive role families ($P_1,\ldots,P_6$ --- descent, representability, route mismatch, refinement, packaging, audit), an admissibility and exact-six scope discipline over $\mathsf{FATCD}$, inherited status, threshold, visibility, and audit machinery, and concrete model fragments such as PICA and Cantor. It does not, however, supply a paper-level finite interaction calculus that records, in one finite typed framework, how the six primitive roles interact, how typed directed cells are judged, how defects induce statuses, how promotion is audited, and how model realizations are scoped. This paper constructs $\BirdInt$, a finite audited typed calculus for six-bird interaction. The calculus carries finite typed schemas of theory packages, instruments, visibility and suppression records, witness and update families, role-channel, directed-cell, pair-observable, promotion, dependency, and no-go judgments, defect records, statuses, gates, audit records, and model-realization maps. Every component is finite, admissibility is checked on finite records, and every claim is recorded under an explicit host or instrument together with a nonclaim register. The main theorem groups are: no total six-symbol algebra; typed non-collapse and status-family separation; finite well-formedness and covered-cell status uniqueness; descent, closure-deficit, completion, saturation, strict-extension, and definability results; graph and cohomology no-drive results; promotion-gate soundness; and no-overreading and finite rotating-audit theorems. The numbered stack comprises theorem-grade Theorems 1--28 and 30--32, model-grade Model Theorems 29, 33, and 34, and audit-grade Proposition 35. The repository includes a Lean 4 validation track, pinned to \texttt{leanprover/lean4:v4.28.0}, whose manifest-driven strict validator audits the paper-to-Lean declaration coverage. The mathematical content of these theorems is standard --- descent through a finite quotient, idempotent saturation, the Kullback--Leibler decomposition, finite cycle/cochain duality, the universal property of the image factorization, and so on --- and is not claimed as novel; what the paper contributes is the calculus, its scope discipline, the countermodel atlas, and the explicit nonclaim register within which these results are restated and used. Twelve countermodels $\mathsf{CM}_1$--$\mathsf{CM}_{12}$ each block a specific overclaim, and four scoped model-realization statements cover finite stochastic PICA, audited Cantor shells, finite abstract-interpretation hosts, and finite graph and cohomology supports. Each model realization is host-bound, fragment-scoped, and certified at claim-strength \texttt{model\_realization} rather than theorem-grade \texttt{accepted}. The paper does not prove a universal exact-six theorem, a universal six-symbol algebra, a unique decomposition theorem, an empirical realization claim, or complete same-level self-certification.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \(\mathbb P\) is the fixed finite set of primitive labels \(\{P_1,\ldots,P_6\}\) defined in Subsection 2.2.1. It is the underlying label alphabet of every role-channel, directed-cell, pair-observable, promotion, and dependency judgment.
\item
  \(\mathsf{Lev}=\{\mathsf{Beh},\mathsf{Ver},\mathsf{Str}\}\) is the finite level set defined in Subsection 2.2.3, used to tag the kind of content a judgment refers to and to gate cross-level claims through translation, lift, forgetting, or reflection bridges.
\item
  \(\mathsf{Host}\) is the finite inventory of permitted hosts declared in Subsection 2.1.2: \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{fin}}\), \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{prob}}\), \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{graph}}\), \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{AI}}\), \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{PICA}}\), \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{CantorShell}}\), \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{DC}}\), \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{instr}}\). Every theorem statement names its host.
\item
  \(\mathsf{Cont}\) is the finite content universe of the domain, defined in Subsection 3.2. It collects the records that claims may use: theory packages, instruments, witnesses, updates, profiles, defect records, threshold records, audit records, visibility records, level/lens/interface records, package and promotion interfaces, quotients, lenses, completion endomaps, kernels, graphs, finite families, refinements, and other finite typed records introduced as the calculus is built.
\item
  \(\mathsf{Instr}\) is the finite family of instrument records, defined in Subsection 3.4. An instrument fixes the visible/suppressed map, scope, claim types, threshold and audit policies, level assignment, bridge policy, source policy, and nonclaim list under which a claim is to be evaluated.
\item
  \(\mathsf{Pkg}\) is the finite family of theory packages, defined in Subsection 3.3, each carrying the inherited Foundations I package data \((Z,f,\Sigma_f,E,\mathcal A)\) together with the additional Foundations III typed records (visibility, source, defect, promotion, model-realization) attached around it.
\item
  \(\mathsf{Prof}\) is the finite family of profile records, defined in Subsection 3.6. A profile fixes per-judgment data such as actor and informant level tags, scale, regime, bridge type, instrument mode, and locality, and is required by every directed-cell, pair-observable, promotion, and claim judgment.
\item
  \(\mathsf{Wit}\) assigns to each primitive \(P_i\in\mathbb P\) its typed witness family \(\mathsf{Wit}(P_i)\), defined in Subsection 3.7. The informant-side data of a directed cell is required to belong to one of these families.
\item
  \(\mathsf{Upd}\) assigns to each primitive \(P_i\in\mathbb P\) its typed update family \(\mathsf{Upd}(P_i)\), defined in Subsection 3.7. The actor-side data of a directed cell is required to belong to one of these families.
\item
  \(\mathsf{Def}\) is the finite family of defect records, defined in Section 5. A defect record carries a defect type, a domain, a witness, a threshold, a measured value, a status consequence, and an audit/source record, and feeds the defect-to-status rules of Subsection 5.6.
\item
  \(\mathsf{Judg}\) is the finite family of judgment forms used by the calculus: role-channel, directed-cell, pair-observable, promotion, dependency, and instrument-indexed claim judgments, all defined in Section 4.
\item
  \(\mathsf{Status}\) is the finite family of status sets, one per judgment family: role-channel, directed-cell, pair-observable, promotion, claim, gate, and square statuses. The sets are listed in Subsection 2.3.2 and defined fully in Section 5.
\item
  \(\mathsf{Gate}\) is the finite family of gate specifications used during promotion and claim acceptance, defined in Section 10. A gate is a finite check whose \(\texttt{pass}\), \(\texttt{fail}\), \(\texttt{not\_required}\), \(\texttt{not\_checked}\), or \(\texttt{outside\_scope}\) result feeds promotion-status and claim-status decisions.
\item
  \(\mathsf{Dep}\) is the finite family of dependency relations between primitives, including positive dependencies, blocked dependencies, bridge-required dependencies, and countermodel-supported no-go dependencies, defined in Subsection 4.6.
\item
  \(\mathsf{Audit}\) is the finite family of audit records, defined in Subsection 4.8. An audit record carries a target, an instrument, replay or check data, and admissibility data; it is distinct from the inherited audit functional \(\mathcal A\) that lives inside a theory package \(\mathcal T\).
\item
  \(\mathsf{Vis}\) is the finite family of visibility maps and visibility bridges, defined in Subsection 3.5. A visibility map sends content to one of \(\texttt{visible}\), \(\texttt{suppressed}\), \(\texttt{outside}\), \(\texttt{unknown}\) under an instrument, and a visibility bridge is the admissible record by which a claim may use suppressed content.
\item
  \(\mathsf{Source}\) is the finite family of source records, defined in Subsection 4.8. A source record fixes source identity, source type, trace, and source validity, and is consulted by pair-observable and claim acceptance rules.
\item
  \(\mathsf{Nonclaim}\) is the finite family of nonclaim records carried by an instrument or attached to a judgment. A nonclaim records what the surrounding statement does not assert, in the same finite typed format as the rest of the calculus.
\item
  \(\mathsf{Real}\) is the finite family of model-realization modules, defined in Section 13: the PICA, audited Cantor shell, abstract-interpretation, and graph/cohomology realizations of named fragments of the calculus.
\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \(\mathbb P\) is the fixed finite set of primitive labels \(\{P_1,\ldots,P_6\}\) defined in Subsection 2.2.1. It is the underlying label alphabet of every role-channel, directed-cell, pair-observable, promotion, and dependency judgment.
\item
  \(\mathsf{Lev}=\{\mathsf{Beh},\mathsf{Ver},\mathsf{Str}\}\) is the finite level set defined in Subsection 2.2.3, used to tag the kind of content a judgment refers to and to gate cross-level claims through translation, lift, forgetting, or reflection bridges.
\item
  \(\mathsf{Host}\) is the finite inventory of permitted hosts declared in Subsection 2.1.2: \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{fin}}\), \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{prob}}\), \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{graph}}\), \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{AI}}\), \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{PICA}}\), \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{CantorShell}}\), \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{DC}}\), \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{instr}}\). Every theorem statement names its host.
\item
  \(\mathsf{Cont}\) is the finite content universe of the domain, defined in Subsection 3.2. It collects the records that claims may use: theory packages, instruments, witnesses, updates, profiles, defect records, threshold records, audit records, visibility records, level/lens/interface records, package and promotion interfaces, quotients, lenses, completion endomaps, kernels, graphs, finite families, refinements, and other finite typed records introduced as the calculus is built.
\item
  \(\mathsf{Instr}\) is the finite family of instrument records, defined in Subsection 3.4. An instrument fixes the visible/suppressed map, scope, claim types, threshold and audit policies, level assignment, bridge policy, source policy, and nonclaim list under which a claim is to be evaluated.
\item
  \(\mathsf{Pkg}\) is the finite family of theory packages, defined in Subsection 3.3, each carrying the inherited Foundations I package data \((Z,f,\Sigma_f,E,\mathcal A)\) together with the additional Foundations III typed records (visibility, source, defect, promotion, model-realization) attached around it.
\item
  \(\mathsf{Prof}\) is the finite family of profile records, defined in Subsection 3.6. A profile fixes per-judgment data such as actor and informant level tags, scale, regime, bridge type, instrument mode, and locality, and is required by every directed-cell, pair-observable, promotion, and claim judgment.
\item
  \(\mathsf{Wit}\) assigns to each primitive \(P_i\in\mathbb P\) its typed witness family \(\mathsf{Wit}(P_i)\), defined in Subsection 3.7. The informant-side data of a directed cell is required to belong to one of these families.
\item
  \(\mathsf{Upd}\) assigns to each primitive \(P_i\in\mathbb P\) its typed update family \(\mathsf{Upd}(P_i)\), defined in Subsection 3.7. The actor-side data of a directed cell is required to belong to one of these families.
\item
  \(\mathsf{Def}\) is the finite family of defect records, defined in Section 5. A defect record carries a defect type, a domain, a witness, a threshold, a measured value, a status consequence, and an audit/source record, and feeds the defect-to-status rules of Subsection 5.6.
\item
  \(\mathsf{Judg}\) is the finite family of judgment forms used by the calculus: role-channel, directed-cell, pair-observable, promotion, dependency, and instrument-indexed claim judgments, all defined in Section 4.
\item
  \(\mathsf{Status}\) is the finite family of status sets, one per judgment family: role-channel, directed-cell, pair-observable, promotion, claim, gate, and square statuses. The sets are listed in Subsection 2.3.2 and defined fully in Section 5.
\item
  \(\mathsf{Gate}\) is the finite family of gate specifications used during promotion and claim acceptance, defined in Section 10. A gate is a finite check whose \(\texttt{pass}\), \(\texttt{fail}\), \(\texttt{not\_required}\), \(\texttt{not\_checked}\), or \(\texttt{outside\_scope}\) result feeds promotion-status and claim-status decisions.
\item
  \(\mathsf{Dep}\) is the finite family of dependency relations between primitives, including positive dependencies, blocked dependencies, bridge-required dependencies, and countermodel-supported no-go dependencies, defined in Subsection 4.6.
\item
  \(\mathsf{Audit}\) is the finite family of audit records, defined in Subsection 4.8. An audit record carries a target, an instrument, replay or check data, and admissibility data; it is distinct from the inherited audit functional \(\mathcal A\) that lives inside a theory package \(\mathcal T\).
\item
  \(\mathsf{Vis}\) is the finite family of visibility maps and visibility bridges, defined in Subsection 3.5. A visibility map sends content to one of \(\texttt{visible}\), \(\texttt{suppressed}\), \(\texttt{outside}\), \(\texttt{unknown}\) under an instrument, and a visibility bridge is the admissible record by which a claim may use suppressed content.
\item
  \(\mathsf{Source}\) is the finite family of source records, defined in Subsection 4.8. A source record fixes source identity, source type, trace, and source validity, and is consulted by pair-observable and claim acceptance rules.
\item
  \(\mathsf{Nonclaim}\) is the finite family of nonclaim records carried by an instrument or attached to a judgment. A nonclaim records what the surrounding statement does not assert, in the same finite typed format as the rest of the calculus.
\item
  \(\mathsf{Real}\) is the finite family of model-realization modules, defined in Section 13: the PICA, audited Cantor shell, abstract-interpretation, and graph/cohomology realizations of named fragments of the calculus.
\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{Host.} Each record carries a host tag drawn from \(\mathsf{Host}\). The host tag fixes which finite mathematical universe the record lives in: \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{fin}}\) for the base host, \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{prob}}\) for finite stochastic content, \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{graph}}\) for finite graph and cohomology content, \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{AI}}\) for finite abstract-interpretation content, \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{PICA}}\) and \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{CantorShell}}\) for the model-realization hosts, \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{DC}}\) for the high-structure fragment, and \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{instr}}\) for instrument-side content.
\item
  \textbf{Level.} Each record carries a level tag drawn from \(\mathsf{Lev}=\{\mathsf{Beh},\mathsf{Ver},\mathsf{Str}\}\). The level tag fixes whether the record describes behavioral/trace content, verification/audit content, or structural/object content. A judgment that uses records at more than one level is admissible only with an explicit level bridge (translation, lift, forgetting, or reflection).
\item
  \textbf{Instrument.} Each record is interpreted under the instrument \(I\) that the surrounding judgment names. The instrument fixes whether the record is visible, suppressed, outside-scope, or unknown for the purpose of the claim, and what bridges may connect it to visible content. A record may be in \(\mathsf{Cont}\) globally and yet be suppressed under a particular instrument; suppression is a relation between a record and an instrument, not a property of the record alone, and it does not assert that the suppressed record is false.
\item
  \textbf{Profile.} Each judgment is tagged by a profile \(\lambda\in\mathsf{Prof}\) which fixes per-judgment data including actor and informant level tags, scale, regime, bridge type, instrument mode, and locality. The profile of a judgment together with its host, level, and instrument tags determines the admissibility of every record in its use-set.
\end{itemize}

conclusion: N_I : the finite nonclaim record of I .
expanded_source_wording_tex:
\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \(\mathrm{id}_I\): a finite identifier under which the instrument is registered. Two distinct instruments have distinct identifiers, and an instrument identifier is part of the data of every claim accepted under that instrument.
\item
  \(\mathsf{Scope}_I\): the finite scope record of the instrument, fixing the host, level, and content classes that fall inside its scope. A claim whose use-set is not contained in \(\mathsf{Scope}_I\) has status \(\texttt{outside\_scope}\) under \(I\).
\item
  \(\mathsf{ClaimTypes}_I\): the finite family of claim types that \(I\) is configured to evaluate, including role-channel, directed-cell, pair-observable, promotion, dependency, and instrument-indexed claim types as appropriate.
\item
  \(\mathsf{Visible}_I,\;\mathsf{Suppressed}_I\): the finite visibility partition of \(\mathsf{Scope}_I\) into visible and suppressed content under \(I\). The complement of \(\mathsf{Visible}_I\cup\mathsf{Suppressed}_I\) within \(\mathsf{Scope}_I\) is the unknown class; content outside \(\mathsf{Scope}_I\) is in the outside-scope class. The full four-way partition is given in Subsection 3.5.
\item
  \(\mathsf{CheckRules}_I\): the finite family of check rules used to classify a claim under \(I\). Check rules are typed finite records: each rule states which fields of a claim it consults, what comparison or test it performs, and what classifier verdict it contributes.
\item
  \(\mathsf{EvidencePolicy}_I\): the finite policy for what counts as admissible evidence under \(I\), distinguishing direct evidence, bridge-relayed evidence, and inadmissible evidence.
\item
  \(\mathsf{ThresholdPolicy}_I\): the finite family of thresholds used by \(I\), including exact, approximate, tolerance, rank/dimension, visibility, and source thresholds. The threshold record schema is fixed in Subsection 5.2.
\item
  \(\mathsf{AuditPolicy}_I\): the finite policy for which audit records \(I\) requires, in what order, and against which sources. The policy is checked by the gate semantics of Section 10 and the rotating-audit semantics of Section 11. Passing an audit policy contributes to an instrument-indexed status; it is not instrument-free truth.
\item
  \(\mathsf{Level}_I\in\mathsf{Lev}\): the level annotation of \(I\). An instrument operates at a single level; cross-level operation requires an explicit level bridge inside the instrument's claim record.
\item
  \(\mathsf{BridgePolicy}_I\): the finite policy for which bridges \(I\) admits, including visibility bridges, level bridges, instrument-transfer bridges, drive bridges, and model-realization bridges. The policy fixes which suppressed content can be brought into the use-set of an accepted claim. A generic audit bridge is not a drive certificate unless the bridge records the required \(\mathrm{P6}_{\mathrm{drive}}\) data.
\item
  \(\mathsf{SourcePolicy}_I\): the finite policy for which source-of-truth records \(I\) accepts, distinguishing real sources, fallback sources, dirty sources, proxy sources, and missing sources.
\item
  \(\mathcal N_I\): the finite nonclaim record of \(I\). The nonclaims of \(I\) are part of the instrument and propagate to every claim accepted under \(I\); an accepted claim under \(I\) is interpreted with the nonclaims of \(I\) attached.
\end{itemize}

conclusion: accepted : the claim is accepted by I under Gamma, T with admissible visibility, threshold, source, audit, and nonclaim data. rejected : the instrument has an admissible refuting witness for the claim. provisional : partial evidence exists and the profile permits provisional status. blocked : the claim is in scope but unadjudicable because required evidence, a bridge, a source, or visibility support is missing. outside_scope : the claim's use-set is not contained in Scope_I , or a host or level mismatch removes the claim from I 's adjudication. absent_with_record : required evidence is absent and the absence is audited. below_threshold : a threshold check required by Theta or by ThresholdPolicy_I has failed. failed_audit : an audit policy check has failed. undefined_circular : the claim depends on an unstratified circular support or audit loop, including the same-level self-audit case of Subsection 11.5.
expanded_source_wording_tex:
\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \(\texttt{accepted}\): the claim is accepted by \(I\) under \(\Gamma,\mathcal T\) with admissible visibility, threshold, source, audit, and nonclaim data.
\item
  \(\texttt{rejected}\): the instrument has an admissible refuting witness for the claim.
\item
  \(\texttt{provisional}\): partial evidence exists and the profile permits provisional status.
\item
  \(\texttt{blocked}\): the claim is in scope but unadjudicable because required evidence, a bridge, a source, or visibility support is missing.
\item
  \(\texttt{outside\_scope}\): the claim's use-set is not contained in \(\mathsf{Scope}_I\), or a host or level mismatch removes the claim from \(I\)'s adjudication.
\item
  \(\texttt{absent\_with\_record}\): required evidence is absent and the absence is audited.
\item
  \(\texttt{below\_threshold}\): a threshold check required by \(\Theta\) or by \(\mathsf{ThresholdPolicy}_I\) has failed.
\item
  \(\texttt{failed\_audit}\): an audit policy check has failed.
\item
  \(\texttt{undefined\_circular}\): the claim depends on an unstratified circular support or audit loop, including the same-level self-audit case of Subsection 11.5.

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \(\texttt{accepted}\): the claim is accepted by \(I\) under \(\Gamma,\mathcal T\) with admissible visibility, threshold, source, audit, and nonclaim data.

\item
  \(\texttt{provisional}\): partial evidence exists and the profile permits provisional status.
\item
  \(\texttt{blocked}\): the claim is in scope but unadjudicable because required evidence, a bridge, a source, or visibility support is missing.
\item
  \(\texttt{outside\_scope}\): the claim's use-set is not contained in \(\mathsf{Scope}_I\), or a host or level mismatch removes the claim from \(I\)'s adjudication.
\item
  \(\texttt{absent\_with\_record}\): required evidence is absent and the absence is audited.
\item
  \(\texttt{below\_threshold}\): a threshold check required by \(\Theta\) or by \(\mathsf{ThresholdPolicy}_I\) has failed.
\item
  \(\texttt{failed\_audit}\): an audit policy check has failed.
\item
  \(\texttt{undefined\_circular}\): the claim depends on an unstratified circular support or audit loop, including the same-level self-audit case of Subsection 11.5.
\end{itemize}

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{Construction.} A finite explicit construction on a named host, with the data of the calculus (carriers, maps, packages, profiles, witnesses, updates, defects, audit and source records) made explicit. The construction is finite at every step.
\item
  \textbf{Supported no-go.} The dependency judgment \(S\mathrel{\mathsf{dep}_r}X\) that the construction supports, in the form fixed by Subsection 4.6.1, with relation type \(r\) drawn from the eight admissible types \(\texttt{suffices}\), \(\texttt{insufficient}\), \(\texttt{destroys}\), \(\texttt{blocks}\), \(\texttt{enables}\), \(\texttt{equivalent}\), \(\texttt{requires\_bridge}\), and \(\texttt{outside\_scope}\).
\item
  \textbf{What it blocks.} The overclaim that the no-go rules out, named together with the corresponding nonclaim NC-\(n\) from Subsection 2.4.3.
\item
  \textbf{What it does not block.} The positive content that the construction is consistent with, so that the no-go is not over-read into a stronger negative statement.
\item
  \textbf{Required positive bridge.} When a positive claim of the form \(S\Rightarrow X\) would need an additional bridge, the bridge type is named (for example, a drive bridge \(B_{3\to 6}^{\mathrm{drive}}\) or a gluing bridge \(B_{\mathrm{glue}}\)).
\end{itemize}

A gate may be marked \(\texttt{not\_required}\) when the bridge does not claim the corresponding content; the descent gate, for example, is \(\texttt{not\_required}\) for a bridge that records only an interface change with no closure claim. A required core gate marked \(\texttt{not\_checked}\) does not yield an accepted promotion; the promotion classifier of Subsection 5.6.4 routes such a bridge to \(\texttt{candidate}\).

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \emph{Fragment-only realization.} A model-realization statement \(\mathcal M\models\mathcal S:\texttt{model\_realization}\) asserts realization of \(\mathcal S\) and not of the whole calculus. The verdict \(\texttt{model\_realization}\) for \(\mathcal S\) does not imply a \(\texttt{model\_realization}\) verdict for any larger fragment \(\mathcal S'\supsetneq\mathcal S\).
\item
  \emph{No theorem grade by realization.} A model-realization verdict is not a theorem-grade verdict. In the absence of a separately admissible theorem-grade bridge, \(\mathcal M\models\mathcal S:\texttt{model\_realization}\) does not yield a \(\texttt{accepted}\) verdict on a theorem-grade claim about \(\mathcal S\). This is the model-realization nonclaim of Subsection 2.4.
\item
  \emph{Host-bound realization.} A model-realization verdict for \(\mathcal S\) under \(\mathcal M\) is bound to the host of \(\mathcal M\): it does not transfer to other hosts without an admissible instrument-transfer bridge in the sense of Subsection 11.9.
\item
  \emph{No model-coverage theorem.} The four realizations recorded in Subsections 13.2--13.4 and Section 12 do not, taken together, support a global model-coverage theorem for \(\mathbf{BirdInt}^{\mathrm{aud}}_{\mathrm{fin}}\). This is the model-coverage nonclaim of Subsection 13.6.
\end{itemize}

The PICA nonclaim register \(\mathcal N_{\mathrm{PICA}}\) contains, in particular:

\begin{enumerate}
\def\arabic{enumi}.{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  PICA is not the universal six-bird algebra: \(\mathsf{PICAReal}_{\mathrm{fin}}\) realizes a declared finite stochastic fragment, not the whole calculus.
\item
  The recovered \(6\times 6\) multiplicity count is a PICA-profile model fact under the cell profile \(\lambda_{\mathrm{PICA}}\), not a universal \(6\times 6\) law.
\item
  Raw PICA status is not formal status without recovery and classifier check; the formal classifier verdict is the authoritative cell status.
\item
  Directed-cell status \(\texttt{action}\) does not imply pair-realness; pair-realness requires the source/visibility/audit/threshold conjunction of Subsubsection 13.2.7.
\item
  A fallback record does not by itself support a real pair source-of-truth; it supports at most \(\texttt{real\_provisional}\).
\item
  Ablation evidence in \(\mathsf{Abl}\) is model-realization evidence, not theorem-grade evidence, in the absence of an admissible bridge to a theorem-grade claim.
\item
  A \(P_3\) route mismatch is not a \(\mathrm{P6}_{\mathrm{drive}}\) assertion in the sense of Section 8: the two are connected only through an admissible drive bridge.
\item
  A dirty record cannot support a real claim under any host configuration of \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{PICA}}\).
\item
  PICA realizes a finite stochastic fragment, and not the entirety of \(\mathbf{BirdInt}^{\mathrm{aud}}_{\mathrm{fin}}\); this restates the fragment discipline of Subsection 13.1.2.
\item
  Implementation correctness of any concrete PICA implementation is future work and is not certified by this realization theorem; the Lean validation record of Section 15 is a separate, manifest-scoped artifact.
\end{enumerate}

conclusion: No universal six-symbol algebra. The paper does not assert a total operation : P^ 2 → P that produces a faithful universal interaction algebra over the six primitive labels. The non-factorization of cell status through the primitive pair (Theorem 1, Section 6) blocks any such operation as a status-decoding map. No all-mathematics reduction. The paper does not assert that all mathematics is six birds, or that every mathematical object is a BirdInt^ aud _ fin object under any reading. No unrestricted exact-six theorem. The paper does not assert that every typed interaction is exactly representable as one of the thirty-six directed cells P_ i P_ j . The exact-six structure is recorded as a finite typed schema with admissibility conditions, not as an unrestricted decomposition theorem. No unique decomposition. The paper does not assert that a typed interaction has a unique decomposition into primitive directed cells. Decomposition records are admissible only under a declared profile and audit, and different profiles can yield different admissible decompositions.
expanded_source_wording_tex:
\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \emph{No universal six-symbol algebra.} The paper does not assert a total operation \(\ast:\mathbb P^{2}\to\mathbb P\) that produces a faithful universal interaction algebra over the six primitive labels. The non-factorization of cell status through the primitive pair (Theorem 1, Section 6) blocks any such operation as a status-decoding map.
\item
  \emph{No all-mathematics reduction.} The paper does not assert that all mathematics is six birds, or that every mathematical object is a \(\mathbf{BirdInt}^{\mathrm{aud}}_{\mathrm{fin}}\) object under any reading.
\item
  \emph{No unrestricted exact-six theorem.} The paper does not assert that every typed interaction is exactly representable as one of the thirty-six directed cells \(P_{i}\leftarrow P_{j}\). The exact-six structure is recorded as a finite typed schema with admissibility conditions, not as an unrestricted decomposition theorem.
\item
  \emph{No unique decomposition.} The paper does not assert that a typed interaction has a unique decomposition into primitive directed cells. Decomposition records are admissible only under a declared profile and audit, and different profiles can yield different admissible decompositions.
\end{itemize}

conclusion: No primitive-pair status determination. The paper does not assert that the primitive pair (P_ i ,P_ j ) alone determines the directed-cell status. The status non-factorization theorem (Theorem 1, Section 6) records the formal counterexample. No status-family collapse. The paper does not assert that the seven status families of Subsection 5.1 collapse into a single status family. Role status, cell status, pair status, promotion status, claim status, gate status, and square status remain typed-separately judgment-indexed; Theorem 5 of Section 6 records representative separations. No directed-cell-to-pair collapse. The paper does not assert that a directed-cell status determines a pair-observable status. CM_4 of Section 9 records a directed cell with status action whose corresponding pair observable is blocked . No role-channel-to-cell collapse. The paper does not assert that the role status of a primitive determines the directed-cell status of any cell whose actor or informant is that primitive. Role status is a separate judgment family from cell status; Theorem 5 of Section 6 includes the channel-not-cell separation.
expanded_source_wording_tex:
\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \emph{No primitive-pair status determination.} The paper does not assert that the primitive pair \((P_{i},P_{j})\) alone determines the directed-cell status. The status non-factorization theorem (Theorem 1, Section 6) records the formal counterexample.
\item
  \emph{No status-family collapse.} The paper does not assert that the seven status families of Subsection 5.1 collapse into a single status family. Role status, cell status, pair status, promotion status, claim status, gate status, and square status remain typed-separately judgment-indexed; Theorem 5 of Section 6 records representative separations.
\item
  \emph{No directed-cell-to-pair collapse.} The paper does not assert that a directed-cell status determines a pair-observable status. CM\_4 of Section 9 records a directed cell with status \(\texttt{action}\) whose corresponding pair observable is \(\texttt{blocked}\).
\item
  \emph{No role-channel-to-cell collapse.} The paper does not assert that the role status of a primitive determines the directed-cell status of any cell whose actor or informant is that primitive. Role status is a separate judgment family from cell status; Theorem 5 of Section 6 includes the channel-not-cell separation.
\end{itemize}

conclusion: No package-implies-closure. The paper does not assert that a P_ 5 -packaging operator on a finite carrier implies macro-dynamics closure of any associated transformer. CM_1 of Section 9 records an active package whose macro dynamics are not closed under I . No idempotence-implies-commutation. The paper does not assert that two idempotent finite completions E_ 1 ,E_ 2 :C→ C commute. CM_8 of Appendix C, named in Subsection 9.8, records two idempotent completions with E_ 1 E_ 2 ≠ E_ 2 E_ 1 . No repeated fixed completion as theory growth. The paper does not assert that repeated application of a single fixed idempotent completion is the same as the packaged completion of a target package. The Cantor target package T_ 1 of Subsubsection 13.3.3 uses a packaged completion E_ tau, =U_ Q_ K^ tau , not a repeated single completion. No strictness-implies-closure. The paper does not assert that a strict-bridge passage Promote(B):strict implies macro-dynamics closure of either side of the bridge. CM_9 of Appendix C, named in Subsection 9.8, records a strict bridge without closure. No strictness-implies-drive. \begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \emph{No package-implies-closure.} The paper does not assert that a \(P_{5}\)-packaging operator on a finite carrier implies macro-dynamics closure of any associated transformer. CM\_1 of Section 9 records an active package whose macro dynamics are not closed under \(I\).
\item
  \emph{No idempotence-implies-commutation.} The paper does not assert that two idempotent finite completions \(E_{1},E_{2}:C\to C\) commute. CM\_8 of Appendix C, named in Subsection 9.8, records two idempotent completions with \(E_{1}E_{2}\neq E_{2}E_{1}\).
\item
  \emph{No repeated fixed completion as theory growth.} The paper does not assert that repeated application of a single fixed idempotent completion is the same as the packaged completion of a target package. The Cantor target package \(T_{1}\) of Subsubsection 13.3.3 uses a packaged completion \(E_{\tau,\ell}=U_{\ell}\circ Q_{\ell}\circ K^{\tau}\), not a repeated single completion.
\item
  \emph{No strictness-implies-closure.} The paper does not assert that a strict-bridge passage \(\mathrm{Promote}(B):\texttt{strict}\) implies macro-dynamics closure of either side of the bridge. CM\_9 of Appendix C, named in Subsection 9.8, records a strict bridge without closure.
\item
  \emph{No strictness-implies-drive.} The paper does not assert that a strict-bridge passage implies a \(\mathrm{P6}_{\mathrm{drive}}\) certificate on either side. CM\_10 of Appendix C, named in Subsection 9.8, records a strict bridge without drive.
\end{itemize}

source_wording_tex:
\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \emph{No package-implies-closure.} The paper does not assert that a \(P_{5}\)-packaging operator on a finite carrier implies macro-dynamics closure of any associated transformer. CM\_1 of Section 9 records an active package whose macro dynamics are not closed under \(I\).
\item
  \emph{No idempotence-implies-commutation.} The paper does not assert that two idempotent finite completions \(E_{1},E_{2}:C\to C\) commute. CM\_8 of Appendix C, named in Subsection 9.8, records two idempotent completions with \(E_{1}E_{2}\neq E_{2}E_{1}\).
\item
  \emph{No repeated fixed completion as theory growth.} The paper does not assert that repeated application of a single fixed idempotent completion is the same as the packaged completion of a target package. The Cantor target package \(T_{1}\) of Subsubsection 13.3.3 uses a packaged completion \(E_{\tau,\ell}=U_{\ell}\circ Q_{\ell}\circ K^{\tau}\), not a repeated single completion.
\item
  \emph{No strictness-implies-closure.} The paper does not assert that a strict-bridge passage \(\mathrm{Promote}(B):\texttt{strict}\) implies macro-dynamics closure of either side of the bridge. CM\_9 of Appendix C, named in Subsection 9.8, records a strict bridge without closure.
\item
  \emph{No strictness-implies-drive.} The paper does not assert that a strict-bridge passage implies a \(\mathrm{P6}_{\mathrm{drive}}\) certificate on either side. CM\_10 of Appendix C, named in Subsection 9.8, records a strict bridge without drive.
\end{itemize}

conclusion: No route-mismatch-implies-drive. The paper does not assert that a P_ 3 route-mismatch witness implies a P6_ drive certificate. CM_2 of Section 9 records a route mismatch without drive, and the cohomology nonclaims of Subsubsection 13.4.4 record the corresponding model-level form. No refinement-implies-improvement. The paper does not assert that a refinement A_ k A_ improves every defect record. CM_5 of Section 9 records a refinement that worsens closure under a chosen defect measure. No local-implies-global. The paper does not assert that local admissibility of a package implies global admissibility. CM_3 of Section 9 records local packages that fail globally.

conclusion: No audit-is-truth. The paper does not assert that a claim status accepted under instrument I is instrument-free truth. The instrument-indexed claim form of Subsection 11.1.3 fixes acceptance as relative to I and the surrounding context Gamma; T . No same-level complete self-certification. The paper does not assert that a single instrument I_ 0 certifies its own complete soundness. Theorem 24 of Section 11 records the formal failure: same-level complete self-soundness is either outside_scope or undefined_circular under I_ 0 . No rotating-audit finality. The paper does not assert that a finite rotating-audit chain is final. Theorem 25 of Section 11 and the non-finality clause of Subsubsection 11.8.3 record that a finite rotating-audit chain audits the lower stack but does not certify its top. No accepted claim overreads hidden content. The paper does not assert that an accepted claim under I implies any fact about I -suppressed content. Theorem 23 of Section 11 records the formal no-overreading result.
expanded_source_wording_tex:
\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \emph{No audit-is-truth.} The paper does not assert that a claim status \(\texttt{accepted}\) under instrument \(I\) is instrument-free truth. The instrument-indexed claim form of Subsection 11.1.3 fixes acceptance as relative to \(I\) and the surrounding context \(\Gamma;\mathcal T\).
\item
  \emph{No same-level complete self-certification.} The paper does not assert that a single instrument \(I_{0}\) certifies its own complete soundness. Theorem 24 of Section 11 records the formal failure: same-level complete self-soundness is either \(\texttt{outside\_scope}\) or \(\texttt{undefined\_circular}\) under \(I_{0}\).
\item
  \emph{No rotating-audit finality.} The paper does not assert that a finite rotating-audit chain is final. Theorem 25 of Section 11 and the non-finality clause of Subsubsection 11.8.3 record that a finite rotating-audit chain audits the lower stack but does not certify its top.
\item
  \emph{No accepted claim overreads hidden content.} The paper does not assert that an accepted claim under \(I\) implies any fact about \(I\)-suppressed content. Theorem 23 of Section 11 records the formal no-overreading result.
\end{itemize}

The fragment discipline of Subsection 13.1.2 records the corresponding rule. No PICA universality. The paper does not assert that PICA realizes the entire BirdInt^ aud _ fin calculus. It is a PICA-profile model fact under the cell profile lambda_ PICA . No raw implementation status as formal status. The fallback-default cap of Subsubsection 13.2.8 records that fallback supports at most real_provisional unless an explicit upgrade bridge is recorded, and CM_11 of Appendix C gives the corresponding finite source-policy countermodel. The paper does not assert that the cohomological drive certificate [a]≠ 0 exhausts every notion of drive. The cohomology nonclaims of Subsubsection 13.4.4 record P6_ drive ^ H^1 as one finite certificate family, not all drive. No double-category completeness. expanded_source_wording_tex:
\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \emph{No model-realization-as-universal-theorem.} The paper does not assert that a \(\texttt{model\_realization}\) verdict promotes to a theorem-grade \(\texttt{accepted}\) verdict, or that it proves the declared structure universally, without an admissible bridge. The fragment discipline of Subsection 13.1.2 records the corresponding rule.
\item
  \emph{No PICA universality.} The paper does not assert that PICA realizes the entire \(\mathbf{BirdInt}^{\mathrm{aud}}_{\mathrm{fin}}\) calculus. The PICA realization is host-bound and fragment-scoped to the finite stochastic cell/pair/provenance fragment.
\item
  \emph{No PICA \(6\times 6\) universal algebra.} The paper does not assert that the recovered \(6\times 6\) multiplicity count of Subsubsection 13.2.5 is a universal \(6\times 6\) law of \(\mathbf{BirdInt}^{\mathrm{aud}}_{\mathrm{fin}}\). It is a PICA-profile model fact under the cell profile \(\lambda_{\mathrm{PICA}}\).
\item
  \emph{No raw implementation status as formal status.} The paper does not assert that a raw PICA implementation status is a formal directed-cell status without recovery and classifier check; Subsubsection 13.2.6 records the recovery step.
\item
  \emph{No fallback-as-real-source.} The paper does not assert that a fallback record supports a real pair observable. The fallback-default cap of Subsubsection 13.2.8 records that fallback supports at most \(\texttt{real\_provisional}\) unless an explicit upgrade bridge is recorded, and CM\_11 of Appendix C gives the corresponding finite source-policy countermodel.
\item
  \emph{No dirty-state realness.} The paper does not assert that a dirty record can support a real pair observable under any host configuration of \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{PICA}}\); Subsubsection 13.2.8 records the dirty-state exclusion.
\item
  \emph{No Cantor generalization beyond audited shell.} The paper does not assert that the Cantor strict-bridge realization extends beyond the audited shell \(\mathcal S_{\mathrm{aud}}\). Subsubsection 13.3.9 records the corresponding nonclaim register.
\item
  \emph{No AI totality.} The paper does not assert that the abstract-interpretation host realizes the entire calculus. The realized fragment is \(P_{1}/P_{2}/P_{4}/P_{5}/P_{6}\); a full six-role AI realization would require additional \(P_{3}\) data, and no such extension is asserted here.
\item
  \emph{No graph cohomology as all drive.} The paper does not assert that the cohomological drive certificate \([a]\neq 0\) exhausts every notion of drive. The cohomology nonclaims of Subsubsection 13.4.4 record \(\mathrm{P6}_{\mathrm{drive}}^{H^1}\) as one finite certificate family, not all drive.
\item
  \emph{No double-category completeness.} The paper does not assert that the finite decorated-square fragment of Section 14 replaces or supersedes the core calculus. Subsubsection 14.5.1 records the corresponding nonclaim.
\item
  \emph{No mechanization beyond manifest scope.} The paper does not assert proof-assistant certification for any theorem, definition, model realization, or audit record outside \texttt{lean/manifest.toml}. The audit-grade verdict of Proposition 35 records the completed Lean validation artifact for the finite manifest scope, not a certificate for unlisted statements, empirical implementations, or unrestricted host extensions.
\end{itemize}

source_wording_digest: Host , the finite and scoped host inventory, recording finite carriers, finite maps, finite records, finite relations, finite diagrams, finite graphs, and finite audit records (Subsection 2.1); Cont , the finite content set whose records may be visible, suppressed, outside-scope, or unknown under an instrument (Subsections 3.2 and 3.5); P=\ P_ 1 ,P_ 2 ,P_ 3 ,P_ 4 ,P_ 5 ,P_ 6 \ , the finite primitive labels with stable role glosses (Subsection 2.2); Lev , the finite level set \ Beh,Ver,Str\ used by the calculus (Subsection 2.2.3); Instr , the finite class of instrument records, with components introduced in Subsection 3.4 and used in the claim semantics of Subsection 11.1; Pkg , the finite class of theory packages with components (Z,f,Sigma_ f ,E, A) (Subsection 3.3); Prof , the finite typed profile family lambda with admissibility predicates (Subsection 3.6); Wit , the finite typed witness family for primitive informants (Subsection 3.7 and Table A.2); Upd , the finite typed update family for primitive actors (Subsection 3.7 and Table A.3); Def , the finite typed defect family with per-component schemas (Subsections 5.2 through 5.5 and Table A.6); Judg , the finite typed judgment family — role-channel, directed-cell, pair-observable, promotion, claim, gate, square — with per-judgment admissibility predicates (Subsections 4.2 through 4.7, 10.2, 11.1, and 14.1); Status , the seven finite status families, with their family-specific classifier and priority rules where defined (Subsection 5.1 and Table A.5); Gate , the finite typed gate family — eight promotion gates, the strict-pass gate, and bridge-admissibility gates (Subsection 10.2); Dep , the finite dependency record, recording producer/consumer relations among store entries and the dependency-graph schema (Subsection 4.6); Audit , the finite typed audit family — host audit, claim audit, bridge audit, rotating-audit (Subsection 4.8 and Section 11); Nonclaim , the finite nonclaim register N (Subsection 16.4 and per-record nonclaim subfields throughout).

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\begin{enumerate}
\def\arabic{enumi}.{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{Universal six-symbol algebra.} No total operation \(\ast:\mathbb P^{2}\to\mathbb P\) recovers cell status across profiles. Theorem 1 of Section 6 records the formal counterexample, and \(\mathrm{NC}\text{-}1\) of Subsection 16.4 records the corresponding nonclaim.
\item
  \textbf{All mathematics is six birds.} The claim that every mathematical structure decomposes into the six primitives is dropped; \(\mathbf{BirdInt}^{\mathrm{aud}}_{\mathrm{fin}}\) is a finite typed audited interaction calculus, not a foundation for all mathematics. \(\mathrm{NC}\text{-}2\) of Subsection 16.4 records the corresponding nonclaim.
\item
  \textbf{Unrestricted exact-six.} The unrestricted decomposition claim, that every typed interaction is exactly representable as one of the thirty-six directed cells, is dropped. The exact-six structure is a finite typed schema with admissibility conditions, not an unrestricted decomposition theorem. The dropped claim is recorded in Subsubsection 1.3.2 and the corresponding nonclaim in \(\mathrm{NC}\text{-}1\) and the algebra/universality grouping of Subsubsection 16.2.1.
\item
  \textbf{PICA as canonical algebra.} The claim that PICA defines the canonical \(6\times 6\) algebra of the calculus is dropped. PICA is a finite stochastic model realization, scoped to the cell/pair/provenance fragment, and the recovered \(6\times 6\) multiplicity count is a profile fact, not a universal law. PICA nonclaims 1 and 2 of Subsubsection 13.2.10 and \(\mathrm{NC}\text{-}20\), \(\mathrm{NC}\text{-}21\) of Subsection 16.4 record the corresponding nonclaims.
\item
  \textbf{Cantor pressure gap as unbridged strictness witness.} The claim that the pressure-gap defect \(\Delta_{T_{0}\to T_{1}}\) is itself the strictness witness, rather than a consequence of the strictness witness, is dropped. The strictness witness is the factorization defect \(\Delta_{\mathrm{fact}}^{\mathrm{Cantor}}\); the pressure-gap defect is recorded as a consequence record. Cantor nonclaim 7 of Subsubsection 13.3.9 and \(\mathrm{NC}\text{-}27\) of Subsection 16.4 record the corresponding nonclaim.
\item
  \textbf{Provenance as proof.} The claim that provenance records constitute proof of any underlying mathematical fact is dropped. Provenance records are finite typed records of producer, source, audit, and visibility data; they support pair-realness and source-of-truth predicates but are not theorem-grade proofs of mathematical claims. The audit nonclaim \(\mathrm{NC}\text{-}15\) of Subsection 16.4 (no audit-is-truth) records the corresponding boundary.
\item
  \textbf{High-structure semantics as replacement calculus.} The claim that the finite decorated double-category fragment of Section 14 replaces or supersedes the core calculus is dropped. The decorated-square fragment is a secondary organizational layer; it records three specific recoveries (Theorems 30--32) and not a general claim that every theorem-grade fact reduces to a decorated-square fact. \(\mathrm{NC}\text{-}34\), \(\mathrm{NC}\text{-}35\) of Subsection 16.4 record the corresponding nonclaims.
\end{enumerate}

conclusion: Foundations IV is not a foundational reset of Foundations I/II/III, not a unification claim about the eight axes, and not an exhaustive catalog.
expanded_source_wording_tex:
Foundations IV is a catalog of layer-agnostic structural laws built on
the Foundations I/II/III apparatus. Its organizing question is what
must be true, before choosing a substrate---whether analysis,
arithmetic, physics, biology, chemistry, economics and finance,
linguistics, cognitive and social science, or computation---for a
layer to have lawful access, stable records, transport, symmetry,
closure, and limits.  The contribution is
a uniform normal-form template applied across 52 laws; each row states
its setup, theorem, proof spine, case structure, interaction status,
and nonclaims, so recurring obstructions such as failed descent, hidden
predictive structure, local-global failure, and record nonclosure can
be compared in one register.  The formalization status is explicit: the
catalog contains 46 direct Lean theorems, 2 substrate-delegated anchors
(No-Needles Stability and Closure--Reality Boundary), 2 partial
wrappers (Hiddenness and Duality Fixity), and 2 obligation wrappers
(CSL Formed-Closure and Spontaneous Symmetry Breaking); the four
trust-base axioms used by the wrappers are disclosed through an
opacity-guard pattern, each guarded by an opaque source predicate that
prevents the axiom from being instantiated without the corresponding
substrate or future-source certificate.  Foundations IV is not a
foundational reset of Foundations I/II/III, not a unification claim
about the eight axes, and not an exhaustive catalog.

conclusion: In each case there is a setup, an obstruction, a repair or boundary, and a statement of what the theorem does not claim.
expanded_source_wording_tex:
The example is intentionally elementary.  It uses no special
operator theory, no hidden regularity hypothesis, and no category
larger than the quotient construction itself.  Nevertheless, the
same shape appears in more elaborate settings.  A local family may
agree on overlaps but fail to come from a global object.  A symmetric
construction may be unable to choose a non-fixed branch without
adding symmetry-breaking data.  A formally closed record may exist
without being physically instantiated.  A finite observation may
determine all declared future probes, or fail precisely because some
future probe separates states the present quotient cannot see.  In
each case there is a setup, an obstruction, a repair or boundary, and
a statement of what the theorem does not claim.  The purpose of this
paper is to put those repeated shapes into a common register.

conclusion: This theorem does not re-prove the saturated-SAT closure result of the PvNP paper , and it does not assert any conclusion about a specific computational complexity class.
expanded_source_wording_tex:
This theorem does not re-prove the saturated-SAT closure result of
the PvNP paper \citep{Tsiokos2026PvNP}, and it does not assert any
conclusion about a specific computational complexity class.  It
records the layer-agnostic access law: hiddenness means that a
predictive distinction exists upstream of current access, and
exposure is the minimal quotient refinement that removes that gap.
The classical quantum-foundations instance of a non-contextual
hidden-variable obstruction is the Kochen--Specker theorem
\citep{KochenSpecker1967Hidden}; that is a substrate-specific
result, not a special case of the layer-agnostic law above.

same-layer case, the previous paragraph blocks complete
self-soundness.  In the meta-layer case, a certificate supplies

\[
  \operatorname{Audits}_{\mu}(m,c)
  \quad\text{and}\quad
  \neg\operatorname{SelfSound}_{\pi}(c),
\]
so the audit has moved to a strict meta-layer.  Therefore any claim
of complete same-layer self-soundness lies outside the scope of
\(\pi\).
\end{proof}

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\item[\emph{Sarbanes-Oxley independent-audit mandate
(corporate-finance regulation).}]
The Sarbanes-Oxley Act of 2002 forbids public-company
financial statements from being audited by the issuer's
own accounting staff.  Management's internal-controls
assessment under \S404(a) is the scoped lower audit; the
independent CPA firm's attestation under \S404(b) is the
meta-layer certificate, and the auditor is itself
overseen by the Public Company Accounting Oversight
Board, producing a tower of meta-audits.  Complete
self-attestation by the issuer is outside the scope of
the regime \citep{SarbanesOxley2002Act}.

conclusion: Complete in-certificate self-trust is outside the scope of the protocol .
expanded_source_wording_tex:
\item[\emph{X.509 PKI external root-of-trust
(cryptographic protocol design).}]
In the X.509 public-key infrastructure, an endpoint
certificate cannot self-certify its trustworthiness to a
relying party: validation requires a chain of signatures
terminating at a root certificate authority in the
client's externally maintained trust store, which acts
as the meta-layer.  The leaf's own self-signature and
local syntactic integrity checks are the scoped lower
audit; self-signed leaves are rejected by default by
mainstream TLS clients.  Complete in-certificate
self-trust is outside the scope of the protocol
\citep{Cooper2008RFC5280}.

conclusion: it does not prove that this joint access is in an admissible access class.
expanded_source_wording_tex:
\paragraph{D1 cases.}
If one input quotient already refines the other, their repair join is
fiber-equivalent to the finer input.  The join of a constant quotient with
\(r\) is \(r\); the join with a discrete quotient is discrete; and on an
empty carrier the universal property holds vacuously.  Presentations with
different or even non-isomorphic codomains are compared only by their fiber
relations.  These cases also fix the order convention: under the
finer-to-coarser order, the operation named \(\vee\) in this corpus is
meet-shaped.  Most importantly, D1 constructs the unrestricted common
refinement; it does \emph{not} prove that this joint access is in an admissible
access class.  The Foundations IV F37 obstruction remains a separate gate.

D3 makes the apparatus a carried record, and E1 applied at apparatus level supplies lawful repair. Since object closure and apparatus maintenance are separately typed certificates—the latter maps a carrier state to an apparatus and compares consecutive apparatus records—object closure alone does not imply apparatus maintenance. This paper does not claim the untested reverse nonimplication. The ablation witness makes the proved separation finite and measurable.
source_wording_tex:
\ProofSpine{} Foundations IV object persistence transports an already formed
object; it does not reproduce the gates and audit that form it.  D3 makes the
apparatus a carried record, and E1 applied at apparatus level supplies lawful
repair.  Since object closure and apparatus maintenance are separately typed
certificates---the latter maps a carrier state to an apparatus and compares
consecutive apparatus records---object closure alone does not imply apparatus
maintenance.  This paper does not
claim the untested reverse nonimplication.  The ablation witness makes the
proved separation finite and measurable.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\paragraph{Compilation theorem.}
The substantive \texttt{CompiledCase} definition contains the carried
candidate, lawfulness, verified in-class descent, silence of the formerly
exposed higher invocation, and the priority exclusions.  The theorem
\texttt{E4\_Compilation} is a packaging wrapper: it takes a carried status
occurrence tagged \texttt{compiled} and an already supplied full
\texttt{CompiledCase}, then returns \texttt{CompiledHolds}.  Its window-level
obstruction-reduction and idempotence-stability arguments are retained for
statement fidelity but unused by the current Lean proof.  The current
\texttt{CompiledOperatorRecordAttributedTo} interface takes the window as an
argument but does not prove an equality or citation to its episode list;
exact-window attribution therefore remains a host/paper obligation.  The
carried compiled operator is indexed by the same challenge class and repair
refinement.  The result is intentionally verification-shaped: the
top-down channel and descent certificates are host inputs checked by their
interfaces; Lean proves that the complete certificate entails the status and
its consequences.

conclusion: Failure to prove irreversibility alone does not prove recoverability.
expanded_source_wording_tex:
\begin{proof}[Proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:e5}]
Completeness turns the universal phrase ``no admissible carried move'' into a
finite inventory statement.  If an in-budget linked candidate descends, the
definition supplies a collapse falsifier, and the falsifier theorem shows
collapsed core is false.  If none exists,
collapsed core holds.  Coherent unreachability of both repair generator and
apparatus viability kernel in a supplied
\texttt{IrreversibleCollapseInput} selects irreversible collapse.  The
recoverable branch requires its own \texttt{RecoverableCollapseInput}:
coherent evidence of self-reachability, external-only reachability, or a
nonempty kernel, together with explicit negation of the irreversible input.
Failure to prove irreversibility alone does not prove recoverability.  A fully linked external descent is
classified by the subsidy witness before either collapsed branch only when
the witness's no-internal-rescue condition and priority exclusions hold;
external descent alone is insufficient.  Intact apparatus plus
gated-off operations selects suspension.  A later internal rescue with a new
lineage selects revival.  The evidence-priority definitions make these
branches pairwise disjoint, and occurrence completeness supplies existence
and same-claim status-kind uniqueness.
\end{proof}

conclusion: These are direct operational instantiations, conditional on the comparator and inventory certificates.
expanded_source_wording_tex:
\paragraph{Layer-specific bridge obligations.}
\begin{description}[style=nextline,leftmargin=2.4em]
\item[Living systems.]
A transcriptional, immune, bioelectric, or metabolic package qualifies only
when perturbing that carried package changes the organism's own future
support and strictly discharges the named viability obstruction.  A
biomarker readable by an experimenter supplies only the correlate branch.
This application is structural and empirical-candidate grade; it makes no
consciousness claim.
\item[Cognitive systems.]
A plan, working-memory state, or learned controller must restrict or orient
action before the outcome under matched controls.  Goals additionally
survive route substitution.  These are direct operational instantiations,
conditional on the comparator and inventory certificates.
\item[Social and economic systems.]
A decision rule, policy package, or governance procedure qualifies only
when its carried invocation changes admissible organizational action and
repairs the declared class.  Minutes or labels that merely predict later
behavior remain correlates; externally installed compliance machinery is
scaffolding unless and until its source status changes.
\end{description}

conclusion: Merely locating a membrane, API, or legal perimeter does not prove this clause.
expanded_source_wording_tex:
For a boundary quotient $B_I$, viability sufficiency and coarsestness are
separate:
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathsf{ViabilitySufficientBoundary}(I,B_I)\iff{}&
\mathsf{SufficiencyClosureCertified}(I,B_I)\\
&{}\land
\forall\pi\in\mathcal Q_{\rm sufficient}\ \exists f,\quad
B_I=f\circ\pi.
\end{aligned}
\]
The direction matters.  Every sufficient quotient $\pi$ may retain extra
distinctions; the boundary keeps no distinction not forced by the declared
viability futures.  Self-maintenance then reuses an actual E3
reinstatement:
\[
\begin{aligned}
\exists t,A_t,A_{t+1},m,R,\quad
&\mathsf{BoundaryApparatus}(I,B_I,A_t)\\
&{}\land\mathsf{MaintenanceReinstatementFor}
  (t,A_t,A_{t+1},m,R)\\
&{}\land I(R.\mathsf{sourceState}).
\end{aligned}
\]
Merely locating a membrane, API, or legal perimeter does not prove this
clause.

conclusion: Lean does not assert that the candidate list exhausts every subcarrier
expanded_source_wording_tex:
The converse for the integrated row is projection: its case contains
maximal individuation, hence all joint closure conditions.  The theorem is
relative to the declared candidate list and certified boundary and viability
records.  Lean does not assert that the candidate list exhausts every
subcarrier; it checks the closure combination, list-relative maximality
predicate, and partition rather than discovering the biologically or
socially correct carrier boundary from raw measurements.
\end{proof}

conclusion: It is the finite-inventory limitation that prevents the paper from claiming robustness against every latent variable.
expanded_source_wording_tex:
One negative governance result is especially important.  An undeclared
proxy cannot be detected by a classifier whose complete universe does not
contain it; the mechanical fixture can retain coherent status until the
proxy is declared and the support controls are rerun.  This is not evidence
that the proxy is harmless.  It is the finite-inventory limitation that
prevents the paper from claiming robustness against every latent variable.
The nine discipline checks record actual-scope, no-hardcoding,
off-inventory-dissipation, predictive-reveal, administrative-rejection,
wrong-claim-E15, same-ID content mutation, same-ID perturbation mutation, and
pair-local flatness isolation.

\paragraph{Formal correspondence and boundary.}
The module \path|Laws.E16Adaptability| contains the canonical route package,
endpoint trial inventories, exact distributions, E15 reconciliation bridge,
five complete control inventories (protocol counterpart, completion,
refinement, continuation, and perturbation), four freedom certificates,
eight evidence/case/Holds families, three
fidelity regressions, and the main consequence theorems.  The direct proved
spine imports canonical Holonomy quotient transport and asymmetry, D4 repair
trials, E6/E9 budget records, and the actual E15 residue type.  Route
admissibility, trial eligibility, ledger probability semantics, control
universes, and bridge acceptance remain certified.  The E15-to-E16 status
obligation is discharged.  The source root aggregator currently omits the
E16 import even though this module, its sweep, review record, and theorem
declarations are present; this is a packaging limitation, not a missing
paper proof.

The module |Laws.E16Adaptability| contains the canonical route package, endpoint trial inventories, exact distributions, E15 reconciliation bridge, five complete control inventories (protocol counterpart, completion, refinement, continuation, and perturbation), four freedom certificates, eight evidence/case/Holds families, three fidelity regressions, and the main consequence theorems. The direct proved spine imports canonical Holonomy quotient transport and asymmetry, D4 repair trials, E6/E9 budget records, and the actual E15 residue type. Route admissibility, trial eligibility, ledger probability semantics, control universes, and bridge acceptance remain certified. The E15-to-E16 status obligation is discharged. The source root aggregator currently omits the E16 import even though this module, its sweep, review record, and theorem declarations are present; this is a packaging limitation, not a missing paper proof.

\paragraph{Formal correspondence and boundary.}
The module \path|Laws.E16Adaptability| contains the canonical route package,
endpoint trial inventories, exact distributions, E15 reconciliation bridge,
five complete control inventories (protocol counterpart, completion,
refinement, continuation, and perturbation), four freedom certificates,
eight evidence/case/Holds families, three
fidelity regressions, and the main consequence theorems.  The direct proved
spine imports canonical Holonomy quotient transport and asymmetry, D4 repair
trials, E6/E9 budget records, and the actual E15 residue type.  Route
admissibility, trial eligibility, ledger probability semantics, control
universes, and bridge acceptance remain certified.  The E15-to-E16 status
obligation is discharged.  The source root aggregator currently omits the
E16 import even though this module, its sweep, review record, and theorem
declarations are present; this is a packaging limitation, not a missing
paper proof.

\item \path|E15_DeficitOnlineFalsifiesNecessity|.
A complete classifier and a carried full
\texttt{deficit\_online\_counterexample} case yield
\[
  \mathsf{DeficitOnlineCounterexample}
  \land\neg\mathsf{AlternationRequired}.
\]
The premise includes a preregistered finite all-online horizon, persistent
strict deficit, online discharge bounded by \(\kappa_{\rm on}\), and carried
debt snapshots below the declared bound; the theorem does not assert
indefinite online persistence.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
The Six Birds corpus through Foundations~IV certifies \emph{states}: each of its laws fixes a single map,
quotient, package, or declared finite family and proves a static classification about it. Nothing in
the corpus certifies \emph{runs} --- liveness (every orbit eventually earns a certificate), amortized
or transfinite cost over unbounded time, covers that must move with their targets, obstructions that
grow, react, or are manufactured by the system's own history, route defects that integrate into
potentials, transport that emerges from substrate dynamics, or content that persists through repeated
loss. This paper is the catalog of exactly those laws: 13 dynamical structural laws
(G1--G13), organized in 4 clusters, each stated in the six-part normal form inherited
verbatim from Foundations~IV and each carrying a temporal quantifier that no static row possesses. The
laws were mined from eccentric mathematical problems --- Collatz, Goodstein, Egyptian fractions,
reverse-and-add, Recam\'an, the angel problem, sandpiles, rule 184, Ducci, aperiodic tilings,
Hadwiger--Nelson, Apollonian packings --- treated as theorem detectors: each problem's folklore
almost-proof names a promoted object, the object's lawful descended certificate fixes a boundary
expression, and the residual surviving comparison against every existing law is the law seed. All
thirteen laws are mechanized in Mathlib-free Lean~4 with per-declaration kernel-axiom audits; six
laws are full \texttt{theorem}-grade rows and one splits into an unconditional theorem and a schema,
four are \texttt{schema}-grade with named boxed hypotheses, and three are calibration-anchored
schemas discharged end-to-end by solved classical instances. The paper solves no open problem and
claims none: Collatz, Erd\H{o}s--Straus, Lychrel, Recam\'an, the Langton's-ant highway, Gilbreath,
and the exact chromatic number of the plane all remain open, and each law's nonclaims say so
explicitly.
