expanded_source_wording_tex:
\paragraph{Needles, membranes, and lawful repairs.} A \emph{needle} is a localized obstruction
surviving all native-layer probes; the corpus discipline prices needles against a declared budget,
dissolves them by promotion, or confines them by duality \citep{Tsiokos2026NeedleKiller}. A
\emph{membrane} is a budget condition holding at every accepted stage, and its failure is a critical
pair with exactly five lawful repairs (declared nonclaim, raised budget, rewritten carrier/audit,
genuinely new probes, completed transport family) --- same-package repetition is not a repair. In the
corpus every needle, budget, and probe family is declared up front and static; Clusters B and D live
precisely in the gap this leaves (history-generated needles, adversarial needles, and needles whose
survival is a positive certificate).

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\paragraph{The catalog form, status tags, and discharge vocabulary.} Foundations~IV presents its
fifty-two laws in a six-part normal form --- Setup, Theorem, Proof spine, Case enumeration,
Interaction status, Nonclaims --- each with five worked layer instantiations
\citep{Tsiokos2026FoundIV}; this paper adopts the template verbatim. One verified fact about that
catalog does structural work everywhere here: every F-IV Setup names fixed, singular data --- one
map, one quotient pair, one declared finite patch system --- and every F-IV theorem is a static
classification of that fixed data; no row contains a step-indexed quantifier, a growing family, an
adversary, a rate comparison, or an emergence-over-time claim. The temporal quantifier is therefore
the novelty axis of every G-law, and each law's Setup states it explicitly. Status tags are
three-valued and typographically fixed: \texttt{theorem} (the abstract implication is proved),
\texttt{schema} (named hypotheses carry the implication; no concrete instance is asserted to satisfy
them until discharged), and \texttt{calibration-anchored schema} (a schema whose mechanism is fully
discharged by a recognized solved classical instance). Residual accounting uses the AOR status
vocabulary \citep{Tsiokos2026AOR}, including the four asymptotic statuses recalled in
\Cref{sec:currency-taxonomy}, and the corpus nonclaim register is in force throughout --- most
prominently: route mismatch never implies drive content (G8's bridge is conditional on its named
hypotheses, which is legal); local admissibility never implies global admissibility without
exhaustion data (G4, G11); no same-level self-certification (G6, G7 are theorist-side); and promoted
support is never literalized at the native layer (all of Cluster A)
\citep{Tsiokos2026FoundIII}.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
For each problem, in order:
\begin{enumerate}
  \item \textbf{Identify the tempting almost-proof} --- the argument everyone reaches for that fails.
    The almost-proof reveals the illegal overread.
  \item \textbf{Name the promoted object the almost-proof secretly uses} --- an invariant measure on a
    completion, a fixed finite certificate package, a well-founded escrow. Typically the object does
    not descend to the native carrier.
  \item \textbf{State what a lawful descended certificate would be.} This fixes the boundary
    expression: the native, checkable assertion that promoted support is allowed to purchase
    (\Cref{sec:apparatus}).
  \item \textbf{Isolate the residual that survives every existing law.} Run the candidate against the
    full Foundations~IV catalog (exact statements, not summaries), the Foundations~V laws, the
    nonclaim register, and the AOR status list. What remains unhandled is the law seed --- and this
    step kills candidates as often as it produces them.
  \item \textbf{Find the siblings.} The seed is a law only if the same residual shape appears in at
    least three independent domains, at least one of them solved (the calibration instance).
    Otherwise it is a substrate observation, not a law.
\end{enumerate}
Admission then passes four further gates inherited from the corpus's discipline: a precise recognition
source making every Setup datum definite; a rebadge test requiring the candidate to differ from every
existing law on at least one declared axis --- for all thirteen laws here the differentiating axis is
the same, a step-indexed, growing, adversarial, or rate-comparison witness schema that no static
catalog row possesses, which is why an editing pass that accidentally deletes a temporal quantifier
from a law's statement collapses the law into its cousin and fails the gate; nonclaim compatibility
(a law that needs an unconditional version of a forbidden inference is dead); and a replication
ladder on the instantiation table (at least one solved calibration plus at least one instance with
genuine engagement beyond citation). The remainder of this section runs the protocol on four seeds:
two that became laws, and two that the protocol correctly killed.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
In interaction terms, G8 turns P3 route data into P6 audit content through a P2 conservation gate: the
legal firing order is route data, the counter vector is bookkeeping, and \textup{[H-G8]} is the gate
that makes the bookkeeping conserved across all legal routes. The claim is conditional on that gate
and on termination; it is not an unconditional inference from route mismatch to potential. The
computational record exercises both sides. Lab G8-L1 ran $500$ seeded random stabilizations on square
sandpile grids of sizes $10, 20, 30, 40, 50$ ($100$ random legal orders per configuration) and found
every run agreeing with the deterministic baselines in both final configuration and odometer vector.
Lab G8-L2 sampled $1000$ random legal orders of the case~(b) witness: every run reached $N$, and
exactly three distinct counter vectors appeared --- confluence without a canonical ledger, as the law
predicts.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\paragraph{Conditionality where the register demands it.} Each law is exactly as conditional as the
corpus's nonclaim register requires, and several hypotheses are load-bearing by design. G8's abelian
compatibility is named and non-negotiable --- terminating confluence alone determines no canonical
counter ledger (the case-(b) witness), and Part~B's least action is the legal-versus-legal
comparison only. G9's transport is certified by recurrence-with-displacement records, never by
holonomy or visual motion; nothing in G8 or G9 is a drive, arrow, or entropy-production claim, and
that vocabulary stays reserved. G4 and G11 are conditional on their exhaustion and per-period
certificate data --- local admissibility never globalizes for free, and G11 supplies no algorithm
against Berger's undecidability. G5's no-go half is not an escape certificate; its confinement half
requires a verified target-free closed language. G6 and G7 are theorist-side throughout: the system
never certifies itself, and the adversary's strategy space is always declared --- no hidden-oracle
devil. G6's two rate hypotheses are proposed formalizations that later labs may refine, and its
designed-variant calibrations deliberately do not upgrade its grade. G7's thresholds are board- and
rule-relative; its finite-board lab is an exhibit, not infinite-board evidence. G10 does not
contradict the corpus's information-loss results and reconstructs nothing lost; its hypotheses must
be proved, not observed empirically. G12's compactness bridge is a purchased set-theoretic
commitment, recorded, and choice sensitivity in plane-coloring questions is a real warning; the
826-vertex lab witness is solver-verified UNSAT without an independent proof-checked certificate,
as its provenance record states. G13's status ceiling is \texttt{schema}; ``thin'' and ``thick''
carry only their strict technical senses, and congruence admissibility is local and incomplete ---
the 2024 reciprocity obstruction shows exactly that. Throughout Cluster A, promoted objects
(ledgers, escrows, completions, ghosts) are never literalized at the native layer; only boundary
certificates descend.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
Many mathematical frameworks come with audit data alongside their
main objects: source ledgers, route registries, residual budgets,
status annotations, nonclaim boundaries, and meta-audit records.
\emph{Audited Operational Realisability} (AOR) is the meta-theory of
typed carriers that close as audit systems within a declared scope.
A \emph{PreSB carrier} is a typed carrier together with this audit
data; it is an \emph{AOR carrier} when every declared audit
obligation is discharged inside the scope.  We show that every PreSB
carrier \(\PreSB_{\mathfrak S}\) admits a canonical completion into
the full subcategory of AOR carriers via a reflection
\(\mathrm{Cl}_{SB}\dashv\iota\) obtained as a monotone Knaster--Tarski
saturation on the complete lattice of AOR-extending operations.  The
reflection is developed in four parts: the closure-completion
construction and its universal property; the eight-stratum
decomposition of the structural defect \(\Xi_{SB}\); the thirteen-type
residual atlas, with reciprocal local and global mismatch types, its
discharge cascades, and cascade-stable AOR; and refinement chains with asymptotic
statuses, yielding the hierarchy
\(\mathbf{AOR}^{\mathrm{ref}}\subseteq\mathbf{AOR}^{\mathrm{casc}}\subseteq\mathbf{AOR}\).  The
development is meta-theoretic and carries no PDE-specific worked
example; concrete AOR-instance applications belong to consumer
manuscripts that cite this meta-theory at paper level.  Two scope
disclosures apply.  The cascade-confluence theorem uses Newman's lemma
as a classical body input after proving the local diamond property and
the well-founded discharge relation; Appendix~D records the corresponding
formal companion row as partial.  The hierarchy is exhibited via named
witness carriers and their typed obstruction markers; full predicate-level
non-membership proofs at every level remain framework future work.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
Fix a scope record \(\mathfrak S\) declaring the admissible
carrier-class, source ledger, interface family, and route registry.
The category \(\PreSB_{\mathfrak S}\) consists of typed carriers
equipped with declared audit data over \(\mathfrak S\) --- observation,
stage, constraint, rewrite, holonomy, residual, status, nonclaim, and
meta-audit registries --- together with morphisms preserving the
scoped package.  Its full subcategory \(\AOR_{\mathfrak S}\) contains
the audit-closed carriers, those whose declared records, routes,
residuals, nonclaims, and meta-audits have all been typed, registered,
statused, or discharged inside \(\mathfrak S\).  The central question
is the corresponding closure problem: when does an arbitrary object of
\(\PreSB_{\mathfrak S}\) admit a canonical completion into
\(\AOR_{\mathfrak S}\), and what is the structure of that completion?

expanded_source_wording_tex:
The first diagnostic device is the structural defect \(\Xi_{SB}\).  For a
PreSB carrier, \(\Xi_{SB}\) measures the aggregate failure of audit
closure.  It has eight named strata: observation, stage, constraint,
rewrite, holonomy, residual, nonclaim, and meta-audit.  AOR membership
therefore decomposes: it holds exactly when every stratum is empty.  The
residual stratum is refined further by a thirteen-type residual atlas:
descent, transport, interface, local mismatch, global mismatch,
presentation, source admission, horizon, scale, limit, symmetry, role,
and target typing.
Residual atoms carry statuses drawn from the AOR-8 catalogue and may
generate downstream obligations, so audit closure is also an
operational question about how discharge propagates.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
The framework developed here abstracts an audit discipline that
already appears in the formed-layer membrane theory of
\citet{Tsiokos2026NeedleKiller}.  In that setting the mathematical
object of interest is never just a bare carrier; it is accompanied by
records of which probes are native, which routes are legal, which
residuals remain unpaid, which statements are explicitly outside
scope, and which bookkeeping obligations have been accepted.  We do
not rederive that membrane theory, but isolate the meta-theoretic
pattern behind it: a carrier can be meaningfully used only after its
record layer has been audited inside a declared scope.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
The adequacy-residual calculus of \citet{Tsiokos2026XiCompanion}
supplies a second motivating source.  There the central object is the
Schur-complement residual \(\Xi_C(D\mid L)\), measuring what a
dissolving probe family \(D\) cannot explain through a native probe
family \(L\) under an audit operator \(C\).  The calculus distinguishes
native explanation from leftover residual, exact adequacy from
defective adequacy, and lawful promotion from blind-spot failure.
AOR neither imports those theorems nor depends on them; it abstracts
the surrounding bookkeeping question: once a residual, route, status,
or nonclaim has been declared, what does it mean for the whole
carrier to be audit-closed?

conclusion: The fieldwise meet of any family keeps precisely the data common to all packages, and the fieldwise generated join adjoins the union of all carrier, route, residual, nonclaim, and meta-audit data while retaining only well-typed scope-compatible entries.
expanded_source_wording_tex:
\begin{proof}
Fix the scope \(\mathfrak S\) and a seed carrier \(\mathsf C\).  Let
\(\mathcal L_{\mathfrak S}(\mathsf C)\) be the poset of AOR-extending
operation packages over \(\mathsf C\), ordered by subcarrier inclusion and
typed-field extension.  The fieldwise meet of any family keeps precisely the
data common to all packages, and the fieldwise generated join adjoins the
union of all carrier, route, residual, nonclaim, and meta-audit data while
retaining only well-typed scope-compatible entries.  These operations give a
complete lattice.  The saturation endomap \(S\) sends a package to the same
package together with the minimal operations forced by its currently missing
AOR obligations.  If \(X\le Y\), then every obligation visible in \(X\) is
also visible in \(Y\), and every operation forced over \(X\) is included
among the operations forced over \(Y\); hence \(S(X)\le S(Y)\).

Knaster--Tarski \citep{TarskiFixedPoint1955} now gives a least fixed
point \(\mathrm{lfp}(S)\).  This object contains the seed package,
because the seed is the bottom datum relative to which the lattice was

conclusion: The minimal operation sigma adds exactly one of the audit-completion data types used by the saturation map: typed-record data, route audits, residual statuses, nonclaim entries, or meta-audit discharge records.
expanded_source_wording_tex:
\begin{proof}
The minimal operation \(\sigma\) adds exactly one of the audit-completion
data types used by the saturation map: typed-record data, route audits,
residual statuses, nonclaim entries, or meta-audit discharge records.  In
each case, the AOR-extending datum of \(\sigma\) is the smallest typed
completion of \(X\) that closes the obligation \(\sigma\) addresses.  The
map \(g_X\) sends the fields already present in \(X\) to a typed
configuration in \(\mathsf D\).  Because \(\mathsf D\) is AOR, the
corresponding obligation is already discharged in \(\iota\mathsf D\), so
the image of the new completion datum is forced.  This defines
\(\widetilde g_\sigma\).

The minimal operation \(\sigma\) adds exactly one of the audit-completion
data types used by the saturation map: typed-record data, route audits,

conclusion: A missing observation typing, an undeclared stage law, an unwitnessed constraint, an unannotated rewrite, a missing holonomy transport, an unstatused residual, an unregistered nonclaim, and an undischarged meta-audit obligation are different audit failures, even when they all obstruct the same conclusion that the carrier is audit-closed.
expanded_source_wording_tex:
The first diagnostic layer is the structural defect \(\Xi_{SB}\): the
aggregate record of ways in which a scoped PreSB carrier has not yet
closed as an AOR carrier.  Splitting the defect into strata keeps the
failure mode visible, in the spirit of typed fault-and-failure
taxonomies in the dependable-computing literature
\citep{Avizienis2004Dependability}.  A missing observation typing, an
undeclared stage law, an unwitnessed constraint, an unannotated
rewrite, a missing holonomy transport, an unstatused residual, an
unregistered nonclaim, and an undischarged meta-audit obligation are
different audit failures, even when they all obstruct the same
conclusion that the carrier is audit-closed.  Strata are recorded as
finite multisets in the sense of \citet{Blizard1989Multiset}, so a
record may appear with multiplicity matching the carrier-field data
that creates it.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\begin{proof}
Each defect record is created from a typed field of the carrier.  The field
that creates it also determines its stratum: an observation record belongs
to \(\Sigma_{\mathrm{obs}}\), a stage entry to \(\Sigma_{\mathrm{stage}}\), a constraint or budget entry
to \(\Sigma_{\mathrm{constraint}}\), a rewrite record to \(\Sigma_{\mathrm{rewrite}}\), a holonomy or route
memory record to \(\Sigma_{\mathrm{holonomy}}\), a residual record to \(\Sigma_{\mathrm{residual}}\), an implicit
exclusion to \(\Sigma_{\mathrm{nonclaim}}\), and a meta-audit obligation to \(\Sigma_{\mathrm{meta}}\).  These
field tags are disjoint by construction, so the structural defect is the
coproduct of the eight typed collections.  Computability is simply the
fieldwise scan of the carrier: inspect each declared record, test whether
the corresponding required annotation is present, and emit the uniquely
tagged defect record exactly when it is absent.

conclusion: The preceding sections develop AOR as a meta-theory of audit-closed carriers. Its formal objects are scope records, PreSB carriers, closure completion, defect strata, residual atoms, discharge cascades, and refinement chains; they are not a direct model of any particular analytic problem. Downstream AOR-instance manuscripts may consume the meta-theory developed here, but they are not theorem-level dependencies of it. [No strong-realism reading of AOR] Membership in AOR_ S is not a metaphysical or philosophical realism claim about the carrier's underlying domain. It is a record-level audit predicate: every declared record is typed, every cited route is audited, every residual is statused, and every nonclaim is registered, within the declared scope S . Any extra-scope interpretation requires its own audit and is outside the present framework.

audits, residual statuses, nonclaim entries, and meta-audit discharge
records, but it does not change the declared scope.  The order is
fieldwise extension, so meets and joins are computed by fieldwise
intersection and generated union subject to scope compatibility.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\noindent
Accounting-style inequalities are central in Six Birds Theory, but they do not by themselves rule out catastrophic extremes: highly localized ``needle'' probes can satisfy global budgets while producing large peaks. We ask when packaging plus accounting forces anti-localization, and propose \emph{Reflexive SBT}: a capacity-based audit of the packaged artifacts (subspaces, feasibility dictionaries, and route ladders). We define a localization metric \(\eta_j\) at cell scale \(2^{-j}\), compute it via an eigenvalue method, and upper-bound it using three auditable capacities: subspace trace/diagonal dispersion, sparse feasibility conditioning on small supports, and a route-union ledger charging multi-route inflation. We find three controlled separations: (i) shift-invariant channels (Fourier/circulant) have uniform projector diagonals and \(\eta_j\) follows the deterministic \(m/2^j\) bound, while diagonal disorder drives \(\eta_j\) rapidly toward \(1\) compared with full-noise perturbations; (ii) feasibility-level needles arise exactly when small-support conditioning collapses (\(\sigma_{\min}\!\to 0\)) and are absent in random baselines; (iii) for spectral packaging, route mismatch spikes only at degenerate cutoffs and is eliminated by a canonical tie-break, with remaining route effects captured by the union ledger. This turns the anti-localization hinge into a reproducible checklist and yields a conditional theorem: vanishing capacity implies \(\eta_j\to 0\) along a ladder. We are explicit that Reflexive SBT is not proven here to universally drive capacities to zero; we prove the capacity\(\Rightarrow\)anti-localization implications and provide auditable closure evidence on canonical failure and repair modes.

conclusion: What this paper does not claim.
expanded_source_wording_tex:
\paragraph{What this paper does not claim.}
We do \emph{not} prove that Reflexive SBT necessarily drives these capacities to zero for every admissible packaging ladder.
Instead, we give (a) theorem-quality implications of the form \emph{capacity} \(\Rightarrow\) \emph{anti-localization}, (b) counterexamples showing the capacities are not optional, and (c) an auditable Reflexive SBT loop (closure tests and primitive-move analogues) whose trajectories empirically reduce the relevant capacities on canonical obstructions.
Proving capacity decay as a consequence of SBT minimality/closure principles is a natural next-paper target; this paper supplies the clean capacity objects that such a theorem must control.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\paragraph{Symmetry breaking is not unique: diagonal disorder behaves differently than full noise.}
A key open-minded finding of the Reflexive SBT scans is that ``breaking symmetry'' can occur in qualitatively different ways.
In the eigenchannel pipeline (extracting packaged channels as eigenvectors of a perturbed operator), diagonal disorder (Anderson-style \cite{anderson1958}) rapidly increases localization at fine scales, while full Wigner-type noise \cite{wigner1958_roots} does not in the same parameter range.
This suggests that diagonal non-uniformity is a more direct driver of trace capacity than generic non-commutation alone.
We emphasize that we do not claim a general theorem of the form ``small symmetry defect \(\Rightarrow\) approximately constant diagonal'' without additional hypotheses; instead we treat diagonal-dispersion bounds as the audit-friendly capacity proxy.

source_wording_digest: Canonical tie-break repairs degeneracy. A Reflexive SBT interpretation is that packaging must include a canonicalization step (P5): when a cutoff eigenspace is degenerate, select a canonical m -dimensional subspace inside the degenerate block. In our experiments, a canonical tie-break that minimizes a symmetry-defect proxy produces a unique, reproducible choice and restores route stability: Scope of canonicalization. Our canonical tie-break is a deterministic rule that operates within an (approximately) degenerate eigenspace using symmetry-defect proxies (e.g.\ diagonal dispersion / shift-commutation surrogates). We do not claim that all packaging families admit such a canonicalizer, nor that canonicalization is unique; we present it as one explicit, auditable choice that removes degeneracy-driven non-uniqueness in the spectral setting.

expanded_source_wording_tex: Formal incompleteness explains why no sufficiently expressive effective theory captures all arithmetic truth, but it does not by itself provide a structural language for comparing theory growth. This paper develops such a language by treating a formal theory as a packaged closure object evaluated on a frozen ledger. First, a fixed idempotent package saturates under iteration: repeated closure does not sustain persistent strict growth. Hence genuine growth requires package change. Second, on a frozen slice with fixed yield, cost, and support data, efficiency transfers across cone-equivalent representatives, yielding a restricted alignment theorem. Third, these internal results combine with an explicit external dependency contract to give a conditional arithmetic lift: if the required canonical-family-on-cone assumptions are discharged from the arithmetic literature, then frontier-efficient extension operators admit canonical representatives on the relevant comparison cone. The result reframes incompleteness and axiom choice in package language. G\"odel becomes the canonical fixed-package failure mode, while new axioms appear as controlled package changes evaluated under a frozen regime. conclusion: We make no consistency claims, claim no new independence results, and treat every infinitary commitment as a named, priced hypothesis.
expanded_source_wording_tex:
The Zermelo--Fraenkel axioms are usually presented as a flat list, adopted because they
work. We show that the list \emph{factors}, theorem by theorem, through a single staged
construction discipline---packaging under a membership lens, audited by rank. We then read,
at discussion grade, G\"odel incompleteness and Cohen independence as the \emph{saturation} and
\emph{extension} faces of that discipline.

Over finite well-founded membership presentations, the Mostowski collapse is an idempotent
packaging map whose fixed points are canonically bijective with the hereditarily finite sets,
and the closure of the empty family under finite packaging is exactly $\mathrm{HF}$---a model of
$\mathsf{ZF}$ minus Infinity with each axiom witnessed by a named clause or the rank audit.
The four infinitary commitments enter only through an explicit assumption box of priced
hypotheses: Infinity as inductive-stage completion, Power set as full subpackage completion,
Replacement as unbounded descent transport, and Choice as canonical-lift existence. Separately,
rank-erasure is shown to be a \emph{lossless} flattening of the finite staged hierarchy. Under
that box, and named classical imports, the rank-erased shadow satisfies $\mathsf{ZF(C)}$
conditionally; countermodels guard each commitment's non-redundancy.

The centerpiece discharges an analogy the framework had only named: we characterize the
density defects of the finite Cohen poset exactly and show that the finite forcing lemma is
precisely their measure. Over an infinite index set these defects vanish, so Cohen
genericity is non-definability from the ground lens and the generic extension is a strict
theory extension. Read through the imported classical forcing facts, independence is the
visible footprint of lawful theory extension, with the continuum hypothesis appearing as lens
relativity.

Selected finite and structural cores are mechanized in Lean on a
$\{\textsf{propext}, \textsf{Quot.sound}\}$ axiom base with the Axiom of Choice absent
throughout; the finite lift used to price choice is verified without using choice. We make no
consistency claims, claim no new independence results, and treat every infinitary commitment as
a named, priced hypothesis. Read structurally, a set-theoretic foundation is an audited ledger:
what the chosen membership instrument supplies, what must be purchased, and why the open
questions are open.

source_wording_tex:
\paragraph{Countermodels and scope (\S\S\ref{sec:atlas}--\ref{sec:scope}).} Because the central
claims are easy to overstate, we accompany them with a small atlas of countermodels, each
blocking a specific overclaim (extensionality is not \emph{forced}; Foundation is not free
\emph{without} staging; Choice is not free infinitarily; and so on), and an explicit
non-claim register.

conclusion: We do not claim that ZFC is the unique or most natural promoted set layer—the continuum-hypothesis instance is precisely an argument that it is not.
expanded_source_wording_tex:
We state the perimeter once, here, and again in \S\ref{sec:scope}. We do \emph{not} derive
$\mathsf{ZF}$ or $\mathsf{ZFC}$ from finite principles; the infinitary content enters only
through the priced assumption box. We prove \emph{no} consistency statement, relative or
absolute, beyond what we explicitly import. We claim \emph{no} new independence result; the
forcing section reorganizes classical theorems, it does not reprove or extend them. We do
\emph{not} claim that $\mathsf{ZFC}$ is the unique or most natural promoted set layer---the
continuum-hypothesis instance is precisely an argument that it is not. And the reading of all
this as an answer to ``where does mathematics come from,'' developed in
\S\ref{sec:discussion}, is offered at the grade of discussion, after the theorems, never as
one of them.

conclusion: What we do not claim. We do not claim ZFC is the unique or most natural promoted set layer.
expanded_source_wording_tex:
\paragraph{What we do \emph{not} claim.}
\begin{enumerate}\itemsep0pt
  \item We do not derive $\mathsf{ZF}$ or $\mathsf{ZFC}$ from finite principles. The infinitary
  content enters only through the priced assumption box; the four commitments are named
  hypotheses, never conclusions.
  \item We prove no consistency statement, relative or absolute, beyond the classical results we
  explicitly import. Nothing here bears on the consistency of $\mathsf{ZFC}$.
  \item We claim no new independence result. The forcing section reorganizes classical theorems
  into the framework's vocabulary; it reproves and extends nothing. No model is constructed.
  \item We do not claim $\mathsf{ZFC}$ is the unique or most natural promoted set layer. The
  continuum-hypothesis instance (\S\ref{sec:ch}) is an argument to the contrary, and structural or
  alternative set theories remain available.
  \item We make no metaphysical claim about the existence of a set-theoretic universe. ``Set'' is
  used as a package; ``$\in$'' as a lens; the readings are structural.
  \item The interpretation of all this as an account of where mathematics comes from
  (\S\ref{sec:discussion}) is offered at the grade of discussion (\gradetag{meta}), after the theorems, and
  is never used as a premise for any of them.
\end{enumerate}

expanded_source_wording_tex: Many ``higher'' mathematical objects are introduced as definitions (limits, completions, analytic continuations), but it is often unclear when a large discrete protocol admits a stable continuous closure and how to test that stability without overclaiming. This question matters because premature or untested closure claims can propagate errors through dependent results. We instantiate the Six-Birds Theory ( ) framework of —which provides a general audit methodology for validating compressions of discrete data into continuous or idealized objects—as a closure-and-audit method for mathematics: a discrete substrate is staged by refinement, compressions are assessed by an explicit defect ledger, and a packaged object is accepted only when defects shrink or stabilize under refinement. Operationally, we (i) formalize two anchor statements in Lean/mathlib —the exact finite-difference Leibniz identity with its explicit remainder term and an algebraic uniqueness anchor for derivations on R[X] —and (ii) implement falsification-first Python diagnostics that compare competing closure routes under matched controls and an artifact contract (tables and macros are generated from snapshot-visible pointer JSONs). Across four exhibits we observe controlled, checkable separations. First, stability-only stencil filtering selects order- 0 closures, while adding a Leibniz-defect gate selects derivative-like order- 1 closures. Second, route mismatch (RM, measuring disagreement between closure paths) under a small coordinate change decays with refinement (power-law fit exponent p 1.46 ). Third, for prime-based closures in a convergence control regime (s)>1 , route mismatch RM_2 decreases with sample size N (e.g.\ RM_2(800) 5 10^ -2 ), whereas the same diagnostic in the critical strip exhibits mismatch growth by many orders of magnitude under naive staging (e.g.\ RM_2(800) 5 10^ 12 ). Fourth, in a self-dual toy family, tightening a positivity constraint sharply confines zeros to the symmetry locus (mean radial deviation drops from 0.87 to 3 10^ -4 ). These results provide a reproducible methodology to separate feasible closures from protocol artifacts and to compare closure proposals across regimes. We emphasize that this paper does not establish new theorems about or zero distributions; we report audit-style diagnostics under explicit controls and document the upgrade points required for stronger claims.

source_wording_digest: Exhibit A-1 (calculus closure). We isolate the exact discrete Leibniz identity for finite differences (with its explicit remainder term) and use it as an accounting ledger: demanding that the remainder vanish in a packaged limit forces the derivation (product rule) structure. We also record an algebraic uniqueness anchor for derivations on polynomial rings in Lean/mathlib . Exhibit A-2 (protocol holonomy). We quantify route mismatch between two natural refinement protocols under a small coordinate change, treating the mismatch as a P3\ holonomy-style defect that decays with refinement. Exhibit B-1 (prime closure diagnostics). We compare staged additive and multiplicative closures (Dirichlet truncations versus Euler-product truncations) under prototype packaging maps, and we separate a convergence control regime from the critical strip where naive staging is unstable. Exhibit B-2 (passivity toy). We show, in a self-dual toy family with a positivity constraint, that tightening feasibility can confine zeros to a symmetry locus—a pattern that motivates (but does not prove) ``passivity ledger'' interpretations of zero confinement.

This toy is not a theorem and does not claim to reproduce the full hypotheses of classical zero-confinement results.
Its role is methodological: it demonstrates a recognizable \textsc{SBT} pattern in a controlled setting.
This motif has rigorous instances, most famously the Lee--Yang circle theorem for ferromagnetic Ising models \cite{LeeYang1952}; we do not invoke that theorem here.

expanded_source_wording_tex: We present a reproducible computational framework---with Lean~4 mechanized proofs and deterministic Python simulations---that treats multi-scale model reduction as a closure-audit calculus: each ``physics theory'' is a packaging operator built from a lens (retained macro information), a completion (canonical reconstruction), and diagnostics that certify when the reduced description is self-consistent. We instantiate the Six-Birds lens/completion/closure dictionary as a multi-scale layer template, centering three cross-domain certificates: closure coherence (idempotence), audit monotonicity (data-processing inequality), and route mismatch (noncommutation of coarse-graining with dynamics). We operationalize this calculus via a reproducible workflow (Python artifacts + Lean-certified lemmas) and demonstrate it on four instantiations: quantum dephasing, discrete BGK-like kinetic closure, filtered Burgers (LES), and nonlinear averaging (backreaction). Under null conditions (no coarse-graining, zero heterogeneity, or exact projections), idempotence defects and route mismatches are $\approx 0$; under controlled interventions they separate cleanly. Dephasing is exactly idempotent; sampled CPTP channels satisfy quantum relative-entropy DPI with no violations beyond tolerance; unitary evolution produces nonzero mismatch that grows with dephasing strength. In the BGK model, packaging coherence improves as collision strength increases, with explicit failure modes when the equilibrium family or retained moments are misspecified. In LES and averaging models, mismatch grows with filter width or heterogeneity and yields canonical subgrid/backreaction correction terms. This reframes ``physics theories'' as comparable closure layers and localizes which effective terms are forced by a chosen scale and audit. We do not derive continuum theories or prove analytic bounds; we report Lean-certified algebraic facts and numerical certificates under stated controls.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
Many of the objects mathematics uses to solve problems do not live in the
layer where the problem is posed.  Imaginary numbers are not real,
infinitesimals are not real scalars, roots of irreducible polynomials need
not lie in the base field, and cohomology classes are not vertex potentials.
We study this pattern by separating a \emph{lower layer}, where a problem and
its accepted answers are stated, from a \emph{promoted layer}, where
additional objects may be available.  We define theory layers, promotion
bridges, audited descending expressions, and the Strict Audited Utility (SAU)
certificate, and we show that the certificate is extracted from strict useful
traces rather than stipulated.

The main results are an essential boundary necessity theorem, which forces
hidden non-descent together with an audited lower-layer boundary expression;
a boundary normal form; a partial converse closing the circle from trace to
validated certificate to accepted lower-layer answer; a soundness theorem
specifying what an accepted certificate licenses; a classification of
primitive boundary heads; four canonical witnesses---imaginary numbers, dual
numbers, Galois roots, and graph cohomology---each instantiating a distinct
minimal or universal profile; and a transfer theorem showing that a validated
profile is portable under matching audit hypotheses while not identifying
objects across domains.  Together these results show that, in finite typed
audited promoted-use traces, strict mathematical usefulness forces hidden
non-descent paired with audited boundary descent.

The scope is intentionally narrow.  The paper concerns strict useful
promoted-use traces, not mathematical practice in general; it does not assert
that every promoted extension is useful, that hidden promoted objects are
lower-layer content, or novelty for the classical constructions themselves.
A companion Lean development supplies substantive proofs for selected direct,
computational, and definitional fragments and records the remaining theorems
as proof-carrying traceability records.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
The scope is bounded.  We address strict useful promoted-use traces, not
mathematics in general; not every promoted extension is useful, and the four
canonical witnesses are not an exhaustive classification of useful structures.
We do not claim novelty for the classical constructions themselves, and hidden
promoted objects are not asserted as lower-layer content.  The companion Lean
development plays a bounded role: it
supplies substantive proofs for selected direct, computational, and
definitional fragments and records the remaining theorems as proof-carrying
traceability records.  Source, Lean code, and reproducibility artifacts are
hosted at \url{https://github.com/ioannist/six-birds-math-usefulness}; see
\Cref{app:formalization} for the discipline that governs which results carry
substantive Lean proofs.  Foundations I--III provide inherited provenance but

expanded_source_wording_tex:
What makes a mathematical object useful when it does not live in the layer
where the problem is posed?  Imaginary numbers are not real, infinitesimals are
not real scalars, roots of irreducible polynomials need not lie in the base
field, and cohomology classes are not vertex potentials.  This paper studies
that pattern by separating a lower layer, where a problem and its accepted
answers are stated, from a promoted layer, where additional objects may be
available.  We define theory layers, promotion bridges, audited descending
expressions, and the Strict Audited Utility (SAU) certificate, and then show
that SAU is extracted from strict useful traces rather than stipulated.

The main results are a theorem stack: Essential Boundary Necessity (Theorem
A), which forces hidden promoted support and an audited lower boundary; SAU
Boundary Normal Form (Theorem B); a Partial Converse and Tautology Barrier
(Theorem C); SAU Soundness (Theorem D); Basic Profile Classification (Theorem
E); four canonical witnesses from imaginary numbers, dual numbers and first
jets, Galois roots, and graph cohomology; Minimality and universal promotion
(Theorem F); and a Profile Transfer theorem (Theorem G).  Together they show
that, in finite typed audited promoted-use traces, strict mathematical
usefulness forces hidden non-descent plus audited boundary descent.  The claim
is deliberately scoped: the paper does not claim that all mathematics is
useful, does not literalize hidden objects downstairs, and does not claim that
the Lean development independently proves every paper theorem.  The Lean
material is a traceability harness, with substantive proof language reserved
for direct, computational, and definitional proof rows.

The transfer plan gives a validated source instance and a target instance in the
same profile skeleton.  Validation of the target plan is the additional
condition \(\mathbf F_{\mathsf{SAU}}(\mathfrak C_t)=\varnothing\), so the target has its
own saturation, strictness, non-descent, descent, solving, audit, and nonclaim
witnesses.  Applying the soundness theorem of \Cref{sec:soundness-failure} to
the target package licenses \(\operatorname{Useful}(B_t,P_t):\texttt{accepted}\).  The source
validation explains why the profile was a legitimate guide, but it does not
identify the source and target objects.  This theorem is tracked by the
formalization harness as a projection over the transfer-plan and validated-target
records.
\end{proof}

conclusion: Enumerating nearly twelve thousand chiral gauge structures token-blind, the closure chain forces a thin skeleton: the Standard Model's gauge algebra (conditional on one separation condition), ^2 _W = 3/8 at the embedding point, exact proton stability.
expanded_source_wording_tex: \textbf{The thin forced skeleton.} Necessity and contingency, in physics, stop being moods and become computed columns. Enumerating nearly twelve thousand chiral gauge structures token-blind, the closure chain forces a thin skeleton: the Standard Model's gauge algebra (conditional on one separation condition), $\sin^2\theta_W = 3/8$ at the embedding point, exact proton stability. And it proves other quantities invisible to in-layer law: the generation count, the electroweak scale, the value of the cosmological constant. ``The Standard Model, on this evidence, is not one derivable object. It is a \emph{selection} with a thin forced skeleton --- and the calculus proves both the skeleton and the thinness.'' The laws of nature, like the axioms of set theory \citep{zfc}, factor into a free column and a purchased column. That physics and mathematics have the same receipt structure is the one-grammar thesis in its most compact form.

It is a \emph{selection} with a thin forced skeleton --- and the calculus proves both the skeleton and the thinness.'' The laws of nature, like the axioms of set theory \citep{zfc}, factor into a free column and a purchased column. That physics and mathematics have the same receipt structure is the one-grammar thesis in its most compact form.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
When does prediction become trivial?  This paper gives a typed
structural answer: within the \textsc{csl} scope, predictive content
collapses when an upstream determining state is exposed to current
observation.  The
load-bearing variable is the visibility coupling predicate
\(\operatorname{Exposure}(L,\sigma)\), which asks whether some polynomial-time
current observable factors through the autonomous lift's internal state
by a function non-constant on the realized carrier.  We state a typed
Candidate Structural Law (\(\textsc{csl}\)) over the predictive-quotient holonomy carrier on
autonomous-lifted polynomial-time substrates.  The law has four clauses:
dissolution under exposure, preservation under non-exposure, a
degenerate clause when there is no predictive witness content, and
strength-independence of the coupling function.  The \textsc{csl} is stated
at \emph{diagnosis grade}.  We also give a granularity-mismatch theorem at
\emph{R-Diagnosis}: the framework's current and predictive quotients are
strictly finer than the standard classes \(P\) and \(NP\) at the
history level, but this strictness can be lost under standard
language-level projection.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
Given two probe families on the same finite-dimensional carrier, this
paper asks what a dissolving family \(D\) measures beyond what a native
family \(L\) can explain under an audit energy \(C\).  Under the
standing legal-energy quotient and null-mode legality hypotheses, the
adequacy residual \(\Xi_C(D\mid L)\) is the Schur-complement leftover
built from the block currencies \(K_{LL}\), \(K_{DD}\), \(K_{DL}\), and
\(K_{LD}\).  We develop this residual as a calculus: the projection
identity identifies it with \(T_D(I-P_L)T_D^*\) in energy-scaled
coordinates; optimality and exact adequacy characterize Loewner
minimality and zero residual; promotion combines native and residual
budgets into a dissolving budget; and chain-rule, data-processing, and
transfer laws describe native extension, post-processing, coarsening,
and exact or defective bridges.  The blind-spot witness theorem turns
failure of a declared residual budget into an explicit recombination
vector with positive excess.  The paper does not claim exact adequacy
generically, does not classify all probe-family pairs, and does not
claim novelty for the classical operator-theoretic constructions it
packages.  A layer-dissolving use of the calculus is given in
\citet{Tsiokos2026NeedleKiller}.

The scope is deliberately narrow.  The paper does not claim that every raw
substrate sees every dissolving probe, nor that the residual vanishes
generically; exact adequacy is a hypothesis to be verified, not a default
state.  It also does not transfer a residual computed from a coarse view to an
intrinsic fine view without an audited bridge: such transfer requires the exact
or defective bridge machinery developed later.  A residual bound at one
accepted finite stage is not treated as predictive adequacy across an indexed
family.  Finally, the paper does not claim novelty for the classical
constructions it uses, such as Schur complements, Moore--Penrose
pseudoinverses, projection identities, and Douglas-style factorization.  The
contribution is one audited residual package: projection, optimality,
exactness, extension, data processing, transfer, and blind-spot witness laws
for the same Schur-complement object.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
Many obstruction arguments exhibit a localized failure mode that appears
irreducible at the layer where it is first visible; this paper studies
one audited route by which such needle obstructions cease to be
obstructions, namely passage to a higher layer where additional
admissible dissolving probes are available.  The framework is the
formed-layer membrane setting: zero-energy directions are removed by a
legal quotient, native probes are assigned a quadratic native currency,
unexplained dissolving currency is measured by an adequacy residual, and
predictive membranes, dissolving transport records, and the all-six
taxonomy control the transfer.  The layer-dissolving endpoint theorem
shows that, under predictive native bounds, residual bounds, and
transport hypotheses, the dissolving currency is bounded uniformly
across accepted stages, so no layer-dissolving predictive needles exist
within the declared scope.  The complementary duality-confinement
membrane theorem shows that, under a separating anti-invariant readout
and a vanishing-trace sequence of domination records, visible object
mass is confined to the fixed locus of the involution.  These are
framework-bound dissolution results, not a universal
singularity-elimination theorem or a claim about any named external
problem.  The adequacy-residual calculus on which the layer-dissolving
endpoint depends is developed in \citet{Tsiokos2026XiCompanion}.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
The framework allows only certain repairs to such a failure.  A repair
is lawful if it excludes the offending recombination by a declared
nonclaim, weakens the claim by raising the relevant budget, strengthens
or rewrites the carrier and audit so that the legal quotient has
changed, adds native probes that see the residual direction, or
completes the missing protocol or transport family and then retests the
same block.  These options are deliberately narrow: they change either
the scope of the claim, the budget being asserted, the legal carrier on
which the currency is computed, the probe family available to explain
the residual, or the transfer record that transports the budget.  By
contrast, same-package repetition saturates.  Repeating the same
Schur-block repair with no new probe content, no new audit, and no new
transport data does not change the residual and therefore cannot remove
the critical pair.

conclusion: Positive semidefinite quadratic forms, Loewner order, Moore–Penrose pseudoinverses, Schur complements, and Douglas factorization enter in standard ways, and the paper does not claim novelty for those constructions.
expanded_source_wording_tex:
The local mathematics used by the framework is classical.  Positive
semidefinite quadratic forms, Loewner order, Moore--Penrose
pseudoinverses, Schur complements, and Douglas factorization enter in
standard ways, and the paper does not claim novelty for those
constructions.  The contribution is the synchronization of these
constructions across a passage between layers.  The quotient used by
the probes must be the quotient used by the budget; the native currency
must be the currency spent by the predictive membrane; the adequacy
residual must be the part of the dissolving currency that native probes
do not explain; and the endpoint theorem must spend exactly those
currencies.  This is the framework-as-discipline claim: the same
operator tools become a dissolution theorem only when their roles are
kept aligned.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
The scope fence is correspondingly explicit.  The paper does not claim
that emergence dissolves every mathematical singularity or obstruction,
does not give a complete classification of needles or repairs, and does
not depend on any particular application instance.  It also does not

uses.  The result is a framework theorem: needle-class obstructions
satisfying the stated predictive, adequacy, endpoint,
duality-confinement, and all-six records can be dissolved in the

machinery at specific external problems, but each such use would need
its own framework-specific records, scope fence, and formalization
disclosure.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
Scoped event admissibility on fixed support leaves a specific gap for strict
tests: the protocol-indexed flagship-seed bridge family realizes the
quadratic-levelset and transition-stability slots, but the
protocol-indexed readout-agreement slot remains unrealized, so no accepted
strict test family is available at the bridge-native event level.  This paper
asks whether strict-test acceptance is admissible on fixed support without
repairing that bridge level.  The method is a layer-local, audit-based PICA
route: promotion, internalization of protocol coordinates, carrier
exactification, and audited source admission produce a H6 carrier
substrate above the bridge-native H2 level.  On the resulting
H6 carriers, the readout-agreement, quadratic-witness, and
transition-witness slots are strict-realized natively; the three-slot strict
domain closes; and three accepted scoped strict test families
survive the required control panel.  The panel covers null-baseline,
memory-only, artifact, boundary, selected-lift, visibility, and claim-boundary
checks.  The bridge-native H2 level is
retained as the real-provisional non-factorization boundary: descent from new-layer evidence to
old-layer compatibility preserves non-factorization without inducing
old-layer strict realization.  The final classification is a strict theory
extension at the new layer with old-layer real-provisional compatibility
intact.  The result is bounded: it does not assert event-package construction,
shared-event identity, proto-effect or effect-algebra structure, Born
valuation, composition readiness, faithful public compression, a lawful public
carrier, or canonical selected lifts.

criteria pass and the controls survive.  It does not provide a packaging

conclusion: Paper 9's strict-extension verdict respects this discipline: it does not claim that a particular lift is uniquely admissible, and the selected-lift variation control of certifies that the accepted families survive admissible variation.
expanded_source_wording_tex:
The selected-lift discipline of \cite{Tsiokos2026FoundationsII} allows level
crossings to record selected lifts without making any one lift canonical.
Paper~9's strict-extension verdict respects this discipline: it does not
claim that a particular lift is uniquely admissible, and the selected-lift
variation control of \Cref{subsec:selected-lift-visibility-controls} certifies
that the accepted families survive admissible variation.  A canonical selected
lift would assert that one section across the layer transition is privileged;
such a claim would conflict with the descent-and-no-section structure of
\Cref{subsec:non-factorization-baseline,subsec:non-factorization-preservation}.
Non-factorization and selected-lift nonuniqueness are therefore complementary:
the H6 carrier admits no inverse reconstruction, and no particular
lift across the transition is canonical.  The acceptance result lives within
both constraints.  These constraints shape the discussion of
\Cref{sec:discussion}.

source_wording_tex:
The selected-lift discipline of \cite{Tsiokos2026FoundationsII} allows level
crossings to record selected lifts without making any one lift canonical.
\PaperNine{}'s strict-extension verdict respects this discipline: it does not
claim that a particular lift is uniquely admissible, and the selected-lift
variation control of \Cref{subsec:selected-lift-visibility-controls} certifies
that the accepted families survive admissible variation.  A canonical selected
lift would assert that one section across the layer transition is privileged;
such a claim would conflict with the descent-and-no-section structure of
\Cref{subsec:non-factorization-baseline,subsec:non-factorization-preservation}.
Non-factorization and selected-lift nonuniqueness are therefore complementary:
the \NewLayer{} carrier admits no inverse reconstruction, and no particular
lift across the transition is canonical.  The acceptance result lives within
both constraints.  These constraints shape the discussion of
\Cref{sec:discussion}.

conclusion: The main limitations are structural. The accepted strict test families do not constitute an event package, a proto-effect fragment, an effect algebra, a Born valuation, or a composition-ready structure. Those remain explicit nonclaims, for the reasons given in : each would require additional construction beyond strict-test acceptance. They are future-work targets rather than negative results. Public-shadow nonfaithfulness and selected-lift nonuniqueness also remain part of the result's scope. They are not incidental caveats; they are structural conditions that keep the strict extension from collapsing into a public-shadow or canonical-lift reconstruction, as discussed in . Finally, Paper 9 is scoped to the flagship-only protocol-indexed setting. Global, cross-seed, and full-core test claims are out of scope here. Whether the carrier exactification framework of can be extended to broader support is a methodological question for a successor paper.

the carrier exactification framework of \cite{Tsiokos2026CarrierExactification}
can be extended to broader support is a methodological question for a successor
paper.

expanded_source_wording_tex: Earlier fixed-support papers in Six Birds Theory introduced admissible event packages, predictive quotients, and recombination witnesses. They left open whether a recombination-positive witness family supports a genuine promoted package or only a lower-layer summary. We answer that question on a frozen Route~A corpus. We define a promotion criterion requiring sufficiency on the designated observable surface, induced update closure, admissible second-stage stability, control admissibility, protocol honesty, and slice legibility. The corpus is exact-finite and controlled: a two-anchor flagship core, four nearby positives, and matched null, memory-only, artifact, and boundary-sensitive controls, together with a support-only erasure comparison surface. We replace an earlier vacuous second-stage rule with an admissible surface-coarsening audit and treat the artifact control in paired protocol-aware form. On this pipeline, an intrinsic candidate package survives on both flagship anchors, covers the four nearby positives, preserves the required control contrasts, and remains honest under the paired artifact audit. Two representative-selected route families also survive on the flagship core, but only as secondary evidence: they do not support a unique best strategy and they do not displace the intrinsic survivor. Slice/dual analyses are support-only and the staging--packaging defect atlas is explanatory. A Lean criterion kernel formalizes the promotion vocabulary and the generic implication from the criterion fields to promoted-package status. The resulting claim is narrow: at least one promoted-package candidate survives honestly on fixed support in the Route~A flagship family.

conclusion: The intrinsic route P_ int is the main result because it survives on both flagship anchors, covers the four nearby positives, separates the required controls, and remains honest under the paired artifact audit without requiring representative-selected correction. The representative-selected routes refine that picture rather than replacing it. They show that the surviving-package surface on the flagship core is richer than a single route, but their support remains route-family-level: they do not justify a unique best strategy claim, and they do not displace the intrinsic route. If P_ int had failed and only a representative-selected route had survived, the natural reading would have shifted toward a lift-selected or protocol-indexed package. That is not the current evidential state. Interpreted modestly, this intrinsic-versus-representative asymmetry is closer to familiar contrasts between intrinsic state abstraction, predictive state, and selected refinement than to a claim that one universal abstraction recipe has been proved . The support layers are easier to interpret when kept in their proper place. The slice/dual analysis shows that the surviving-route picture is not exhausted by a single scalar tradeoff ordering: different slices can favor different material route families. This is informative but remains support-only and provisional. The staging–packaging defect atlas contributes explanatory route geometry; it is not a classifier and not even positively ordered in the simplest positive-versus-control way. It sharpens interpretation without entering the claim-bearing pipeline.

It packages the assumptions a flagship-style survivor route would need in order to instantiate the criterion kernel, and so functions as an interface between the abstract criterion language and the route-family evidence used in the main text. expanded_source_wording_tex:
\paragraph{Contribution and scope.}
The substrate contributed by this paper is a \emph{carrier-to-event admissibility layer} on fixed support: a record-level discipline in which every candidate event carries an explicit instrument, a selected lift, visibility and suppression data, a threshold record, an exact-six role profile, and an audit trail, and in which tests and higher structure are built only from accepted records of this kind. expanded_source_wording_tex: Every candidate is then converted into an event bridge record of the form introduced in Section~\ref{sec:bridge-records}. The resulting artifact contains seventeen bridge records, one per candidate, each recording a carrier-side condition, a public/readout-side condition, an instrument, one or more selected lifts or forgetting maps, a visibility and suppression record, a threshold record, a reference to an exact-six skeleton, and an audit record. Each bridge record also annotates the candidate's weaknesses. Public-shadow candidates carry carrier-pullback or fiber-record requirements; they do not assert that public signatures determine refined carrier conditions. Quadratic candidates carry nonclaims against probability and against a global quadratic geometry. Completion candidates carry selected-lift and section-dependence notes. The absent readout-agreement baseline is represented as a negative bridge record rather than silently dropped. The bridge stage therefore establishes representational completeness for later testing, not event acceptance: a complete bridge record is necessary for event acceptance but not sufficient, and the event gate must still check the declared surface, instrument visibility, suppression honesty, selected-lift stability, protocol honesty, threshold activation, controls, layer assignment, exact-six completeness, and claim-boundary compliance.

expanded_source_wording_tex: The no-shortcut discipline is the methodological guardrail behind the constructive non-definability findings of Paper~10.  It says that an incomplete construction may not be silently upgraded to a stronger result, that a preserved nonclaim may not be turned into an inherited positive, and that a formal proof gap may not stand in as an axiom.  This discipline matters because the paper deliberately records several strong absences: no event-package construction, no H2 strict-test closure, no H6 reconstruction from H2, and no event-level threshold criterion.  Those absences are part of the result, not temporary wording gaps.  The anti-claim flags are the Lean-level companion to this methodological rule; \Cref{sec:formal-framework} and \Cref{app:formalization} record their formal setting.

expanded_source_wording_tex: The intrinsic identity lane is rejected first.  That lane would have treated the role's carrier-native strict-test content as intrinsically the same across the three H6 PICA carriers, using the inherited role labels from Paper~9 as if they supplied identity by themselves \citep{Tsiokos2026StrictTests}.  The discipline it fails is scoped comparison: a cross-carrier comparison must carry the protocol-indexed route by which the two carrier contexts are compared, rather than collapsing role-labeled strict-test data into an unqualified sameness claim.  The candidate triangles therefore remain role-matched probes until a lane supplies that route.  If the intrinsic lane were permitted as a fallback, the paper would erase the distinction between same-role candidacy and accepted protocol-indexed comparison, and the result would drift toward shared-event identity in the strong sense, which Paper~10 does not claim.

expanded_source_wording_tex: The role-specific descent contract at the H2 boundary treats the readout-agreement role differently from the two witness roles.  The readout-agreement role descends as a pair-observable boundary record at H2.  This means that the role leaves a boundary observation compatible with the preserved real-provisional non-factorization boundary, but only as a non-strict observation.  The observation is pair-level: it records boundary-compatible readout agreement without asserting that the old layer carries the full strict slot.  It does not promote the old-layer readout slot to a strict realization. Paper-10-new claims are layer-local at H6 PICA; the event-package candidate, proto-effect fragment, effect algebra, Born valuation, and composition readiness all remain future work; the per-role bridge-level law basis is named but not constructed; and the strict-test starting point is inherited rather than re-established. The paper does not claim shared-event identity in the strong sense, does not certify a global cross-carrier comparison base, and does not alter the H2 boundary inherited from Paper 9.
source_wording_tex: The scope of \PaperTen{} is the strict-test-to-event-package admissibility question on fixed \NewLayer{} \PICA{} support, beginning from the accepted strict-test substrate inherited from \PaperNine{}.  Paper-10-new claims are layer-local at H6 PICA; the event-package candidate, proto-effect fragment, effect algebra, Born valuation, and composition readiness all remain future work; the \BridgeLevelLawBasis{} is named but not constructed; and the strict-test starting point is inherited rather than re-established.  The paper does not claim shared-event identity in the strong sense, does not certify a global cross-carrier comparison base, and does not alter the \OldLayer{} boundary inherited from \PaperNine{}.

conclusion: Seven inherited nonclaims from Paper 7 and Paper 9 are preserved: faithful public compression, lawful public carrier, canonical selected lift, old-layer strict-test closure, old-layer readout strict realization, H6 reconstruction from H2, and global, cross-seed, or full-core tests. Paper-10-new identity-scope nonclaims are added: intrinsic identity lane, lawful-same-branch identity lane, and lift-only identity lane are rejected as fallback identity lanes; shared-event identity in the strong sense is not claimed; and no admissible cross-carrier comparison base is certified. The downstream package, proto-effect, effect-algebra, Born, and composition structures remain outside the positive claims. Appendix E records the complete ledger.

expanded_source_wording_tex: The common proof shape behind the 14 schemas of \Cref{subsec:lean-theorem-schemas} is conditional.  A schema introduces typed inputs, usually a record together with hypotheses about that record, and proves only the implication licensed by those inputs in Lean type theory.  The proof does not import an empirical witness as a theorem and does not assert that a paper-10 artifact satisfies the antecedent.  For example, when a schema takes an accepted event-level predicate as an input, the proof may project the threshold, control, and boundary components required by that predicate; it does not establish that an accepted event-level record exists.  The implication direction is part of the discipline: Lean may consume a typed hypothesis, but it does not manufacture that hypothesis from the artifact ledger.  The antecedent is always typed structural data, not an empirical conclusion smuggled into the kernel.

expanded_source_wording_tex: We study recombination-sensitive branch structure on a fixed-support substrate in Six Birds Theory. Building on prior work on event packaging and predictive holonomy, we introduce branch assemblages and two quotient levels at an interface: a branchwise predictive quotient ($K_i$), which captures independent predictive treatment of the branches, and a recombination quotient ($R_i$), which captures admissible recombination observables on branch families. On this architecture we exhibit a benchmark suite separating classical mixture, hidden predictive memory without recombination sensitivity, route-marked suppression, erasure-conditioned recovery, cyclic-family generalization, dissipative washout, and artifact controls based on protocol internalization and flattening/completion. A supporting theorem layer proves the abstract factorized no-interference regime and its obstruction by strict refinement, and one promoted positive family is connected to a theorem-backed concrete witness in an aligned Lean model. We do not claim a general reconstruction of non-Hilbert interference or a formalization of the full benchmark runtime. The claim is narrower: these recombination phenomena arise on fixed support, can be audited exactly, and admit a partial formal backbone on the Six Birds substrate.

conclusion: The paper establishes a substrate-level result. On a fixed-support Six Birds architecture, branchwise predictive structure and recombination-sensitive structure can be separated operationally, and that separation can be audited under exact finite controls. The benchmark suite shows that the same substrate supports a classical-mixture null regime, hidden predictive memory without additional recombination sensitivity, readable-route suppression, erased conditional recovery, bounded cyclic-family generalization, dissipative washout, and artifact controls based on protocol internalization and flattening/completion. The formal contribution is narrower. The Lean development proves an abstract refinement layer under detectability, a factorized no-interference regime in which the recombination quotient collapses to the branchwise quotient, and the corresponding obstruction result that strict refinement rules out global branchwise factorization. It also proves one theorem-backed concrete positive instance for an aligned Lean model of the promoted family n5_d1_w1of4_3of4 . These results support the interpretation of the benchmark suite but do not replace it.

scalar. Since $\pi_k \propto 1/w_k$ depends only on weight \emph{ratios}, that scalar cancels

choice was made deliberately to keep every computation exactly rational; the invariance is its
elementary, proven consequence. It is filed here as a design caveat because it has a concrete

unobservable.

\claimref{GB1}{4173705a52c358bc74b51815929cb2a28c8f680b3421dafdb7633e97b051fa8e}
The published protocol-trap theorem (F-I T-AOT-02) requires all phase kernels reversible w.r.t.\ a
\emph{common} stationary measure; Kovacs kernels $K_\epsilon$ are reversible w.r.t.\ different
Gibbs measures per $\epsilon$, so the theorem does not apply as published. GB1 --- the
temperature-protocol version, in the style of the protocol-trap microarticle
\sbtcite{sbt-protocol-trap} --- ships as a recognition-grade math demo: a pseudo-EPR identity
plus a finite exact numerical check, with the closed general theorem filed as an explicitly open
obligation in the artifact payload. GT4's triage therefore carries the GB1 caveat as a standing
theorem-wrapper limitation: the triage computation itself is deterministic and exact, but the
protocol-trap \emph{discipline} it applies rests partly on a demo, not a closed theorem. This is
F-II conditional reporting working as designed.

conclusion: The knockout panel makes each primitive's causal activity checkable, in two distinct modes that the artifact's own nonclaim keeps separate.
expanded_source_wording_tex:
The knockout panel makes each primitive's causal activity checkable, in two distinct modes that
the artifact's own nonclaim keeps separate. For P1--P3 the knockouts are \emph{numeric}: disabling
the primitive (identity run kernels; the unconstrained-lumpable replacement; constant-$\epsilon$
replacement) degrades a declared numeric diagnostic past its declared threshold. For P4--P6 the
knockouts are \emph{capability-loss} rows: removing the primitive makes the relevant downstream
diagnostic unavailable or undefined rather than numerically degraded --- there is no numeric
threshold to cross, and none is claimed.

expanded_source_wording_tex: At the level of adjacent literatures, the predictive quotient is closest to future-oriented state constructions such as causal states, observable operator models, and predictive state representations \citep{ShaliziCrutchfield2001ComputationalMechanics,Jaeger2000ObservableOperatorModels,LittmanSuttonSingh2002PredictiveRepresentationsState}. The current/future comparison layer added here is closer in spirit to a comparison between observational and behavioral equivalence, and thus also sits near bisimulation traditions in concurrency and probabilistic processes \citep{Park1981ConcurrencyAutomata,Milner1989CommunicationConcurrency,LarsenSkou1991BisimulationThroughProbabilisticTesting}. The paper does not claim to subsume those frameworks. Its claim is narrower: on fixed support, one can compare what is visible now with what matters later, and one can separate flat, artifactual, removable, currentizable, dissipative, and loop-asymmetric cases within one operational language.

expanded_source_wording_tex: Protocol-driven dynamics often conflate \emph{route dependence} (noncommutativity/holonomy of update steps) with an \emph{arrow of time}, making time-asymmetry audits vulnerable to scheduling artifacts. We introduce an autonomous lifted-protocol formulation and a path-reversal audit decomposition, operationalize it via a fully explicit finite-state benchmark, and demonstrate a clean null-versus-driven separation between holonomy and directionality. Concretely, we define two reversible Markov kernels \(K_0,K_1\) on three states and compare (i) an \emph{externally scheduled} stroboscopic composition on \(X\) with (ii) an \emph{autonomous} time-homogeneous lift on \(Z=X\times\Phi\) driven by a clock. Under external scheduling, each step is reversible but the stroboscopic update has strictly positive entropy production \(\mathrm{EPR}\ensuremath{\approx 0.083}\), with a noncommutativity witness \(\|K_0K_1-K_1K_0\|_\infty=0.1296\). Under the autonomous lift with a reversible (unbiased) clock (null control), the lifted chain is reversible and the arrow audit collapses to \(\mathrm{EPR}\ensuremath{\,{<}\,10^{-17}}\) (equivalently, path-reversal asymmetry vanishes). Turning on clock bias (drive) yields a positive arrow and the measured \(\mathrm{EPR}_{\mathrm{lifted}}\) matches \(\alpha\,\mathrm{EPR}_{\mathrm{clock}}\) across a bias sweep (Figure~\ref{fig:epr_vs_bias}). This separation reduces false positives when interpreting protocol effects as directionality and provides a reproducible audit template for switching Markov models and algorithmic protocols. We do not claim a general characterization of all nonequilibrium protocols; the conclusions are for finite-state discrete-time kernels and the random-scan autonomous lift studied here.

conclusion: The theorem is conditional on the admissibility and Boolean-stability of the shared-event relation on the relevant fixed comparison object.
expanded_source_wording_tex:
\paragraph{Proof sketch of \Cref{thm:shared-event-quotient}.}
The theorem is conditional on the admissibility and Boolean-stability of the shared-event relation on the relevant fixed comparison object. Under that assumption, if \(E_1\sim F_1\) and \(E_2\sim F_2\), then admissible probes and downstream identifications cannot distinguish the left and right unions either, so \(E_1\cup E_2\sim F_1\cup F_2\). Likewise, if \(E\sim F\), then admissible Boolean complementation on the local event algebras preserves the identification. The quotient is therefore stable under the local Boolean operations that the theorem uses. \qed

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\noindent
We ask not merely whether layer birth occurs, but how many primitive kinds of birth are experimentally accessible. Within the Six-Birds framework, birth events can be organized by activation of packaging ($P5$), directed circulation ($P6_{\mathrm{drive}}$), and staging anomaly ($P4$). We show that these primitives support a small canonical taxonomy of four layer-birth classes and that the corresponding classes can be operationally instantiated and separated in a common measured observable space. Class-I activates packaging without drive; Class-II activates packaging together with directed circulation; Class-III activates packaging together with a staging anomaly but without drive; and Class-IV activates all three. The strongest empirical separation is between Class-I and Class-II, where affinity at structural birth robustly discriminates drive-free from driven births and explicit no-fake-arrow controls rule out coarse-graining artifacts. We then place all four classes on a shared observable map using structural boundary location, affinity at boundary, and a strict-rule-aligned staging proxy. Capacity/depth behaves as a post-birth field rather than a primary classifier, and at least one upstream/PICA-style system can be embedded in the same coordinate system. We do not claim stabilized universality exponents. Instead, we provide a primitive taxonomy and observable separation of layer-birth classes that future universality work must respect.

expanded_source_wording_tex: We study a class of continuous Cantor substrates generated by six interacting mechanisms---operator rewrite, admissibility gating, protocol/timescale adaptation, lens selection, packaging/completion, and budget dynamics---and isolate an audited shell on which the resulting full-loop dynamics are lawful. On this shell we define a base cocycle-pressure theory~$T_0$ and a completion-based extension~$T_1$ built from an evolve--forget--reinstantiate packaging endomap. We prove four theoremlets on this shell-stable class: (i)~a continuous full-loop lawfulness theoremlet, (ii)~closure of a selector-weighted cocycle pressure object, (iii)~a strict theory-extension theoremlet showing that~$T_1$ is not definable from~$T_0$, via saturation, material $P4 \leftarrow P5$ forcing, and macro-admissibility obstruction, and (iv)~a thermodynamic consequence theoremlet in the form of a nontrivial conditional pressure disintegration over packaging fibers. The contribution is therefore a theorem of theory depth rather than broader family coverage: the packaged object carries object structure not present in the cocycle object even on a fixed shell-stable class. We make no broader-class, shell-general, or non-SFT breadth claim beyond this audited shell, but the resulting hybrid Cantor object yields a closed and thermodynamically meaningful audited-shell theorem package.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
Work on multi-scale organization and audit-based directionality lacks a minimal-substrate theorem: key primitives are often realized only by smuggling in external schedules, ad hoc audits, or declared quotients, making results hard to verify and compare across substrates.
We introduce a no-smuggling minimal-substrate semantics for SPT, operationalize it via matched-control audit tests on finite stochastic machines, and demonstrate separations between protocol artifacts, intrinsic drive, and route-dependent packaging defects.
Operationally, we define a canonical machine class $\mathcal S_{\min}$ of autonomous finite stochastic dynamics with phase-in-state, deterministic lenses, induced packaging endomaps $E_{\tau,f}$, and intrinsic audits (path-reversal KL asymmetry $\Sigma_T$ and ACC affinities), and we implement exact computations together with a reproducible witness suite and a Lean-checked idempotent/closure backbone for packaging equivalence and saturation \citep{demoura2021lean4,mathlib2020}.
Under calibrated controls, stroboscopic protocols can exhibit $\Sigma_T>0$ while their autonomous lifts yield $\Sigma_T\approx 0$ (protocol trap), whereas turning on internal phase drive produces a clean null-vs-driven separation with $\Sigma_T(Z)>0$ and a detectable projected macro arrow; moreover deterministic coarse-graining never increases $\Sigma_T$ and can erase it entirely, and packaging along refinement routes exhibits a prototype-driven holonomy defect that is large at moderate timescales while a uniform baseline is near zero and satisfies a gain-plus-mismatch bound.
These results supply a machine semantics and separation witnesses for a minimal substrate theorem, reducing false positives and turning SPT from a language into a compilation target up to packaging equivalence.
We are explicit that we do not establish a universal physical substrate or continuum limit: our conclusions are semantic and rest on exact finite-state audits and controlled constructions rather than empirical natural-system data.
