conclusion: We do not derive physical spacetime here
expanded_source_wording_tex:
Time is often treated as a primitive background parameter, and empirical discussions frequently conflate three distinct notions---event ordering, clock measurement, and irreversible directionality---making it difficult to determine when a layer \emph{has time} versus when time is an artifact of description. Building on Six Birds Theory (SBT) \citep{sixbirds_foundations}, we propose a layer-relative account in which time is a \emph{closure artifact} assembled from stable succession (order), staged repeatable carriers (ticks), and irreversible bookkeeping (arrow). We distinguish \emph{causation-time} within a fixed closure from \emph{enablement-time}, where the closure itself is rewritten. We instantiate this account in a finite-state Markov laboratory ($Z=X\times\Phi\times R$) and operationalize it through an audit-and-control workflow: calibrated null regimes, matched controls, and auto-generated evidence tables from reproducible artifacts.

We obtain four controlled separations: (i) in a nearly reversible null regime, arrow proxies are $\approx 0$, whereas in a record-coupled driven regime they become decisively nonzero (with absolute irreversibility signaled by $\mathrm{EP}=\infty$); (ii) under consistent estimation, coarse-graining reduces path-space asymmetry (micro $\ge$ macro), preventing ``fake arrows''; (iii) increasing maintenance budget reduces clock drift and failure, while progress metrics detect stall regimes that would otherwise appear stable; and (iv) closure-defect thresholds trigger theory extension only in an enablement regime (not in a no-birth control), and protocol loops exhibit nonzero holonomy in a noncommuting regime but $\approx 0$ under a commuting control, obstructing a global time potential. These results provide a reproducible method for separating arrows, clocks, constraints, and protocol effects, and for clarifying when ``instant updates'' reflect constraints and records rather than causal channels. We do not derive physical spacetime here; our conclusions rely on audited proxies in a minimal laboratory together with lightweight mechanized structural lemmas.

A layer comes with a feasible region or move set: what transitions are allowed and what can influence what. P2 asserts that causation is always conditional on feasibility.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\paragraph{Limits and scope.}
Several limitations are intentional. First, we do not claim that the laboratory's $\Phi$ is ``physical time''; it is a staged carrier used to audit when a clock can exist in a closure. Second, we do not claim that entropy production is the unique arrow; it is one audit proxy among many, selected for exactness in finite Markov worlds. Third, our enablement mechanism is deliberately simple (a thresholded closure defect). In richer systems, enablement is likely multi-scale and multi-object, with competing closures and budgets. Finally, we do not resolve foundational questions in quantum theory or relativity; we provide an SBT parsing that distinguishes feasibility constraints from causal channels and highlights the role of records and protocol dependence.

conclusion: We do not claim that all randomness is reducible to hidden microstructure, nor do we identify route mismatch with genuine irreversibility.
expanded_source_wording_tex: Our claims are deliberately narrower than the familiar metaphysical debate between ontic and epistemic randomness. We do not claim that all randomness is reducible to hidden microstructure, nor do we identify route mismatch with genuine irreversibility. We claim something operationally sharper: once a substrate, a packaging, and a maintenance budget are fixed, the non-intrinsic part of layer-relative randomness is measurable as the information about the next packaged state that remains hidden inside the current one. That claim is exact, falsifiable, and portable across domains.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
Formal theories of consciousness often mix mathematical structure, empirical
access, and ontological interpretation inside single claims. We present an
architecture that separates them by construction: an eight-clause closure
package (objecthood, strict promotion, a reflexive self-coordinate,
non-exposure, action credit, temporal closure, binding, and viability)
specified as a full design and audit contract, with every result graded as a
structural theorem, a recognition bridge, a conditional ontological
implication, or an open target. The evidence base consists of exact finite
studies, meaning exhaustively enumerated rational computations on declared
carriers, together with selected machine-checked Lean kernels. The central exact
result: on a declared twelve-state deadline carrier, every public-lens policy
has an empty viability kernel, the canonical predictive quotient restores a
ten-state kernel, and the unique minimal closure-restoring refinement splits
exactly one public fiber; extension beyond the carrier is a conditional
schema, not a generic theorem. A structural catalog then recasts privacy, the
explanatory gap, zombies, free will, binding, temporal experience, valence,
quality geometry, inverted spectra, personal identity, combination, and the
meta-problem as interface-relative factorization, quotient, viability, gauge,
and audit results. Realization is split into seven graded claims: a mechanized
conditional bridge purchases it only from assumed certificate soundness plus
an ontic-closure postulate, and there is no integrated certified instance and
no empirical validation. An auditable code baseline with executable
finite controls and predeclared prospective empirical obligations accompanies
the paper.

This paper takes that obligation as its organizing principle. It presents an
architecture for consciousness built from standard finite mathematics:
finite carriers, lenses, quotients, refinements, closure operators, viability
kernels, and audited promotion between description layers. Around that
architecture it assembles a catalog of exact finite results, a small set of
machine-checked kernels, and one explicitly priced ontological bridge. Every
scientific sentence in the paper is assigned to one of four \emph{claim lanes},
defined in Section~\ref{sec:claims}: structural results \textsf{[S]} (theorems and

interpretive mappings, never derivations), ontological implications \textsf{[O]}

discipline is not decoration; it is enforced by a sentence-level claim ledger
in the artifact, and the paper's central negative rule is that no amount of
\textsf{[S]} material ever implies an \textsf{[O]} conclusion without the named
purchases.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\begin{description}
\item[Tier S (structural).] Mathematical content about declared finite
objects. Tier~S subdivides by \emph{claim form}: a \emph{theorem-grade exact
result} is proved or exhaustively computed on its declared carrier; a
\emph{schema} is a definition or conditional statement whose hypotheses are
displayed and not discharged; a \emph{pointer} re-scopes an existing result to
a new reading without new mathematics; a \emph{composition} combines landed
results under a declared convention. Tier~S claims are established relative to
their carriers and interfaces, and to nothing else.
\item[Tier R (recognition).] A proposed mapping between a structural object
and a familiar mental or phenomenal category, for example reading a
constraint's dual price as felt valence. Recognition bridges are hypotheses.
They are \emph{proposed}, \emph{named}, and \emph{retractable}; they are never
derivations, and a counterexample to a bridge retracts the bridge, not the
mathematics under it.
\item[Tier O (ontological).] A claim about what satisfaction of the structure
would be. All Tier~O content in this paper is conditional on named postulates
(Section~\ref{sec:t17}); the paper contains no unconditional Tier~O sentence.
\item[OPEN.] A target that is stated, motivated, and not achieved. Open
targets are recorded in the artifact with explicit markers rather than
implied by silence.
\end{description}

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\paragraph{T6: introspection limits without introspection nihilism.}
\begin{theorem}[Same-level audit failure, rotating towers, confabulation; T6]
\textsf{[S]} \emph{Grade:} direct instantiation of imported self-audit theorems
plus finite toy extension. \emph{Scope:} instrument-indexed claims; complete
same-level self-certification, not ordinary introspection. No instrument
certifies its own complete soundness at its own level: the claim classifies
\texttt{undefined\_circular} or \texttt{outside\_scope}; a level-shift bridge
reclassifies it as \texttt{provisional}, never as same-level final. Every
finite rotating-audit tower has an uncertified top: the three-level toy tower
computes own-level statuses (\texttt{undefined\_circular} at each level),
bridge statuses (\texttt{provisional}, \texttt{provisional}), and
top-requires-next-level $=$ true. \emph{Confabulation corollary} (toy
extension; schema beyond it): with an audit update missing, the unique
closure-preserving completion from visible records is \emph{left} while the
hidden true state is \emph{right}: coherent and wrong. With the update
present, the unique completion is correct and the verdict disappears.
\emph{Nonclaim:} introspection is neither impossible nor worthless; partial,
level-shifted, bounded audit remains admissible, and self-image stability
over time is named as dependent on an open conjecture, not claimed.
\end{theorem}

\paragraph{T12: a descended quality geometry, exactly audited.}
\begin{theorem}[Induced-kernel similarity geometry; T12]
\textsf{[S]} \emph{Grade:} theorem-grade induced-kernel construction and exact
audit; the geometry-birth grade is audit-only. \emph{Scope:} the corrected
32-state micro-carrier (eight hues, two chroma, two texture levels), packaging
lens forgetting texture, staged twice. The lens descends the symmetric micro
kernel to a 16-point macro kernel $\hat P = U P^2 C$ with exact lift
consistency $UC = I$; texture is deliberately macro-relevant (a sluggish
grain multiplies move rates by $1/2$), so prototype content is operational,
not decorative. The exact max-product path similarity gives warm-neighbor
similarity $43/270$ versus cool-target $1/810$, so the warm neighbor is
strictly nearer; $d = -\log D$ is the additive distance on positive support.
Audits, all exact: closure defect $13441/52488$ (the swapped-prototype
incoherent control: $2619989/3499200$, strictly larger); prototype stability
maximum $2/3$, mean $13801/25920$; all $256$ ordered pairs connected; all
$16^3$ multiplicative triangle checks pass; route mismatch $0$. A texture-0
point-prototype lift preserves $UC=I$ yet changes the induced object and is
rejected: lift consistency alone does not certify prototype content. A local
signature table is chroma-favored at hues $0,3,7$, balanced at $1,5,6$,
hue-favored at $2,4$; a hand-declared signature-change transport has loop
residue $0$ on the balanced plateau and $1$ at the warm/cool boundary, with
multiplicative residual ratios $180/169$ (plateau) and $102/59$ (boundary),
both above one and strictly ordered. \emph{Nonclaim:} no smallness threshold
adjudicates the audits (only the computed controls do); the full
geometry-birth checklist (fitted inter-scale distortion, dimension
diagnostics, and curvature via neighborhood-MDS/Procrustes transport) is
not implemented; geometry is layer-relative; and the recovered similarity is
descended structure, never the hidden experience.
\end{theorem}

conclusion: Nonclaim: no claim that any particular quality space has nontrivial G
expanded_source_wording_tex:
\paragraph{T13: the inverted spectrum as a gauge computation.}
\begin{theorem}[Descent-fixing gauge and rigidification; T13]
\textsf{[S]} \emph{Grade:} theorem-grade exact finite construction; the broader
quality-space rigidification principle is schema-grade. \emph{Scope:} an
eight-state fiber bundle, $|Q| = 4$ public classes with two fiber points
each, declared descents. Define the descent-fixing gauge group
$G = \{\sigma \in \mathrm{Aut}(M) : \pi\sigma = \pi \text{ and } d\sigma = d
\text{ for every admissible descent } d\}$. Spectrum inversion is a lawful
distinct possibility exactly to the extent that $G$ is nontrivial. Exact
enumeration: $|\mathrm{Aut}|=40320$ automorphisms of the support, $16$
projection-fixing, and $G = \{\mathrm{id}, \text{global swap}\} \cong
\mathbb{Z}_2$ in the symmetric case; adding \emph{one} declared,
descent-visible discrimination-density orientation (calibrated by T12's
landed local signature at one public class) recomputes $G = \{\mathrm{id}\}$.
Route transport between two isomorphic fibers shows the same contrast: two
admissible transports symmetric, exactly one rigidified. \emph{Nonclaim:} no
claim that any particular quality space has nontrivial $G$; the rigidifier is
a modeled assumption, not a measurement; and if richer quality spaces always
rigidify, the inverted spectrum dissolves, which is an allowed outcome.
\end{theorem}

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{T18a (layer-minted proper time).} \textsf{[S]} theorem-grade finite
extension. The package's temporal coordinate does not factor through
substrate time: the exact strictness witness is a state pair with equal
substrate time and different package tick parity, so
$\Delta_{\mathrm{fact}}(\text{substrate time}, \text{package time}) \neq \emptyset$; T8's
funded triple is reused unchanged. Nonclaim: no relativistic proper time, no
claim that every subject has this clock.
\item \textbf{T18b (enablement as a lens rewrite).} \textsf{[S]} theorem-grade
exact finite instantiation. Promotion of a layer is an \emph{enablement-time}
event: a closure rewrite that creates the variable set in which the layer's
causation-time then runs. Exactly: the phase-omitting coarse lens has closure
defects $(1,1,1)$ across horizons; the enriched lens has $(0,0,0)$; the
partial-enrichment variant drops $(4/7,4/7,4/7)$ to $(0,0,0)$ using only the
relevant parity coordinate, strictly coarser than full reveal; the no-birth
control has zero defects before and after, so no beneficial rewrite exists.
Nonclaim (the repository name is ``subject birth''): no subject is created or
detected; the theorem is a finite lens-rewrite computation.
\item \textbf{T18c (demoted).} The intended theorem, temporal closure as a
precondition for stating the other clauses, is \emph{not} landed. The
static source audit finds explicit horizon/deadline tokens only in T1 among
T1/T2/T5/T7. T18c is therefore a schema-grade dependency observation,
recorded as demoted, and nothing in this paper cites it as a theorem.
\item \textbf{T18d (state taxonomy by funding and gating).} \textsf{[S]}
taxonomy-grade finite construction. Funding and entrainment gates classify
temporal-state rows: unfunded (tick rate $0$); funded and entrained (match
rate $1/1$, tick $1/1$); funded but decoupled (match $1/3$, tick $1/1$). The
rows are descended structural readings under T9's report discipline:
no claim about actual sleep, dreaming, or clinical states is licensed without
a recognition bridge, and none is proposed here.
\item \textbf{T18e (no canonical now-transport).} \textsf{[S]} direct temporal
reading of T13's machinery. Comparing ``nows'' across sub-closures is a route
transport problem: two admissible transports in the symmetric case, exactly
one after rigidification. There is no canonical inter-layer now unless the
declared descents rigidify the transport.
\end{itemize}

\paragraph{T14: identity as predictive lineage.}
\begin{theorem}[Lineage, trauma, fission/fusion, empty target; T14]
\textsf{[S]} \emph{Grade:} theorem-grade transfer of imported route-transport
machinery plus finite extensions. \emph{Scope:} a declared memory-wheel route
package with three histories, one current class, two predictive classes.
Identity over time is represented by the lineage of the predictive quotient
$M$: by the imported reachable-image factorization theorem, any
future-sufficient self-summary factors to $M$ (the toy computes the factor
from a strictly finer candidate and rejects the reverse). \emph{Trauma
shape:} a loop that is current-trivial and predictively nontrivial moves
$0/1$ of current classes and $1/1$ of predictive classes: same by all
present tests, changed in continuation. The identity-loop control moves
neither. \emph{Fission/fusion:} continuation maps on $M$-fibers classify
exactly as fiber-splitting (duplicated support) and fiber-merging (merged
support). \emph{Empty target:} the funded support has kernel size $3$; the
underfunded support has $K_{\mathrm{viab}}=\emptyset$ and empty post-exit fiber image,
so no continuation preserves the pre-exit $M$-fiber. \emph{Nonclaim:} no
complete metaphysics of personal identity. Token-independence and
death-as-dissolution readings are one-sentence Tier~O pointers deferred to
Section~\ref{sec:t17}; the Tier~S death fact is only $K_{\mathrm{viab}}=\emptyset$ plus
no fiber-preserving continuation, and the empty-target computation is
Python-certified (it is outside the law's Lean kernel).
\end{theorem}

\paragraph{T15: combination as a two-gate audit on one carrier.}
\begin{theorem}[Combination gate; T15]
\textsf{[S]} \emph{Grade:} schema with an exact one-carrier construction.
\emph{Scope:} one joint-package carrier with live states
\emph{diagonal}/\emph{crossed} and a dead exit. Combination into a joint
subject is certified only when the joint family passes both gates on the
\emph{joint} carrier: (i)~C7 joint strict refinement, where the exact witness has
$K_{\mathrm{bw}} = (2)$, $R_{\mathrm{rec}} = (1,1)$; and (ii)~C3 joint reflexivity, where per-action
refinement of the joint public lens terminates at the pairing-valued
predictive quotient, trajectory $1 \to 2 \to 2$, and that quotient carries the
viability-relevant joint coordinate (public-lens kernel $\{$diagonal$\}$
versus terminal-lens kernel $\{$diagonal, crossed$\}$). Aggregation is
exactly the collapsed $R_{\mathrm{rec}} = K_{\mathrm{bw}}$ interface with no forced joint
self-coordinate. The subject boundary is gate-determined by the surviving
promoted carrier, not by a topological surface or by summing micro-packages.
Interface contrast on the same states: the subject interface hides pairing
(exposure false); the collective-ledger interface publishes it (exposure
true), failing C4 by design, an institution-shaped control.
\emph{Nonclaim:} no general verdict about real collectives, and aggregation
of local contents is never sufficient: it is the collapsed regime.
\end{theorem}

Twelve limitations, before any conclusion.

\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{Exact finite models only.} Every positive result lives on a
declared toy carrier. Nothing licenses transfer to large, noisy, or
continuous systems beyond the displayed conditional schemas.
\item \textbf{No empirical content.} No dataset, no parameter fit, no
validation, no phenomenon rows (Section~\ref{sec:empirical}).
\item \textbf{Provenance of predictions.} The artifact contains documents
labelled as predictions, but their initial Git history does not establish
temporal precedence over implementations, and later corrections are
versioned. Nothing in this paper calls them preregistered.
\item \textbf{Selected mechanization.} Lean coverage is selected, not
catalog-wide: kernels prove core facts and pin many enumerated values as
certified constants matching the Python computations (per-law boundaries in
Table~\ref{tbl:catalog} and Appendix~\ref{app:repro}); the current
manifest-level validator accepts a zero-row schema and is a known release
blocker, so no manifest-audited coverage claim is made.
\item \textbf{Inherited trust base.} The Lean development trusts vendored
foundations modules and declared axioms from the companion corpus, cataloged
in Appendix~\ref{app:repro}; their opacity guards are inherited, not
re-proved.
\item \textbf{T1's family boundary.} The forcing theorem is exact on one
carrier; the family schema's hypotheses (live non-definable phase, deadline
relevance) are strong and not claimed common (Section~\ref{sec:t1family}).
\item \textbf{T12's open target.} Geometry birth (fitted distortion,
dimension, curvature transport) is not landed; the landed object is an
audited induced geometry.
\item \textbf{T16's conventions.} The meta-problem composition is relative
to a declared completion convention, and its carrier collapses several
premises extensionally.
\item \textbf{T17's open core.} The simplified/full schema relation is
unproved in both directions, certificate soundness is assumed where used,
A2 has no formal theorem, and T17-I, the integrated instance, is open
(Section~\ref{sec:t17}).
\item \textbf{T18c demoted.} The temporal-precondition claim is a dependency
observation, not a theorem.
\item \textbf{Recognition bridges are unproved.} Valence, phenomenological
clause mappings, attention readings, and all state-taxonomy readings are
named hypotheses (\textsf{[R]}), each retractable without structural loss.
\item \textbf{Review status.} The artifact's ``external review request''
documents record an internal author-driven review loop; they are not
independent peer review, and this preprint has not been peer reviewed.
\end{enumerate}

expanded_source_wording_tex: We present a reproducible computational framework for defining and measuring agency in finite controlled Markov kernels without assuming goals, utilities, or homunculi. The framework operationalizes three complementary metrics: (i)~viability kernels (greatest controlled-invariant safe sets under ledger-gated feasibility and successor-support semantics), (ii)~feasible empowerment (channel capacity of the induced action-to-output channel restricted by budgets), and (iii)~an empirical packaging endomap whose idempotence defect quantifies objecthood for coarse lenses. Building on Six Birds Theory (SBT, \citep{six_birds_theory}), we propose that an agent is a \emph{theory object}---a maintained package inside an induced layer with a ledger-gated interface---and we separate \emph{agenthood} (enablement: the layer exists and persists) from \emph{agency} (causation: interface interventions change outside futures). Throughout, ``theory'' is used in the SBT technical sense---a closure (lens + completion + audit)---not as a speculative hypothesis or manuscript-type category. Across matched-control ablations in a minimal ring-world substrate, we obtain four auditable separations: (1)~calibrated null regimes prevent false positives (single-action: 0-bit empowerment; schedule trap: 1~bit under the wrong model, 0 under the correct one); (2)~enabling repair collapses idempotence defect at $\tau=2$ from 1 to 0; (3)~enabling protocol holonomy leaves $H=1$ unchanged but increases empowerment for $H\ge2$; and (4)~operator rewriting (skill $\theta$) monotonically increases median empowerment ($0.73\to1.34$ bits). All experiments are driven by deterministic, hash-traceable scripts with a strict audit mode, and a Lean~4 anchor formalizes the viability-kernel fixed-point property. We are explicit that stronger claims about goals, consciousness, or real organisms are not established here; our conclusions rely on finite witnesses and operational proxies under explicit controls.

conclusion: Six Birds Theory (SBT) supplies the admissibility calculus for that ledger: typed audited layers of the language model (called closure-package layers when formalized in ), explicit quotient maps, audit and nonclaim records, and promotion gates for deciding when a proposed layer is a strict extension rather than an unaudited readout .
expanded_source_wording_tex: We study an alternative formulation: a non-gradient setting in which the language model is an audited ledger of finite theory extensions rather than a parameter vector. Six Birds Theory (SBT) supplies the admissibility calculus for that ledger: typed audited layers of the language model (called closure-package layers when formalized in \Cref{sec:problem-setup}), explicit quotient maps, audit and nonclaim records, and promotion gates for deciding when a proposed layer is a strict extension rather than an unaudited readout \cite{Tsiokos2026FoundationsIII}. These objects are not presented as a replacement for large-scale parametric training, but as a controlled substrate for asking when a fixed corpus supports a structural refinement claim. We instantiate the substrate as Language Theory Models (LTMs), a prototype architecture whose runtime accumulates transition evidence, proposes audited layers, and records failed or non-certifying attempts rather than converting fallback evidence into stronger claims. \Cref{sec:methods} describes the gate panel and runtime mechanics; here the point is the modelling shift from learned weights alone to an explicit audit trail of finite extensions.

expanded_source_wording_tex: Six Birds Theory (SBT) enters this paper as an admissibility calculus for structural claims, not as a replacement training objective. Its primitive objects are typed audited layers, explicit quotient maps, audit and nonclaim records, and promotion gates that determine whether a proposed extension can be claimed \cite{Tsiokos2026FoundationsI,Tsiokos2026FoundationsII,Tsiokos2026FoundationsIII}. In ML terms, the calculus specifies what counts as evidence, what must be logged, what must remain a nonclaim, and when a gate panel may certify that a candidate layer strictly refines the current quotient; this is distinct from learning, since it constrains when a recovered structure is admissible rather than choosing what the next model should optimize. The load-bearing sources are used narrowly: Foundations I supplies the typed layer atom and its idempotence condition \cite{Tsiokos2026FoundationsI}, Foundations II the admissibility meta-theory \cite{Tsiokos2026FoundationsII}, Foundations III the dependency-relation calculus and gate scaffolding \cite{Tsiokos2026FoundationsIII}, with Promotion Criteria for gate templates \cite{Tsiokos2026PromotionCriteria}, the strict-extension paper for the relabeling-rejection hypothesis cluster \cite{Tsiokos2026CantorShell}, the accepted-new-layer tests for readout-sufficiency contracts \cite{Tsiokos2026AcceptedNewLayer}, To Notch a Stone for the causation/enablement-time distinction \cite{Tsiokos2026NotchAStone}, Recombination Witnesses for the recombination-aware quotient \cite{Tsiokos2026RecombinationWitnesses}, and the no-go results for the conditional-information obstruction \cite{Tsiokos2026NoGo}.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
Relative to next-token and autoregressive language modeling \cite{Bengio2003NPLM,Vaswani2017Attention}, the LTM is not a replacement objective: it adds a non-gradient ledger that audits where a fixed corpus does or does not support compositional refinement claims. Relative to compositional generalization benchmarks such as SCAN, COGS, and CFQ, which usually evaluate trained models post hoc \cite{Hupkes2020Compositionality}, the LTM instruments the recovery process itself and records non-certifying attempts before a finished artifact is declared; relative to mechanistic interpretability and circuits work \cite{Olah2020ZoomIn,Elhage2021Framework,Olsson2022InductionHeads,Conmy2023ACDC}, it shares the auditability motivation but tracks typed recovery layers and gate-panel decisions rather than activation patches or circuit attributions; and relative to symbolic, neurosymbolic, and program-induction approaches \cite{Ellis2023DreamCoder,GarcezLamb2020Neurosymbolic}, it is adjacent in seeking typed structural objects but treats them as recoveries from a fixed corpus with explicit nonclaim records rather than as programs from a search engine.

expanded_source_wording_tex: The LTM setting in this paper is fixed-corpus inverse recovery: the input is a finite sequence corpus, and the task is to recover audited refinements already supported by that corpus rather than to explain how the corpus was produced. The locked empirical instantiation uses a Shakespeare corpus derived from a Gutenberg source, tokenized by a word-punctuation regular-expression tokenizer with a frozen vocabulary; \Cref{sec:primary-results} reports the resulting run. At startup, the runtime declares its scope in a regime record naming the corpus, tokenization surface, lens family, candidate-search family, budget profile, and audit instrument stack. This declaration is the operational boundary for every later evidence record: candidate layers, quotient tests, and gate outcomes are interpreted only relative to the declared corpus and tokenizer. In SBT terms this is an inverse-emergence regime, but the ML claim is narrower: fixed-corpus structural recovery under explicit nonclaim discipline, with runtime mechanics described in \Cref{sec:methods} \cite{Tsiokos2026FoundationsII}. The runtime, locked-run artifact set, and probe suite are available at \url{https://anonymous.4open.science/r/how-to-chat-a-stone-nips} (anonymous code repository for double-blind review).

expanded_source_wording_tex:
The readout path is capped by the same nonclaim discipline as layer promotion \cite{Tsiokos2026FoundationsII}. When the audited path does not produce a committed answer, for example because no current layer's quotient covers the requested microstate at sufficient confidence, the runtime does not promote fallback statistics into a stronger claim. Instead, it either emits a provisional or silent claim with a typed defect record, or refuses to emit a token claim. The structural posture is the abstention / reject-option discipline familiar from selective classification \cite{Chow1970Reject,ElYanivWiener2010Selective}, paired with the reliability concern that motivates calibration in modern neural networks \cite{Guo2017Calibration}. At pass end, a halt-verdict classifier reports the final status as accepted, provisional, blocked, outside-scope, failed-audit, absent-with-record, or below-threshold \cite{Tsiokos2026FoundationsIII}. Each verdict is paired with required nonclaim references that state what is and is not in scope; \Cref{sec:primary-results} reports the locked-run outcome, \Cref{sec:analysis} analyzes the verdict semantics, and \Cref{app:methods} gives the verdict-class table.

Both halves are deferred to future work as a joint pair, because unfreezing parents without bidirectional flow models a half-loop no published characterization covers, with the underlying causation/enablement distinction following ; records the literal nonclaims and the maintenance-loop rationale. The runtime also relies on bounded-precision thresholds and a small set of finite hyperparameters (cadence, persistence streak, canonicalisation iteration cap), each reported as a runtime approximation in . The concrete trigger for reopening the deferred work would be persistent stagnation at intermediate chain depths despite long horizons and sustained pressure-source diversity; the locked run does not show this signal.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
Repeated interaction routinely produces structure absent from the one-shot
game: reputations, norms, conventions, and other institutions.  The problem is
to say what this structure is, when the bare game predicts play, and where the
extra structure comes from.  This paper argues that the
institutional content of repeated play is a strict extension of the stage game:
a refinement with genuinely new predictive distinctions not definable as a
function of the game's own vocabulary.  The argument uses a finite, fully
explicit repeated-game laboratory, with mathematical claims verified by exact
finite recomputation and reproducible validators, and a pre-registered
re-analysis of a published human repeated Prisoner's Dilemma dataset.

The institutional state studied here has a canonical form: the coarsest
predictive summary of history, equivalent to a predictive-sufficiency or
causal-state construction.  On the finite carrier this object is non-definable
from the game itself, and the predictive failure of stage-vocabulary models is
priced exactly by a conditional mutual information.  The quantitative constants
governing institutional collapse are reproducible within declared protocols
but resist shortcut: across a declared formula class and three frozen
out-of-sample transfer attempts, no tested low-complexity shortcut transfers
across families.  In the human data, the corresponding predictive-residue
hypothesis is confirmed out of sample under a protocol registered before any
data access, while a more specific pre-registered timing hypothesis fails in
the reverse direction: history-dependence grows with experience.  Claims are
scoped to the declared finite carrier, declared run families and protocols, and
analyzed dataset; broader framework theorems are imported and cited, not
re-proved here.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
An example of the successful label is a recent-deviation bit: it can be on
because a defection occurred in the last two completed profiles, and then turn
off after two clean rounds.  This is public and history-computable, but it is
not merely the current stage profile or the empirical count summary.  Because
the trigger can be live at the comparison round, two histories that look
the same through the base game can lead extended strategies to different
future laws.  The landed exhibit holds relative to
the declared extension.  Its institutional reading is narrow:
publishing institutional state can change behavior broadly, but it enriches
the institution itself only under specific conditions--live,
non-stage-definable, reactive feedback--and, on this carrier, only where the
structure is still forming.  It does not assert universal forcing.

conclusion: This paper does not claim the predictive-state or causal-state quotient construction as new It does not claim the closure-deficit identity, or the optimality of the best autonomous macro-predictor, as new It does not claim the strict-extension, saturation, or promotion-obligation framework as new
expanded_source_wording_tex:
The anti-relabeling ledger is part of the result.  This paper does not claim
the predictive-state or causal-state quotient construction as new; that is a
standard way to summarize a process by its predictive consequences
\citep{ShaliziCrutchfield2001ComputationalMechanics,
LittmanSuttonSingh2001PredictiveRepresentations}.  It does not claim the
closure-deficit identity, or the optimality of the best autonomous
macro-predictor, as new; those are imported from the closure-deficit and no-go
accounts \citep{Tsiokos2026CastStone,Tsiokos2026NoGo}.  It does not claim the
strict-extension, saturation, or promotion-obligation framework as new; those
are imported standards for recognizing when a higher vocabulary is a genuine
layer rather than a relabeling
\citep{Tsiokos2026CantorShell,Tsiokos2026FoundationsIII}.  Nor does it claim
as new the game-theoretic fact that added structure matters.  Folk theorems
show that repeated interaction can support many outcomes; global games show
how noisy private information can select; reputation models show how type
structure changes play; evolutionary and stochastic-stability models show
that convention selection can be a property of a run; correlated equilibrium
and type spaces show how signals and hidden state enlarge the game
\citep{FudenbergMaskin1986FolkTheorem,CarlssonVanDamme1993GlobalGames,
KrepsMilgromRobertsWilson1982RationalCooperation,
KandoriMailathRob1993LearningMutation,Young1993EvolutionConventions,
Aumann1974SubjectivityCorrelation}.  These are reference points the paper uses, not
results it rebrands.

conclusion: The exact results in this paper live on a specific finite carrier: a memory-one reactive-rule catalog, two main payoff families, a uniform prior, and declared lenses, rounds, horizons, and extensions. Their highest grade is theorem-grade-on-the-carrier, not a general repeated-game theorem. The run constants are scoped to the declared payoff families, evolutionary dynamics, population sizes, noise grids, estimators, and protocols. The no-shortcut conclusion is correspondingly scoped to the tested formula classes and the three frozen transfer tests; it is not a proof that no transferable shortcut exists. The human-data analysis is one published dataset analyzed under one frozen protocol, with mapping amendments recorded before analysis; it does not confirm or refute any carrier theorem. The broader framework results used here, including predictive quotients, closure deficit, strict-extension obligations, and promotion gates, are imported and cited , not re-proved. Finally, the material-forcing result is relative to its declared label-feedback extension; it is not a claim that institutional labels generally enrich play.

It is not a proof that no transferable shortcut exists. The run constants are scoped to the declared payoff families, stochastic dynamics, population sizes, noise grids, estimators, and execution protocols. Changing any of these can change the measured constant. The human-data analysis concerns one published dataset under one frozen protocol. It neither validates nor invalidates any carrier theorem, and the memory-one strategy-space alignment is a shared language rather than a bridge theorem. The material-forcing result holds relative to its declared label-feedback extension. It is not a claim that public institutional labels generally enrich play. The paper makes no welfare, mechanism-design, real-world-institution, or universal-equilibrium-selection claim. The institution in this manuscript is a predictive-state object, not a claim about agents' internal representations. The crystallization mechanism suggested by the human timing reversal is open. A within-agent learning or acquisition layer is named as the next construction, not resolved here. The paper's own finite-carrier results are verified by exact finite recomputation rather than by a proof assistant. Imported framework theorems carry their own status in the cited source papers.

Six Birds Theory has produced three landed Clay-class conditional
closures: Navier--Stokes regularity, the Riemann Hypothesis, and
P~vs~NP, each under the SB closure assumption of Foundations~I.  This
paper does not re-prove those substrate results.  It extracts their
common meta-theoretic form for a reader who treats Six Birds as a
typed framework for organizing attempted closures of open conjectures.
The account has two complementary halves.  The negative half,
Foreclosure, studies a typed primary carrier, meaning an attempted
proof construction whose type signature targets a designated
conjecture, and proves that admissible carriers fall into a finite
state space: non-target-equivalent, target-equivalent tautological,
bridge-failed, or matrix-element-terminal.  The positive half,
Recognition-Mode Landing, gives a seven-stage route for
trace-state-only substrates: instead of deriving the load-bearing
source from framework primitives, it imports that source as named
recognition under closure formation.  The v5 refinement states the
joint thesis: derivation routes remain subject to foreclosure, while
recognition-mode landings are structurally distinct peer routes under
the same closure assumption.  A third part, the Calibration Family,
provides the typed bookkeeping that makes this comparison uniform
across substrates: calibrations, bridges-as-theorems, directed bridge
types, coverage geometry, framework-type mismatch, and named
functorial gates.  Layer-instantiation examples appear throughout: the
three substrate validation rows (NS, RH, and PvNP), a thirteen-entry
calibration seed catalog of typed detectors, two named coverage holes,
and three named functorial gates from the PvNP track.  The formal
catalog contains seventeen rows: three partial structural derivations,
eight primary theorem-grade rows, and six primary obligation rows.  The body gives the mathematical proofs or
obligation analyses, while Lean serves as the mechanization companion
and audit trail.  The nine honest obligation axioms are
recorded with opacity guards, so their assumptions are explicit rather
than silently instantiated; the full validator chain cross-checks the
inventory, manifest, and trust base.  The scope is deliberately
limited: BSD and Hodge are out of scope except as future work or
prediction, and no substrate closure is strengthened here to a
standard-ZFC unconditional claim.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
The present paper is not a survey of the analytic, arithmetic, or
complexity-theoretic details of the three substrate papers.  It
extracts from them the common structural question: when the framework
has produced a formed setting, which parts of the work are genuinely
internal, which parts are named external mathematics, and how does the
audit prevent the two from being conflated?  The resulting answer is
modest in one respect and ambitious in another.  It is modest because
it does not claim new unconditional results about the Clay problems.
It is ambitious because it claims that the framework's closure
behavior has a reusable meta-theoretic form.

conclusion: The paper does not claim that the space of mathematical ideas is finite.
expanded_source_wording_tex:
This also explains the precise sense in which the paper speaks of
foreclosure.  The paper does not claim that the space of mathematical
ideas is finite.  It claims that, after the framework fixes the type
of the target and the admissible role of a carrier, the audit sees a
finite set of state-types through which a derivation-mode attempt can
pass.
The word ``foreclosure'' is therefore not a statement about human
ingenuity.  It is a statement about typed bookkeeping: certain moves
cannot be counted as free progress because they reintroduce the target
content, miss the target, or terminate at content not supplied by the
carrier.  This is the level at which a meta-theorem can speak across
Navier--Stokes, RH, and P versus NP without pretending that the three
problems have the same mathematics.

In predicate form, with \(R_C=0\) denoting closure of the residual,
the four states used throughout Part~I are:
\[
\begin{aligned}
  \mbox{$X$-equivalent}_X(C)
    &\Longleftrightarrow (R_C=0 \leftrightarrow X),\\
  \mbox{non-$X$-equivalent}_X(C)
    &\Longleftrightarrow
      \exists X'.\, (R_C=0 \leftrightarrow X')\wedge X'\neq X,\\
  \mbox{\textsc{CRE-TE}}_X(C)
    &\Longleftrightarrow
      \mbox{$X$-equivalent}_X(C)\wedge
      \operatorname{SelfAuditFail}(C),\\
  \mbox{\textsc{CRE-BF}}_X(C)
    &\Longleftrightarrow
      \operatorname{NoBridge}(C,X)\vee
      \operatorname{BridgeMismatch}(C,X),\\
  \mbox{\textsc{CRE-CTMT}}_X(C)
    &\Longleftrightarrow
      \operatorname{MRed}(C)\wedge
      \neg\operatorname{IRDec}(C)\wedge
      \neg\operatorname{MDEqTarget}(C,X).
\end{aligned}
\]
Here \(\operatorname{SelfAuditFail}(C)\) abbreviates the
Foundations~III audit alternatives \(C\)'s same-level audit being
outside scope or undefined-circular.  The symbols
\(\operatorname{NoBridge}\), \(\operatorname{BridgeMismatch}\),
\(\operatorname{MRed}\), \(\operatorname{IRDec}\), and
\(\operatorname{MDEqTarget}\) abbreviate, respectively, the
target-relative bridge failures, matrix-family reduction,
inherited-records decision predicate, and target-equivalence test for
the terminal matrix family.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
This paper proves a conditional separation between \(P\) and \(NP\)
inside Six Birds Theory, a typed framework for closure formation in
mathematical structures.  For SAT, the framework supplies a saturated
SAT layer \(T^{!}_{\mathrm{SAT}}\) --- a typed carrier of polynomial-time SAT
computations together with their audit data --- observed through a
lawful polynomial-time instrument \(I_{\mathrm{poly}}\) that declares which
observations on the layer count as \emph{current}.  Two translation
theorems connect this setup to standard SAT semantics.  Translation A
identifies \(\mathrm{SAT}\in P\) with decision currentization: the SAT
decision bit is itself a current observation on \(T^{!}_{\mathrm{SAT}}\).  Translation
B identifies decision currentization with currentization of the
canonical witness producer of the autonomous lift \(\Omega_{\mathrm{SAT}}\), using
SAT self-reducibility and closure of current observables under
post-processing, finite products, and composition.

The structural hypothesis \(\Gamma_{\textsc{csl-sat-hidden}}\) of
\citet{TsiokosHiddenness2026} says that this canonical witness producer
is not a lawful current observable on \(T^{!}_{\mathrm{SAT}}\).  Under that
hypothesis, the four-step contradiction chain gives
\(\mathrm{SAT}\notin P\); combined with \(\mathrm{SAT}\in NP\) from the
standard verifier package, the framework accepts
\(P^{\mathrm{SB}}\neqNP^{\mathrm{SB}}\) at recognition grade.  Outside the framework, the
result is the conditional theorem: formed-SAT closure carrying
\(\Gamma_{\textsc{csl-sat-hidden}}\) under \(I_{\mathrm{poly}}\) implies \(P\neq NP\).

The same closure records also tag \(T^{!}_{\mathrm{SAT}}\), in the audit-closure
register of \citet{Tsiokos2026AOR}, as a carrier-attached
cascade-stable AOR package under \(\Gamma_{\textsc{csl-sat-hidden}}\).  This is packaging
of the same conditional theorem.  The hypothesis further localizes to
one residual: the canonical lexicographic SAT-branching readout is not
a lawful current observable on the standard fixed-presentation
polynomial current carrier.  A scoped Class-B Irremovability theorem
rules out one removal route: no basis-generated Class-B
carrier-feature method can remove that residual, except by leaving the
basis or importing a target-equivalent lower bound.

The paper does not claim an unconditional standard-ZFC separation of
\(P\) and \(NP\), derivability of \(\Gamma_{\textsc{csl-sat-hidden}}\) from framework
primitives, circumvention of the classical barriers in their native
senses, absolute irremovability of \(\Gamma_{\textsc{csl-sat-hidden}}\), or any AOR claim
outside the stated formed-SAT, standard-basis scope.

source_wording_tex:
This paper proves a conditional separation between \(P\) and \(NP\)
inside Six Birds Theory, a typed framework for closure formation in
mathematical structures.  For SAT, the framework supplies a saturated
SAT layer \(\Tsat\) --- a typed carrier of polynomial-time SAT
computations together with their audit data --- observed through a
lawful polynomial-time instrument \(\Ipoly\) that declares which
observations on the layer count as \emph{current}.  Two translation
theorems connect this setup to standard SAT semantics.  Translation A
identifies \(\mathrm{SAT}\in P\) with decision currentization: the SAT
decision bit is itself a current observation on \(\Tsat\).  Translation
B identifies decision currentization with currentization of the
canonical witness producer of the autonomous lift \(\OmegaSAT\), using
SAT self-reducibility and closure of current observables under
post-processing, finite products, and composition.

The structural hypothesis \(\CSLSATHidden\) of
\citet{TsiokosHiddenness2026} says that this canonical witness producer
is not a lawful current observable on \(\Tsat\).  Under that
hypothesis, the four-step contradiction chain gives
\(\mathrm{SAT}\notin P\); combined with \(\mathrm{SAT}\in NP\) from the
standard verifier package, the framework accepts
\(\PSB\neq\NPSB\) at recognition grade.  Outside the framework, the
result is the conditional theorem: formed-SAT closure carrying
\(\CSLSATHidden\) under \(\Ipoly\) implies \(P\neq NP\).

The same closure records also tag \(\Tsat\), in the audit-closure
register of \citet{Tsiokos2026AOR}, as a carrier-attached
cascade-stable AOR package under \(\CSLSATHidden\).  This is packaging
of the same conditional theorem.  The hypothesis further localizes to
one residual: the canonical lexicographic SAT-branching readout is not
a lawful current observable on the standard fixed-presentation
polynomial current carrier.  A scoped Class-B Irremovability theorem
rules out one removal route: no basis-generated Class-B
carrier-feature method can remove that residual, except by leaving the
basis or importing a target-equivalent lower bound.

The paper does not claim an unconditional standard-ZFC separation of
\(P\) and \(NP\), derivability of \(\CSLSATHidden\) from framework
primitives, circumvention of the classical barriers in their native
senses, absolute irremovability of \(\CSLSATHidden\), or any AOR claim
outside the stated formed-SAT, standard-basis scope.

conclusion: For a reader already working inside Six Birds Theory, the paper proves a framework-relative judgment: under the standard closure assumption of Foundations I, and conditional on a specified structural recognition source, the internal predicates P^ SB and NP^ SB separate at recognition grade .
expanded_source_wording_tex:
The first result has two readings.  For a reader already working inside
Six Birds Theory, the paper proves a framework-relative judgment: under
the standard closure assumption of Foundations I, and conditional on a
specified structural recognition source, the internal predicates
\(P^{\mathrm{SB}}\) and \(NP^{\mathrm{SB}}\) separate at \emph{recognition grade}
\citep{TsiokosFoundationsI2026}.  A \(\mathbf{BirdInt}^{\mathrm{aud}}_{\mathrm{fin}}\) judgment is the typed
audit-and-judgment shape supplied by Foundations III: it records the
source being used, the layer on which the source acts, the instrument
through which observation is made, and the proposition being accepted
\citep{TsiokosFoundationsIII2026}.  The grade matters.  At recognition
grade the acceptance depends on a structural source supplied to the
construction rather than derived within it.

This is the scope of the paper.  It does not prove an unconditional
standard-ZFC separation of \(P\) from \(NP\).  Its headline judgment is
framework-relative and recognition-grade; outside the framework, what
is established is the conditional theorem just described.  Nor does
the paper claim to bypass natural proofs, algebrization, or
relativization in their native settings.  The construction works at a
different layer: typed observable saturation over a SAT-specific
history carrier.  Finally, the paper does not claim that
\(\Gamma_{\textsc{csl-sat-hidden}}\) follows from the framework primitives.  It is a
structural recognition source supplied by \citet{TsiokosHiddenness2026}.
The Class-B barrier theorem
also has its own scope: it does not prove absolute irremovability of the
recognition source, rule out future Six Birds laws using genuinely new
carrier structure outside the fixed-presentation basis, or apply to
enriched carriers such as objective SAT, branchwise carriers, or
presentation-quotiented carriers.  \Cref{sec:pvnp-aor-instance} then
reads the same closure records in the audit-closure register of
\citet{Tsiokos2026AOR}, tagging \(T^{!}_{\mathrm{SAT}}\) as a carrier-attached
audit-closure package under \(\Gamma_{\textsc{csl-sat-hidden}}\) without adding new
content.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
We now combine the two translation theorems with the recognition
source.  Translation A converts a standard polynomial-time SAT decider
into decision currentization.  Translation B converts decision
currentization into witness currentization.  The recognition source
\(\Gamma_{\textsc{csl-sat-hidden}}\) says that witness currentization fails on the
formed SAT layer under \(I_{\mathrm{poly}}\).  The resulting contradiction gives
\(\mathrm{SAT}\notin P\), conditional on the structural recognition
source.  We then record the standard verifier-package fact
\(\mathrm{SAT}\in NP\).  Together these are the construction-side
inputs for the framework-relative judgment stated in the next section.

conclusion: Conditional on pseudorandom function generators of the required strength, no such natural property proves the strong circuit lower bounds needed for P versus NP .
expanded_source_wording_tex:
The Razborov--Rudich natural-proofs barrier
\citep{RazborovRudich1997NaturalProofs} rules out a broad class of
combinatorial lower-bound methods.  In that setting a natural property
of Boolean functions is constructive, large, and useful against the
circuit class under attack.  The carrier-level fact is
pseudorandomness: a large constructive property useful against all easy
functions would distinguish pseudorandom functions from truly random
functions.  Conditional on pseudorandom function generators of the
required strength, no such natural property proves the strong circuit
lower bounds needed for \(P\) versus \(NP\).  Subsequent work has
refined the largeness and constructivity conditions
\citep{Chow2011AlmostNaturalProofs} without removing the barrier in its
intended scope.

Positively, the paper claims the following.  The saturated SAT layer
construction, including \(T^{!}_{\mathrm{SAT}}\), \(E^{!}_{Q}\), \(M^{!}_{\mathrm{SAT}}\),
\(Q^{!}_{\mathrm{SAT}}\), and \(\Omega_{\mathrm{SAT}}\), is standard mathematics expressed in
the framework's typed vocabulary.  The closure properties of
\(E^{!}_{Q}\) are the current-observable closure rules needed by the
translation theorems.  Translation A identifies standard
\(\mathrm{SAT}\in P\) with \(\operatorname{Currentize}^{\mathrm{dec}}_{Q}(\mathrm{SAT})\), and
Translation B identifies \(\operatorname{Currentize}^{\mathrm{dec}}_{Q}(\mathrm{SAT})\) with
\(\operatorname{Currentize}^{\mathrm{wit}}_{Q}(\Omega_{\mathrm{SAT}})\).  Conditional on the structural
recognition source \(\Gamma_{\textsc{csl-sat-hidden}}\), the four-step contradiction
gives \(\mathrm{SAT}\notin P\).  The BirdInt judgment records
\(P^{\mathrm{SB}}\neqNP^{\mathrm{SB}}\) at \emph{recognition grade} under the standard Six Birds
closure assumption.  Read as ordinary mathematics, the result is the
conditional theorem
\[
  \text{formed-SAT closure carrying \(\Gamma_{\textsc{csl-sat-hidden}}\) under \(I_{\mathrm{poly}}\)}
  \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
  P\neq NP.
\]
The paper also proves the Six Birds Class-B Irremovability barrier on
the standard fixed-presentation polynomial current carrier
(\Cref{thm:pvnp:irremovability-scoped}).  The localization in
\Cref{sec:recognition-source} identifies the concrete residual on
which the barrier acts:
\(\mathrm{Br}^{\mathrm{lex}}_{\mathrm{SAT}}\notinE^{!}_{Q}\).

Independently of the audit records — in particular the recognition source Gamma_ csl-sat-hidden and the six declared per-discharge structures — the result is not an unconditional standard-ZFC P≠ NP claim; the AOR-instance reading reframes the closure stack as a carrier-attached audit-closure package but does not upgrade the conditional separation to an unconditional one outside the audit-record presentation. These six nonclaims distinguish what the paper proves from what would be required to upgrade the result to an unconditional standard-mathematics theorem, or to a result that addresses the classical barriers in their native formulations. The fourth nonclaim is the scope fence for the Class-B Irremovability barrier theorem of ; the fifth and sixth are the scope fences for the AOR-instance recasting of . expanded_source_wording_tex:
\paragraph{Construction grade vs recognition grade.}
The construction-grade content of the paper is the part built directly:
the saturated SAT layer, observable saturation and its closure
properties, Translation Theorem A, Translation Theorem B, the
conditional four-step contradiction, and the standard verifier package
for \(\mathrm{SAT}\in NP\).  These are ordinary mathematical
constructions expressed in the framework's typed vocabulary.  The
recognition-grade content is different.  It is the \(\mathbf{BirdInt}^{\mathrm{aud}}_{\mathrm{fin}}\)
judgment that packages the conditional theorem into the
framework-relative assertion \(P^{\mathrm{SB}}\neqNP^{\mathrm{SB}}\) at
\emph{recognition grade}, using the supplied recognition source
\(\Gamma_{\textsc{csl-sat-hidden}}\).  The finite-audit judgment apparatus is the
Foundations-III setting for such records \citep{TsiokosFoundationsIII2026}.
This distinction is the reason the paper is not presented as a
candidate unconditional proof: the contradiction chain is theorem-grade
conditional on the source, while the final judgment is recognition
grade relative to that source.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
The paper has proved three linked results.  First, it constructs the
saturated SAT layer \(T^{!}_{\mathrm{SAT}}\), the lawful polynomial-time current
instrument \(I_{\mathrm{poly}}\), and the saturated current-observable family
\(E^{!}_{Q}\), then proves Translation Theorem A and Translation Theorem
B.  Conditional on the structural recognition source
\(\Gamma_{\textsc{csl-sat-hidden}}\), the four-step contradiction gives
\(\mathrm{SAT}\notin P\); combined with the standard verifier-package
fact \(\mathrm{SAT}\in NP\) \citep{Cook1971TheoremProving}, this yields
the framework-relative \(\mathbf{BirdInt}^{\mathrm{aud}}_{\mathrm{fin}}\) judgment \(P^{\mathrm{SB}}\neqNP^{\mathrm{SB}}\) at
\emph{recognition grade}.  Outside the framework, this is the conditional
theorem that formed SAT closure carrying \(\Gamma_{\textsc{csl-sat-hidden}}\) under
\(I_{\mathrm{poly}}\) implies \(P\neq NP\).
Second, \Cref{sec:recognition-source} makes the structural source
concrete by localizing \(\Gamma_{\textsc{csl-sat-hidden}}\) to the fixed-branch residual
\[
  \mathrm{Br}^{\mathrm{lex}}_{\mathrm{SAT}}\notinE^{!}_{Q},
\]
the assertion that the canonical lexicographic SAT-branching readout is
not a lawful current observable on the fixed-presentation carrier.
Third, \Cref{sec:class-b-barrier} proves the Six Birds Class-B
Irremovability barrier: no basis-generated Class-B carrier-feature law
on the standard fixed-presentation polynomial current carrier removes
\(\Gamma_{\textsc{csl-sat-hidden}}\) except by leaving the fixed basis or importing a
target-equivalent lower bound.  That barrier rests on Fixed-Presentation
Orbit Collapse (\Cref{thm:pvnp:orbit-collapse}) and polynomial
pairing closure, organized through Basis Exhaustiveness
(\Cref{thm:pvnp:basis-exhaustiveness}), Basis Combination Closure
(\Cref{thm:pvnp:basis-combination-closure}), and the scoped
Irremovability theorem (\Cref{thm:pvnp:irremovability-scoped}).  It
is analogous in role to Baker--Gill--Solovay relativization,
Razborov--Rudich natural proofs, and Aaronson--Wigderson algebrization
\citep{BakerGillSolovay1975Relativization,RazborovRudich1997NaturalProofs,AaronsonWigderson2009Algebrization},
but methodologically distinct and internal to Six Birds.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
This paper gives a conditional Six Birds closure of the Riemann
hypothesis by moving the question from classical analytic number
theory to a formed-layer trace setting.  The substrate is the
saturated completed Selberg trace closure of the completed Riemann
zeta function, equipped with the functional-equation involution and
with a typed ledger of nontrivial zeros.  A translation theorem T
shows that the anti-invariant zero ledger of the completed zeta
shell vanishes, \(A_{Z}(\zeta)=0\), if and only if every typed nontrivial
zero has real part \(1/2\).  The conditional
landing chain uses the Selberg-class instance of Self-Dual Trace
Confinement supplied by \citet{TsiokosSDTC2026}: its recognition
source gives domination records whose vanishing trace forces
\(A_{Z}(\zeta)=0\), and theorem T converts that ledger collapse into the
critical-line statement.
Stated in the audit-closure language of \citet{TsiokosAOR2026},
the same conditional chain is recorded as a local
refinement-stable audited-operational-realisability instance,
\(\mathrm{Sel}^{!}_{\zeta,\mathrm{tr}}\in\mathrm{RefStableAOR}^{\mathrm{ref}}_{\mathfrak S_{\mathrm{RH}}}\),
whose typed-zero-ledger readout is the critical-line statement.

Outside Six Birds, the result is the conditional theorem
\(\Gamma_{\mathrm{SDTC}\text{-}\mathrm{Selberg}}\Rightarrow
\mathrm{RH}\) on the typed zero ledger.  This is not an unconditional
proof of the Riemann hypothesis in standard ZFC.
The shell's admissibility is a standing Foundations-II hypothesis, and
the real-part coordinate of a typed zero is a representation parameter
identified with the classical real part by construction-parameter
assignment.  The development is formalized in Lean as a mathlib-free
mechanization (Appendix~\ref{app:formalization}).

The paper's scope is correspondingly narrow.  The main result is
conditional on \(\Gamma_{\mathrm{SDTC\text{-}Selberg}}\); no unconditional RH claim in standard
ZFC is made, and \(\Gamma_{\mathrm{SDTC\text{-}Selberg}}\) is not claimed to be derivable
from framework primitives.  The conditional theorem takes a value of
the recognition source as an explicit hypothesis.  The
real-part coordinate of a typed zero is represented by a parameter;
under construction-parameter assignment when the shell is
instantiated, this parameter is identified with the classical real
part of a nontrivial zero of \(\zeta\).  Deriving this identification
from analytic-number-theoretic infrastructure is left as a future extension.
Admissibility of \(\mathrm{Sel}^{!}_{\zeta,\mathrm{tr}}\) under the seven Foundations-II schemas is
carried as an audit witness in the shell, not derived here.  The
classical RH programs named above are neither refuted nor
circumvented in their native sense: they aim at unconditional RH
within their classical substrates, while the present paper
establishes a conditional formed-layer result on the typed Selberg
trace shell.  The generalized Riemann hypothesis lies outside the
scope; the construction is instantiated for \(L=\zeta\) only.

The V-Differential classification organizes such structural laws by
the determining-state information the formed layer may expose.  A
determining state is the internal state through which observable
behavior is required to factor; in a trace-state-only column, the
layer may expose trace observables on a typed positive cone but not
a richer witness that would solve the target problem directly.  For
the RH closure, the visible currency is \(A_{Z}(\zeta)\), the order
\(\preceq\), and the trace functional \(\trace\); the admissible
content has the form of trace domination records
\[
  A_{Z}(\zeta) \preceq B_n,
  \qquad
  \trace B_n \to 0,
\]
not a hidden list of zero locations.  \citet{TsiokosSDTC2026}
identifies Self-Dual Trace Confinement, \(\Gamma_{\mathrm{SDTC}}\), as the
V-Differential trace-state-only law for involutive self-dual formed
closures; the present paper is the worked single-substrate
application of that apparatus to \(\mathrm{Sel}^{!}_{\zeta,\mathrm{tr}}\), conditional on the
Selberg-class recognition source.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
The SDTC structural law used in this paper is the involutive
self-dual member of that family \cite{TsiokosSDTC2026}.  Its
apparatus is the duality-confinement membrane theorem: given a
separating anti-invariant readout and a vanishing trace domination
sequence, the anti-invariant ledger collapses.  In the RH instance,
the recognition source \(\Gamma_{\mathrm{SDTC\text{-}Selberg}}\) supplies the domination
records for \(A_{Z}(\zeta)\), and the bridge theorem
\Cref{thm:rh:dc-master-applied} applies the
\cite{TsiokosSDTC2026} master theorem to \(\mathrm{Sel}^{!}_{\zeta,\mathrm{tr}}\).  The present
paper is therefore the worked single-substrate application of the
SDTC apparatus on the saturated Selberg trace shell, conditional on
the Selberg-class recognition source.  The unconditional analytic
content of any one of the broader formed-layer tracks is not derived
from a common primitive calculus; it is closure content of its formed
layer, supplied as recognition source.  This is why the parallels are
useful but not load-bearing: they show the paper is following a
stable formed-layer pattern inside the Six Birds program, while the
actual RH argument still depends only on the RH-specific shell, the
SDTC apparatus of \citet{TsiokosSDTC2026}, and the Selberg-class
recognition source.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
The paper is organized as follows.  \Cref{sec:xi-membrane} recalls the
adequacy-residual calculus from \citet{Tsiokos2026XiCompanion} and the
layer-dissolving membrane endpoint from
\citet{Tsiokos2026NeedleKiller}, and specializes both to the
Navier--Stokes carrier.  \Cref{sec:ns-carrier} fixes the carrier, the
fixed readout \(D^{\mathrm{BG}}\), the physical-native family \(L^{\mathrm{phys}}\), the
BG-windowed exact package, and null-mode legality.  \Cref{sec:imports}
records the six imported PDE results and rules out the criterion-native
shortcut (NG1).  \Cref{sec:adequacy-cascade} develops the
source-admission ledger \(\Omega_{\mathrm{src}}\) and the stage-to-stage recurrence
for the physical-native residual along the doubling stages.
\Cref{sec:no-go} states the remaining no-go family NG2--NG10,
excluding scalar-energy, packing, sparse-shadow, marker-only,
metric-shadow, moving-window, half-log endpoint, available-analyticity,
and raw-nonlinearity shortcuts.  \Cref{sec:gevrey-lp} develops the
Gevrey radius-window branch and the Littlewood--Paley transport rescue.
\Cref{sec:main-theorem} assembles \(R_1,\ldots,R_9\) and concludes
the framework-deliverable regularity theorem.
\Cref{sec:ns-aor-instance} recasts the closure records as the
AOR-membership witness for the smooth-data carrier.
\Cref{sec:status} closes with the external interpretation and the
locked nonclaim boundary.

\begin{proof}
The six listed records discharge by record-class inspection.
\(R_1\) (adequacy orientation), \(R_2\) (exact BG-windowed
package), and \(R_3\) (null-mode legality) are by-construction
fields of the smooth-data carrier of \Cref{sec:ns-carrier}:
the BG-windowed exact package and the legal-energy quotient
are part of the carrier definition, so the corresponding
discharge witnesses are the constructions themselves.  \(R_5\)
(BG frequency-doubling staging) is by-construction from the
doubling-stage indexing of \Cref{sec:adequacy-cascade}: the
stage map \(J\mapsto J+1\) is the carrier's declared
refinement.  \(R_9\) (nonclaim boundary) is by-construction
from the locked nonclaim list in \Cref{sec:status} together
with the per-paper nonclaim registers.  \(R_8\) (paper-grounded
PDE imports) discharges \texttt{approved\_other} as the
citation chain assembled in \Cref{sec:imports}: each of BKM,
BG, Kato local well-posedness, half-log analyticity,
Littlewood--Paley / Bony--Chemin--Danchin, and Sobolev/Besov
embedding is admitted as a single named external record, and
the bundle is the AOR \texttt{approved\_other} discharge for
\(R_8\).  These six records contribute the mechanical
components of the AOR-membership witness; the substantive
components \(R_4,R_6,R_7\) are treated in the next three
theorems.\footnote{Verified in Lean as \texttt{SixBirdsNeedles.NS.AORInstance.aorMechanicalRRecords}; see \Cref{subsec:paper3-per-label-coverage}.}
\end{proof}

frameworks:
\begin{itemize}

physical-native probe family, the BG-windowed exact package, and
null-mode legality (\Cref{sec:ns-carrier});

(\Cref{sec:adequacy-cascade});
\item the no-go family NG1--NG10 excluding shortcut payments
(\Cref{sec:imports,sec:no-go});

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{nonclaim:ns:outside-framework}
Outside the Six Birds closure framework, \Cref{thm:ns:framework-deliverable-regularity} reads as the conditional implication
\[
  \bigl(\mathsf R\text{ holds on the smooth-data carrier}\bigr)
  \Longrightarrow
  \bigl(T_{\max}(u_0)=\infty\bigr).
\]
This paper does not claim:
\begin{enumerate}
\item a standalone Clay--Millennium
solution~\citep{Fefferman2000NavierStokes} independent of the Six
Birds closure discipline;
\item generic critical-Besov data regularity outside the smooth-data
subcarrier \(H^{\gamma_0}\), \(\gamma_0>5/2\), in the sense of
critical-space well-posedness
results~\citep{KochTataru2001,Cannone1995,LemarieRieusset2023};
\item a criterion-native rewriting of \(D^{\mathrm{BG}}\) in place of
physical-native adequacy, as ruled out by
\Cref{thm:ns:no-go-criterion-native};
\item that any single PDE input alone closes the problem, since the
argument uses the full \(R_1,\ldots,R_9\) bundle architecture;
\item engagement with Caffarelli--Kohn--Nirenberg partial
regularity~\citep{CaffarelliKohnNirenberg1982}, which concerns
Leray--Hopf weak solutions~\citep{Leray1934,Hopf1951} on a different
carrier class;
\item an untyped global comparison, since every comparison in the proof
is made inside the typed-context discipline;
\item a full-log analyticity radius theorem, since the paper uses only
the available half-log analyticity import together with the
LP-transport rescue.
\end{enumerate}

highly localized gradient peaks, which is why global regularity is typically reduced to
``peak-channel'' criteria (e.g.\ Beale--Kato--Majda \citep{bkm_1984}).
We develop a multiscale \emph{decision scaffold}, inspired by the Six-Primitives/Six-Birds framework,
that separates (i) system-agnostic inequality logic, (ii) Navier--Stokes-facing hinge assumptions,
and (iii) numerical diagnostics.

Operationally, we (A) mechanize in Lean a No-Zeno engine: refinement events are encoded by crossing
times, and Zeno cascades are ruled out under work/capacity/divergence hypotheses; (B) mechanize a
route-stability $\Rightarrow$ polynomial-capacity lemma; and (C) mechanize a discrete no-go theorem:
if the feasible interface inputs at a scale admit highly localized tests, then any uniform ICAP-style
capacity certificate forces a pointwise positive-gain bound---the discrete analogue of a peak/strain
control in the PDE interpretation.
Motivated by this obstruction, we propose an \emph{SBT-legal} variant in which feasibility excludes
strong localization, and we operationalize legality as a reproducible certificate based on
per-shell anti-localization and channel diagnostics.
In numerical demos, typical smooth random seeds pass the certificate with $\max_j \kappa_j=O(1)$,
while intentionally localized shell wavepackets fail immediately (e.g.\ $\max_j\kappa_j\sim 10^2$).

These results clarify exactly where a Clay-style proof would require a genuinely new Navier--Stokes
inequality (a provable channelization/delocalization-to-anti-localization hinge) and provide a
reproducible workflow for testing such hypotheses.
We do not claim a proof of Clay regularity, nor do we prove that the legality certificate is preserved
under the classical Navier--Stokes flow; PDE-facing implications are stated explicitly as OPEN
assumptions.

conclusion: This paper does not claim a solution to the Clay problem.
expanded_source_wording_tex:
This paper does \emph{not} claim a solution to the Clay problem. Instead, it builds a sharp, reproducible \emph{decision scaffold} for a multiscale approach inspired by the Six Birds framework \citep{tsiokos_2026_18365949}. The core idea is to treat scale-elimination not as a modeling choice but as a canonical \emph{packaging} operation: the eliminated degrees of freedom become a causal ``bridge object'' acting on the retained variables through an interface, and the overall dynamics are constrained by an \emph{accounting} law. In Six Birds terms, we rely on six recurring structural moves:
(i) rewrite/coordinate change, (ii) feasibility/gating constraints, (iii) route dependence of reductions, (iv) sectorization/quantization of interaction channels, (v) packaging of eliminated structure into an effective object, and (vi) accounting (passivity-like) inequalities \citep{tsiokos_2026_18365949}. Our repo makes this concrete for Navier--Stokes by defining canonical multiscale objects (dyadic shells, frontier scales, and packaged subgrid operators) and then asking which primitive-shaped lemmas would be sufficient to rule out ``Zeno'' cascades to infinite depth.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\paragraph{What we do instead: an SBT-legal Navier--Stokes variant.}
Rather than chasing Clay as stated, we formalize and study a sharpened program: define an operational notion of \emph{SBT-legal} initial data that forbids extreme localization at dyadic scales, motivated by the channelization/anti-localization hinge required to escape the wavepacket obstruction. Concretely, we implement a certificate that measures anti-localization metrics per shell (normalized concentration factors, burst ratios, and effective channel counts), and we show (numerically) that typical smooth random seeds pass while intentionally constructed localized shell wavepackets fail immediately. This does not prove global regularity for all smooth data; it clarifies a precise, testable boundary between ``legal'' and ``illegal'' regimes for the Six Birds program.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\paragraph{Definition vs.\ diagnostic.}
Throughout, ``SBT-legal'' is used in two explicit senses.
\emph{Analytically}, it denotes a restricted variant/theory in which feasibility at each scale excludes
wavepacket-like concentration (a hypothesis on admissible interface signals, not a theorem about
classical Navier--Stokes).
\emph{Operationally}, we implement a certificate that tests this exclusion at a chosen resolution and
time window; in this paper we use it primarily as an initial-data filter and as a controlled
LEGAL-vs-ILLEGAL diagnostic.
We do not claim that passing the certificate at $t=0$ implies it remains true for later times under
the classical PDE flow; that invariance problem is recorded as an OPEN hinge in
Section~\ref{sec:discussion}.

conclusion: We do not claim bitwise identity across arbitrary BLAS/FFT backends or thread schedules
expanded_source_wording_tex:
\paragraph{Determinism scope.}
Our determinism checks verify byte-identical \texttt{.npz} outputs when rerunning in a fixed
software environment (same code, dependencies, and backend behavior). We do not claim bitwise
identity across arbitrary BLAS/FFT backends or thread schedules; for cross-platform reruns we
recommend pinning threads (e.g.\ \texttt{OMP\_NUM\_THREADS=1}, \texttt{MKL\_NUM\_THREADS=1})
and using tolerance-based numeric comparisons where appropriate.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\paragraph{What we do instead: an ``SBT-legal'' variant.}
Given the above obstruction, the only viable bypass within this scaffold is to restrict feasibility
so that localized wavepacket tests are \emph{not} admissible. We formalize this as an anti-localization
hinge and show that it can follow from finite-channel delocalized feasibility in a discrete model.
We then propose an operational certificate (computed by scripts in this repository) that checks
anti-localization-style metrics for initial data (Section~\ref{sec:spt-legal}).
This does not claim that legality is preserved under Navier--Stokes evolution; rather, it proposes
a concrete restricted theory where the No-Zeno engine becomes meaningful without smuggling in a
classical supremum regularity hypothesis.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
Certifying multiscale anti-localization only at $t=0$ is not useful unless legality is forward-closed; we lack general, mechanizable conditions under which SPT-legality propagates under time evolution.
We propose a slot-audited channelized-feasibility contract in a Hilbert/band/cell model, where legality is defined by the normalized max-cell concentration audit $\kappa_j$ and enforced structurally by feasible representations $\mathcal{F}_j=\mathrm{Ran}(\Gamma_j)$ with packaging projectors $E_j$.
We introduce these objects and theorem-grade constants (delocalization, frame bounds, mode growth, and cellwise defect), operationalize them with standardized experiment outputs and an automated \texttt{audit.json}, and evaluate the resulting bounds in toy dynamics together with matched failure-mode controls.
In an invariant-ladder regime (exact feasibility invariance), $\kappa_j(t)$ stays uniformly below the predicted envelope $K^{\mathrm{pred}}_{\mathrm{glob}}$; injecting a globally tiny but cell-localized off-feasible component causes immediate deep-band violations despite leakage below $10^{-2}$.
With per-channel delocalization held fixed, worsening frame conditioning produces extreme $\kappa$ tails, whereas well-conditioned artifacts keep $\kappa$ far below the envelope; under cellwise defect control $\mathrm{def}^{\infty}\le \varepsilon_\infty f_j$, maxima grow monotonically with $\varepsilon_\infty$ and remain within the robust bound $K^{\mathrm{rob}}(\varepsilon_\infty)$.
This yields a closed, regression-tested regime for ``SPT-legal evolution'' in the model and pinpoints which structural slots are necessary (and which global diagnostics are misleading) when building auditable multiscale representations.
We are explicit that stronger claims---PDE smoothing, physical entropy production, or emergent learning of channel maps---are not established here; our conclusions hold in a finite-dimensional Hilbert/cell setting and rely on theorem-aligned bounds together with controlled counterexamples.

source_title: A Six Birds Eye View of Quantum Theory
source_wording_digest: firstpage We present a reproducible computational framework—with Lean 4 mechanized proofs and deterministic Python simulations—that recasts quantum measurement, contextuality, and the measurement problem using operational semantics drawn from Six Birds Theory (SBT), a closure-based emergence calculus. Standard presentations of quantum mechanics mix causal evolution with inferential state update, so ``collapse,'' contextuality, and Schr\"odinger's cat are often treated as physical discontinuities or as evidence for surplus ontology. We separate these roles explicitly: causal substrate dynamics are distinguished from packaging (an idempotent closure operation that stabilizes record-level objects via a chosen record algebra). Operationally, we define an SBT theory package (Z,T,f,Q_f,U_f,E_f,A) , mechanize its quotient/closure/audit lemmas in Lean 4, and implement a reproducible suite of simulations spanning quantum and classical examples. Our results are comparative and controlled: (i) dephasing in a fixed record basis is an idempotent packaging map whose fixed points are exactly the diagonal (record-classical) states; (ii) route mismatch between evolution and packaging is approximately zero when the Hamiltonian is diagonal in the record basis, but nonzero for generic Hamiltonians or incompatible record bases; (iii) in a double-slit model, decreasing environment-record overlap continuously suppresses fringe visibility, while conditioning in a quantum eraser restores complementary fringes; (iv) in a system–apparatus–environment measurement model, the global state can remain near-pure while the packaged record state is a classical mixture, and packaging remains idempotent. This role separation localizes which distinctions are layer-relative and yields information-theoretic diagnostics for context dependence and record stability. We do not claim to derive the Born rule or resolve Bell's theorem; instead, we provide a structurally explicit reformulation supported by mechanization and reproducible demonstrations.
